docs.title: Turn your expertise into an AI-powered App, MCP or API
Turn your expertise into an AI-powered App, MCP or API
docs.text:
Describe how the work gets done in plain English, and your coding agent builds it into a method with the Pipelex plugin. A method is a multi-step, deterministic AI procedure that chains LLMs, OCR, image generation and more. Then run it as a webapp for your team or as SaaS for your customers, as an MCP for chatbots, or via API for your software.

Quick Start Sign up at app.pipelex.com Cookbook

docs.title: Get Started
docs.text:
• Quick Start

    Sign up, install the Pipelex plugin in Claude Code or Codex, and ask your agent for the method you want — then run it from your chatbot, as a webapp, or via API.

  • Run It Yourself

    Install the Pipelex runtime and run methods from your terminal: on the hosted Pipelex API with one sign-in, or on your own machine against the model providers you choose.

  • MTHDS Language Tutorial

    Learn the declarative language step by step: concepts, pipes, sequences, inputs, and structured outputs.

  • Cookbook

    Example methods you run by their address, each with a page showing every way to use it: in your chatbot, in your code, as an app, or as a method of your own.

docs.title: What a Method Looks Like
docs.text:
A method is a reusable, typed AI procedure, written in MTHDS, an open standard, and saved as a .mthds file. Each step is explicit, each output is structured, and every run is repeatable.

A single pipe in MTHDS — five lines that call an LLM with typed inputs and output:

[pipe.summarize_article]
type    = "PipeLLM"
inputs  = { article = "Text", audience = "Text" }
output  = "Text"
prompt  = "Summarize $article in three bullet points for $audience."

From here, Pipelex handles model routing across 60+ models, structured output parsing, and pipeline orchestration.

docs.title: Why Methods?
docs.text:
• Declarative

    Express business logic at a high level of abstraction, in human-readable .mthds files that work across models.

  • Typed

    Concepts are semantic types: AI understands what you mean, and every input and output connects with purpose.

  • Repeatable

    Deterministic orchestration that leaves exactly the room you want for AI to express its intelligence and creativity.

  • Composable

    Chain pipes into sequences, nest methods inside methods, and share them with the community.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Typed Concepts

    Semantic types that give meaning to every input and output — native, inline, or backed by Python classes.

  • Pipe Operators

    Operators that do the work: LLM calls, text structuring, document extraction, image generation, web search, composition, and custom functions.

  • Pipeline Orchestration

    Sequence, parallel, batch, and conditional controllers that wire pipes into full methods with shared working memory.

  • 60+ AI Models

    Your own provider keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Google, Deepseek, Hugging Face and more, or local models.

  • Validation and Dry Run

    Validate pipelines before execution and dry-run with mocked responses — catch errors without spending tokens.

  • CLI and Tooling

    Full CLI for init, build, validate, run, and graph visualization. Plus plxt for formatting and linting .mthds files.

docs.title: The Ecosystem
docs.text:
MTHDS is the open standard behind Pipelex methods. It defines the language, the file format, and the ecosystem for sharing methods.

Explore the MTHDS ecosystem

  • mthds.ai — The MTHDS language specification
  • mthds.sh — The Methods Hub for discovering and sharing methods

Build and run methods with Pipelex

  • Pipelex plugin — The Pipelex plugin for Claude Code and Codex: skills that build and run methods, a hook that checks every edit, and the Pipelex tools
  • Pipelex MCP — The Pipelex MCP, which ChatGPT or Claude adds to run the methods saved in your account

docs.title: Documentation Site Architecture
docs.text: This file documents non-obvious architectural decisions for the docs site (docs.pipelex.com). Read this before modifying anything under docs/.

docs.title: Site Architecture Overview
docs.text:
• MkDocs Material with mike versioning, published at docs.pipelex.com
  • site_url is https://docs.pipelex.com/ (bare domain, NOT /latest/) — mike rewrites sitemap URLs by inserting the version prefix during deployment; if site_url already contains /latest/, mike creates double paths like latest/0.20.9/page/. Canonical URLs are forced to /latest/ via a template override in docs/overrides/main.html.
  • Custom domain via docs/CNAME (value: docs.pipelex.com)
  • Theme overrides live in docs/overrides/

docs.title: URL Structure & Redirects
docs.text:
Legacy URL paths (e.g. home/1-features/) are redirected to current clean paths (e.g. features/) via two mechanisms:

  • The mkdocs-redirects plugin maps old→new paths (see redirect_maps in mkdocs.yml)
  • docs/404.html contains client-side JS rewrite rules for the same prefixes, covering URLs that bypass MkDocs routing

Both must stay in sync. mkdocs-redirects must be installed in CI (doc-check.yml).

docs.title: The Two 404 Pages (critical — do not conflate)
docs.text:
There are two distinct 404 pages serving different purposes:

  1. docs/404.html — Standalone root-level fallback for GitHub Pages. Copied to /404.html on gh-pages by docs-deploy-root. Contains JS redirect logic for legacy URLs. NOT part of the MkDocs build.

  2. docs/overrides/404.html — MkDocs Material template override. Controls the versioned site/404.html rendered by MkDocs. Extends main.html. Must include both SEO tags (noindex, canonical) AND visible user-facing content (heading + link back to /latest/).

There must be NO docs/404.md — a Markdown 404 would be treated as content, appear in the sitemap, and create an indexable /latest/404/ URL.

docs.title: SEO Architecture
docs.text:
• docs/overrides/main.html — Owns OG tags, Twitter cards, JSON-LD for all pages. Uses null-safe page.meta access (page.meta and page.meta.description). Does NOT special-case 404 behavior.
  • docs/overrides/404.html — Extends main.html, adds noindex/nofollow + canonical back to /latest/. Must also render visible content.
  • docs/.meta.yml — Default frontmatter for all pages via meta-manager plugin (image, description, keywords).
  • Per-page description frontmatter in individual .md files overrides the default.

docs.title: robots.txt: Two Files, Different Purposes
docs.text:
• docs/robots.txt — Lands at /latest/robots.txt inside the versioned site. Crawlers ignore it (RFC 9309: only domain-root robots.txt is authoritative). Exists as a courtesy/fallback.
  • Makefile ROOT_ROBOTS_TXT — The authoritative robots.txt deployed to domain root by docs-deploy-root. Allow-by-default with targeted disallows: it blocks versioned paths (/0.), /pre-release/, and /404.html; everything else — including root-level files like /llms.txt — is implicitly allowed (the explicit Allow: lines for /latest/, /sitemap.xml, /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt just document the intended crawl surface). Points sitemap to root /sitemap.xml (which contains /latest/ URLs, generated by docs-deploy-root from the latest/ alias sitemap via sed version-to-latest rewrite).

docs.title: Deployment (docs-deploy-root)
docs.text:
The docs-deploy-root Makefile target deploys root assets (404.html, robots.txt, index.html, sitemap.xml) directly to the gh-pages branch via a temporary git worktree. The root sitemap.xml is generated from latest/sitemap.xml on gh-pages (the alias directory) by sed-rewriting version numbers to /latest/. This ensures the root sitemap always reflects what /latest/ actually serves, even after pre-release deploys — because mike only updates the latest/ alias directory during stable deploys, not pre-release ones.

  • Called automatically after docs-deploy-stable and docs-deploy-specific-version-pre-release
  • The root index.html is a meta-refresh redirect to /latest/

docs.title: MkDocs Plugins
docs.text:
• search — site search with custom separator
  • redirects — legacy→current URL path mapping
  • meta-manager — applies docs/.meta.yml defaults to all pages
  • glightbox — image lightbox
  • llmstxt-md — generates llms.txt / llms-full.txt (LLM-friendly docs index + full content), which docs-deploy-root copies from latest/ to the site root

docs.title: Sidebar Width
docs.text:
Material for MkDocs hard-codes .md-sidebar { width: 12.1rem }. The root font-size is 20px (not 16), so rem values are larger than you'd expect (12.1rem = 242px). Custom overrides live in docs/stylesheets/general.css.

To widen the sidebar you must override two things: 1. .md-sidebar { width: ... } — the container itself 2. .md-sidebar .md-sidebar__inner { padding-right: 4px } — the theme dynamically inflates padding-right on .md-sidebar__inner to absorb extra container width, keeping the nav at its original size. Pin this padding to prevent that.

docs.title: Mike Versioning Behavior (critical — non-obvious)
docs.text:
Mike (mike deploy X.Y.Z latest) creates two directories on gh-pages: X.Y.Z/ and latest/. Understanding what mike does and does NOT rewrite is essential:

What mike rewrites: HTML files — mike inserts the version prefix into relative URLs, asset paths, and navigation links so pages work from both /X.Y.Z/ and /latest/.

What mike does NOT rewrite: Sitemap URLs. latest/sitemap.xml is a copy of X.Y.Z/sitemap.xml with the same versioned URLs (e.g., /X.Y.Z/page/). Mike does NOT replace the version with the alias name. This means you cannot simply copy latest/sitemap.xml and expect /latest/ URLs — you must sed-rewrite them.

What mike does NOT rewrite: Canonical tags, OG URLs, JSON-LD — these come from site_url + page path at build time. Mike does not touch them during deploy. That's why we override them in docs/overrides/main.html.

The double-path trap: If site_url is set to https://docs.pipelex.com/latest/, MkDocs builds URLs like /latest/page/. Then mike inserts the version prefix, producing /latest/X.Y.Z/page/ — a broken double path. This is why site_url must be the bare domain.

docs.title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
docs.text:
• Do NOT create docs/404.md — it poisons the sitemap with an indexable /latest/404/ URL
  • Do NOT delete docs/overrides/404.html — it controls the versioned 404 page
  • Do NOT put 404-specific SEO tags in main.html — that's overrides/404.html's job
  • Do NOT treat docs/robots.txt as the production robots policy — the authoritative one is ROOT_ROBOTS_TXT in the Makefile
  • When changing URL paths, update BOTH mkdocs.yml redirect_maps AND docs/404.html JS rewrite rules
  • Always add mkdocs-redirects to CI pip install when redirect_maps exist
  • Do NOT set site_url to include /latest/ — mike will create double paths like /latest/X.Y.Z/page/
  • Do NOT assume latest/sitemap.xml has /latest/ URLs — mike copies sitemaps verbatim from the version directory without rewriting
  • Do NOT source the root sitemap from $(DOCS_VERSION)/ — use latest/ so pre-release deploys don't overwrite it with pages not served at /latest/
  • Do NOT flip ROOT_ROBOTS_TXT to a deny-by-default Disallow: / policy — a Sitemap: directive does NOT override Disallow, so every root-level asset (/sitemap.xml, /llms.txt, ...) would silently drop from crawl unless individually Allowed. The shipped policy is allow-by-default with targeted disallows for versioned and non-content paths

docs.title: Blueprints in Documentation
docs.text: The docs/building-methods/ section documents the MTHDS language — what users write in .mthds files and what those files parse into via MthdsParser, the blueprint layer. Documentation under docs/building-methods/ describes blueprint-level fields only.

docs.title: Our Pledge
docs.text:
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

docs.title: Our Standards
docs.text:
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:

  • Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
  • Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
  • Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
  • Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
  • Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

  • The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
  • Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
  • Public or private harassment
  • Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
  • Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

docs.title: Enforcement Responsibilities
docs.text:
Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official email address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement at abuse@pipelex.com. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Enforcement Guidelines
docs.text: Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

docs.title: 1. Correction
docs.text:
Community Impact: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

Consequence: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

docs.title: 2. Warning
docs.text:
Community Impact: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.

Consequence: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

docs.title: 3. Temporary Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior.

Consequence: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

docs.title: 4. Permanent Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

Consequence: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.

docs.title: Attribution
docs.text:
This Code of Conduct is adapted from the Contributor Covenant, version 2.1, available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html.

Community Impact Guidelines were inspired by Mozilla's code of conduct enforcement ladder.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• callback_urls and pipeline_run_id on /v1/execute: the API server's blocking run route takes the caller's webhooks, whose events are sent before it answers, and a caller-chosen pipeline_run_id, honored as /v1/start honors it, a run still in flight under the same id answering 409 pipelex.run.already_exists. PipelexMTHDSProtocol.execute takes pipeline_run_id too.
  • COMPLETION_CALLBACK_URL, the deployment's completion target: the API server notifies this URL, which may name the run's id with one {pipeline_run_id} placeholder in its path or its query, when each /v1/start run ends, with the completion notice in the operator's view and its X-Completion-Signature. A malformed value, or one set without COMPLETION_CALLBACK_SECRET, stops the server at boot, and a /v1/start request's callback_urls entry equal to the run's completion URL is notified once, as the completion target, while on /v1/execute, which notifies no completion target, it is a caller's webhook.
  • pipelex.webhook.secret_not_configured: a 422 registry code naming in setting the runner setting that holds no secret to sign a caller's webhooks with.
  • The library delivers caller webhooks: DeliveryAssignment.caller_webhooks lists CallerWebhookTargets, each with the delivery_id its calls carry, and pipelex.tools.network.standard_webhooks signs a call in the Standard Webhooks format. DeliveryExecutor delivers a run in two steps a durable orchestrator may run apart: execute_host_delivery stores the results and notifies the host's webhooks, then execute_caller_delivery sends the caller's events, last and once, with how the run ended, which run_ending_after_host_failure gives when the host step failed. DeliveryExecutor.execute runs both, and takes the run's finished_at and extras.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• callback_urls receive the signed run.finished event (Breaking): each URL a request to the API server registers receives the caller-webhook contract's event, type, timestamp, attempt and data, the run as the protocol's status read serves it with a failed run's problem in the caller's view, signed with the Standard Webhooks headers webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature under the whsec_ secret or secrets in CALLER_WEBHOOK_SECRET. It replaces the completion notice and its X-Completion-Signature, which no caller webhook receives any more, so a self-hosted receiver now verifies the Standard Webhooks signature, and a server without CALLER_WEBHOOK_SECRET refuses a request carrying callback_urls with a 422 pipelex.webhook.secret_not_configured. Each URL is delivered on its own, three attempts within 15 seconds each and no redirect followed, and a delivery that fails is logged and never changes the run.
  • The completion notice goes to COMPLETION_CALLBACK_URL alone (Breaking): a host that relied on callback_urls to receive the completion notice and its X-Completion-Signature, as a hosting platform does, sets COMPLETION_CALLBACK_URL to its completion URL before taking this release; otherwise its URL is a caller webhook and, on a server without CALLER_WEBHOOK_SECRET, every /v1/start carrying it is refused. The notice now always carries the operator's view of a failed run's problem, whoever started the run.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A /v1/start run whose dispatch fails gives its id back: the API server releases what it set up for a run its orchestrator could not enqueue, its registration, its graph tracer and its library, so the same pipeline_run_id can be started again; pipeline_run_setup's new companion release_run_setup does it for any host.
  • A cancelled run is never reported completed: a run cancelled before it ended, which PipeRun re-raises the cancellation of, now tells its webhooks, the host's completion notice included, that it failed, with the problem run.cancelled, where the notice said COMPLETED; a delivery that fails afterwards never replaces the cancellation.
  • A failed notice to a host's webhook names its reason: the pipelex.webhook.delivery_failed problem a run fails with when one of its host's webhooks cannot be notified carries the reason its code requires, http_status with the receiver's receiver_status, or unreachable.
  • A refused webhook no longer replaces a failed run's own failure: a delivery destination the SSRF guard refuses after the run failed logs its security event and the delivery's failure, and the run fails with its own error, where the refusal used to be raised in its place.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• mthds and pipelex-sdk versions (Breaking): The pins move to mthds==0.26.0, the release following the MTHDS standard's v8.0.1, and pipelex-sdk==0.57.0, the release built on it, whose own breaking changes since 0.53.0, such as list_runs and iterate_runs taking method_id as a keyword-only filter and method-version fields no longer coerced, reach anyone importing pipelex_sdk beside pipelex. Everyone downstream inherits those exact versions.
  • MTHDS standard 8.0.1 and MTHDS Protocol 2.0.1 (Breaking): every crate pipelex normalizes, on the command line and on the API server's POST /v1/resolve, is stamped mthds_version: "8.0.1", a METHODS.toml whose mthds_version is exactly 8.0.0 now warns where >=8.0.1 passes, and pipelex --version, pipelex-agent --version and GET /v1/version report the MTHDS Protocol 2.0.1. Crate fingerprints do not move.
  • The problems a run raises carry titles written for whoever follows it: every problem pipelex emits under a core code a run can raise, in a run's failure, an API server answer or the CLI's error output, carries the title the core error registry 8.0.1 gives it for someone following a run of a method they did not write: pipe.output_multiplicity is titled "A step produced a list instead of one result, or the reverse" where it read "A pipe's output does not have the declared multiplicity", and pipe.output_invalid "A step's result does not have the structure the method declares". No code, domain, retry verdict, step kind or status changes.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • The API server checks a files map's blobs last: as the MTHDS Protocol 2.0.1 orders a map's refusals, a map holding a key the tree's rule refuses, colliding keys or a malformed entry is refused for that before any blob it names is read, where a hash held at another size than its entry states answered 422 request.invalid, and a damaged stored blob 500 pipelex.storage.damaged, ahead of the key's own refusal.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • pipelex.billing.credit_exhausted names the credit ledger that ran out: the code declares an optional ledger parameter, inference or usage, so the hosted platform's refusal of a run says whether the organization's inference credit or its usage credit is spent, and BillingCreditExhaustedParams gains the ledger field. A model call refused once the credit has run out names no ledger, as before.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A direct provider's spent quota is read from its structure, not its wording: a call with your own keys to OpenAI or a backend on the OpenAI SDK, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Mistral or Amazon Bedrock is a spent quota only on the status, error code or error detail that provider documents for one, and is otherwise retried as provider.rate_limited. A 429 whose message mentioned a quota, as Gemini's per-minute throttles do, used to fail at once as provider.quota_exhausted. Anthropic's credit-balance and self-set usage-limit refusals, which carry no code, are still read, by their opening words.
  • Throttles sent on another status than 429 are retried: OpenRouter's 402 for its in-flight budget, Groq's 498 for its flex tier at capacity, and Bedrock's ServiceQuotaExceededException, from Bedrock's SDK or from Claude on Bedrock through the Anthropic SDK, are now provider.rate_limited where they failed at once.
  • Gemini's retry delay is carried: the delay Gemini gives in its error's RetryInfo detail, not in a Retry-After header, is now the failure's retry_after and is named in its advice.
  • A delay in milliseconds is read: a retry-after-ms header above zero, which Azure OpenAI sends beside retry-after, is now the delay a rate limit carries, read first as the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs read it, on a call through either SDK, Azure's REST API or a gateway. The transport retry of a call to Azure's REST API now waits that delay too, where it read Retry-After alone.
  • More of Bedrock's wordings of an input over the window are recognized: a ValidationException saying "Input Tokens Exceeded" (Amazon Nova), "Too many input tokens" (Amazon Titan) or "prompt tokens (N) exceed model maximum (M)" is now model.context_exceeded where it was runtime.unexpected.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • ProviderErrorMetadata.is_quota_exhaustion (Breaking): a plugin reads ProviderErrorMetadata.limit_verdict instead, a ProviderLimitVerdict of quota_exhausted, rate_limited or neither, the one entry point the classifier reads.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • A gateway's rate limit is no longer read as a spent quota: a 429 relayed by a Portkey-dialect gateway is now provider.rate_limited, retried with the provider's Retry-After, unless its error code is one the provider documents for a spent quota: OpenAI's insufficient_quota, credit_balance_exhausted, organization_spend_limit_exceeded, project_spend_limit_exceeded or organization_usage_limit_exceeded. A 429 whose message mentioned a quota, as Azure OpenAI's throttles do, used to fail at once as provider.quota_exhausted with advice to add credit. A 402 is still a spent quota.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • A fetched method's provenance carries its declared name: MethodProvenance gains display_name, the display_name the package's METHODS.toml declares at the fetched commit, and null when it declares none, so the method_provenance of a method_ref run on /v1/execute and /v1/start reports it beside the address, tag, commit and tree digest, and a host can name the run's method after it. A fetched copy's .provenance.json sidecar records it too, and a sidecar or a record written without it still reads, its display_name null.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The S3 storage provider reuses one client per event loop: each event loop opens one aiobotocore client on its first S3 operation, and every later operation on that loop shares it and its pool of S3_MAX_POOL_CONNECTIONS connections, where every operation, a presigned URL included, built a client and opened a TLS connection of its own; the client is closed as its loop shuts down or at the runtime's teardown, which now calls StorageProviderAbstract.teardown(), a no-op that a storage plugin keeping a client open between operations overrides to close it. Measured from a laptop against a bucket in another region, the API server's read of a method tree of 20 blobs went from 4,261 ms of wall time and 425 ms of CPU to 1,582 ms and 32 ms with this change alone.
  • The API server reads each blob a request names in one request: a run, a validation and the tooling routes read each hash entry of files and dependencies with one read of at most one byte past the size the entry states, 16 at a time, where they looked each blob's size up first and then read the blobs 4 at a time; a hash held at another size still answers 422 request.invalid, its size looked up only for that refusal's message, and damaged bytes still answer 500 pipelex.storage.damaged. Measured as above with both changes, reading a tree of 1, 20 and 50 blobs takes 194, 419 and 838 ms of wall time and 1.3, 14 and 31 ms of CPU, where it took 1,142, 4,261 and 10,253 ms and 26, 425 and 1,000 ms. The local storage provider now reads such a leading range of a file without loading the whole file.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The API server refuses a method's unmet requirements as an invalid method (Breaking): /v1/execute and /v1/start refuse a method whose requirements.txt the PipeFunc sandbox does not meet, or holds a line the standard refuses, with a 422 method.invalid whose errors hold one method.dependency_missing or method.package_invalid item per refused line, located at requirements.txt and the line, the problem a local run of the method raises and the items /v1/validate gives, where they answered a bare method.dependency_missing or method.package_invalid with no item and no location; a client reads the refused requirement from the item's params and location.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • A failed step's trace records the failure's own code: a failed node of the execution graph, and the pipe_end_error trace event, now carry the problem the run fails with when the step's error wraps a carrier of a problem recovered across a transport boundary, such as pipe.function_raised for a PipeFunc whose function raised in a sandbox, located at the step, where they carried the carrier's catch-all runtime.unexpected. The step's own message names that recovered code too, Error: <carrier class> (pipe.function_raised), and reported_failure_code (pipelex.pipe_run.located_failure) reads the code a failure reports without building its problem.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• OpenRouter model research: pipelex-dev openrouter list-models looks up the public catalog across modalities, filters and sorts models, and emits Markdown or clean JSON. --save writes disabled draft backend TOML with output-token limits and known token prices for review, independently of remote-config tooling.
  • The validation report names the files each step reads: PipelexValidationReport, and so the valid verdict of /v1/validate, carries tree_files_read, mapping each validated pipe's pipe_ref to the files of the method's tree it reads, each a TreeFileRead with its tree_path and its use (template for a PipeDocGen step's template_file, template_asset for a file its HTML template names by a literal relative URL, python_module for the module holding a PipeFunc step's function), an empty list for a pipe reading none, and tree_file_readers, mapping each of those files to the pipes that read it. pipelex-agent validate bundle and validate method carry both in their envelope, and the Markdown of a valid verdict lists them in a "Files the steps read" section.
  • A sandboxed PipeFunc reports its function's own failure: when the function a PipeFunc call runs raises inside a sandbox, python -m pipelex.pipe_operators.func.pipe_func_transported_entrypoint writes a PipeFuncRaisedReport to its result file before it exits non-zero, holding the operator's view of the pipe.function_raised problem, which names the function and the step and the class of what the function raised, never its text, while a sandbox failing any other way, such as a timeout inside it, still writes nothing there. An out-of-process executor reads the result file of a call that exited non-zero with read_pipe_func_raised_report (pipelex.pipe_operators.func.pipe_func_execution_transport), which answers the problem, rendered again from the registry and with only the diagnostics a sandbox writes, or None for no report or a report of any other code, and raises a Pipelex error carrying it, so the step reads pipe.function_raised as it does in process.
  • A fetched package is checked against the calling method's methods.lock: when a method carries a methods.lock at the root of its tree, a package it calls by address that the runtime fetched itself, for this load or by an earlier fetch whose installed copy records its provenance, must have the tree digest the lock records for its address, whatever version the lock names, else the load is refused with the core code security.integrity_mismatch (domain method, a 422 with its security event on the API server), whose message names the locked and fetched versions and digests and says to pin the reference to the locked version or to lock the method again, or, when an installed copy answered a reference pinning another tag, says so and to remove that copy. A lock not naming the address, or no lock, checks nothing, and packages shipped with the method or installed by another tool are not checked. The lock is read only when a dependency resolves to such a copy, and one the runtime cannot read, one recording a hash from before tree digests included, then refuses the load with method.package_invalid and the new reason lock_invalid.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Every S3 write carries its SHA-256 (Breaking): the S3 storage provider sends the SHA-256 of every object it writes, so S3 refuses a body that arrived damaged and keeps the checksum beside the object, where a HeadObject with ChecksumMode=ENABLED returns it, and a generated file's write carries the whole digest of which its key carries the first 16 digits; its client no longer signs the payload, which the signed checksum protects. StorageProviderAbstract.store takes the digest as checksum_sha256_hex from a caller that hashed the bytes already, and hands it to _store, so a storage plugin adds the keyword checksum_sha256_hex to its _store, sending it when its storage can check a write's checksum and ignoring it otherwise.
  • pipelex-agent validate bundle --graph writes into an output folder (Breaking): the flowchart it draws, dry_run.html, and mermaidflow.html with --graph-format mermaidflow or both, go into a new numbered folder, <pipe_code>_output_<NN>/, under the results/ directory a run bundle of the same target writes to (beside the bundle file named, beside the bundle defining a folder's entry pipe, or in the folder's own results/ when --pipe names the pipe), holding the .gitignore a run's output folder holds, instead of beside the bundle drawn, so validating a method no longer adds files to its tree or changes its digest. Read each file's path from graph_files in the envelope, the Markdown listing them under ## Graph files, and the folder from graph_output_dir.
  • The API server's examples send a method in files: the server's README and the API Server pages send a method to /v1/execute and /v1/validate in files, a map from each file's path in the method's folder to its content, where they sent mthds_contents. The reference pages and the OpenAPI artifact now say that mthds_contents, with bundle_b64, resources and /v1/validate's mthds_sources, is being retired and will be refused by a later release, so a client sends files now.
  • A PipeFunc package-offer factory is never called on a thread running an event loop (Breaking): the factory a plugin registers with PluginRegistrar.add_pipe_func_package_offer may block for as long as its work takes and must not use an event loop of its caller's, and pipelex enforces it: a load that would call the factory on a thread running an event loop fails with PipelexUnexpectedError instead, so a host that calls a load itself from asynchronous code, such as a worker's activity, moves it off the loop with run_method_load (pipelex.libraries.method_load_threads) or with acquire_library_async (pipelex.pipeline.execution_seams), the twin of acquire_library that loads off the loop. The factory's signature is unchanged, and so is the plugin API version. run_method_load runs a blocking call in the method-load pool, a named pool of at most METHOD_LOAD_MAX_THREADS threads (four) apart from asyncio's default executor, in a copy of the caller's context, and when its caller is cancelled, the shutdown of asyncio.run included, withdraws a call no thread has taken yet or lets the cancellation through only once the running call has ended; the general mechanism is WorkerThreads (pipelex.tools.misc.async_utils).
  • The refusal of a package the request did not send: the message of the unresolved_package_dependency refusal a static resolution gives, such as the one behind /v1/resolve, /v1/codegen and /v1/pipe-io, tells its reader to send the package's files in dependencies, keyed by its address, beside the method's own files in files, where it spoke of an in-memory resolve and the host filesystem and advised directory-based resolution; it still carries the words address-based dependency '<address>'.
  • A run lists each method tree once (Breaking): the method trees a run reads, the method's own, its library directories' and its dependency packages', are each listed once, and the run loads the trees its caller listed, so the method_tree_digest a run records is the digest of the tree it loaded: PipelexMTHDSProtocol.execute, pipeline_run_setup, acquire_library, acquire_library_async, validate_bundle, validate_bundles_in_process, fix_bundle_file, fix_method_folder, and LibraryManagerAbstract.load_libraries and load_from_blueprints take tree_listing, a MethodTreeListing (pipelex.libraries.method_tree_listing) holding the trees already listed, which run bundle, validate bundle and fix bundle on both CLIs hand down from the listing that resolved their target. The listing reads a path as the standard's lister does before it takes anything from what it holds: a folder and a symbolic link naming it are one listing, since the lister follows such a link, a bundle file named alone inside a library directory shares the listing of the tree that directory roots, and a symbolic link to a bundle file, named alone, is refused as the lister refuses it, even once the run listed the file it points to. Loads of one run running at the same time list each tree once and list different trees side by side. The API server's run routes and /v1/validate load the trees their check of the method's requirements listed, which ensure_served_method_requirements_met now lists through tree_listing in place of its limits, and which reaches the in-process validator through scoped_tree_listing, so the bundle-validator plugin contract is unchanged. list_library_trees and list_library_dir_trees (pipelex.libraries.method_trees) take the lister of a directory's own tree or of its trees (own_tree_of, trees_of), through which the listing lists them, and tree_bundle_of_lone_file is removed: a bundle file named alone is placed in its tree with MethodTreeListing.lone_file_bundle.
  • A run asks the PipeFunc package-offer factory once per tree: the run's MethodTreeListing keeps each method tree and each dependency package whose requirements.txt a check found met, with the execution mode and the factory it was judged against (PipeFuncEnvironmentSource, current_pipe_func_environment_source in pipelex.libraries.package_environments), so a run judges each tree once against them however many of its steps and loads read it, two loads judging one tree at the same moment ask once (MethodTreeListing.judge_requirements_once), and on the API server the load serving a request takes the verdict of the runner's check of the served method instead of asking the factory again. A check against another mode or factory, a refused tree and every new run ask again: pipelex keeps a verdict for one run alone, so a factory whose answer takes time keeps its own cache across runs, by the requirements' texts. ensure_method_requirements_met and ensure_package_requirements_met take the listing as tree_listing.
  • mthds 0.25.0 and pipelex-sdk 0.53.0 (Breaking): pipelex pins mthds==0.25.0 and pipelex-sdk==0.53.0, the release whose errors carry the hosted API's problem document, so it implements the MTHDS standard 8.0.0 and the protocol 2.0.0, which the version handshake reports, and a method tree never holds a run's inputs file, inputs.json or inputs.toml at any depth, so a method folder holding one is listed, and digested, without it.
  • PipelexMTHDSProtocol takes the protocol's files (Breaking): execute, start and validate take the MTHDS protocol's files map in the position the protocol gives it, and the local runtime refuses a map holding a file with request.unsupported and the reason method_files_on_local_runtime, METHOD_FILES_UNSUPPORTED_REASON in pipelex.errors.unsupported_reasons; mthds_contents is a keyword-only argument, which validate requires. The API server's ApiRunner takes the same arguments, and its routes, which write a method sent in files out as a tree before they run it, are unchanged.
  • A hosted run sends its method as a tree (Breaking): pipelex run --hosted and pipelex-agent run --runner hosted send a local method to /v1/pipe-io, /v1/start and /v1/execute as the MTHDS protocol's files map, each .mthds bundle under its path in the method's tree and each library directory beside the method under a top-level folder named after it, inline up to 256 KiB and by hash beyond, where the run took the bundles' bare contents and pipe-io a list the runner now refuses with a 422, so a hosted run whose inputs name a local file reads the signature again, and a method that does not load is reported by the tree path of each faulty file. HostedRunRequest (pipelex.hosted.hosted_run) takes contents, each bundle's bytes by tree path, in place of mthds_files. A file of the tree that cannot be uploaded stops the run before anything starts, as pipelex-sdk's MethodFileTransferError, which both CLIs report with the SDK's verdict and a next step: run again, or report a file the storage refused. A bundle file given with -L that the membership rule keeps out of its tree, a hidden one under a dot segment or one .gitignore excludes, is refused before anything is sent, as a local run refuses it, where it was sent as it was.
  • A hosted run's lost connection follows pipelex-sdk's reading: pipelex run --hosted and pipelex-agent run --runner hosted report a connection lost on the start or the execute request as HostedRunOutcomeUnknownError (client.outcome_unknown) whenever pipelex-sdk reads it as one that may have started the run (its problem's retry verdict outcome_unknown), a proxy's failure and a TLS handshake that was dropped included, which read as an unreachable API, while a connection lost on a request sent before the run's, such as the blob check of a tree sent by hash, stays pipelex-sdk's ApiUnreachableError.
  • Both CLIs report a hosted failure as its problem (Breaking): pipelex run --hosted prints the problem pipelex-agent run --runner hosted reports, its title, detail, next step, code with its domain and retry verdict, request id, run and items, and a failed run's own problem below it, both read from pipelex-sdk's exc.problem through describe_hosted_error, which now takes credential_sent and returns the problem, the error's own sentence and pipelex's advice. The readers of the hosted API's answers in the shape that predates the problem document are removed: an answer that is no problem document keeps pipelex-sdk's reading by its status, except a bare 401 or 403, which reads as auth.missing_credential when no key was sent and auth.invalid_credential when one was, and a bare 404, request.not_found, each with the next step that names the CLI's settings. HostedMethodInvalidError carries the items of the pipe-io verdict as errors, the standard's problem items, where it carried validation_errors, and a run past the wait reports pipelex-sdk's client.follow_failed.
  • pipelex-agent validate bundle and fix bundle exit 2 on a configuration refused before the boot: a configuration that does not validate, which these commands read before the boot for the limits a method's folder is listed under, exits 2, no verdict, where it exited 1, as pipelex validate bundle and pipelex fix bundle exit on it; the problem is unchanged, and run bundle and inputs bundle still exit 1.
  • The development Python is pinned in .python-version: the library's .venv and the API server's api/.venv are built on the version the root .python-version names, and the Makefiles hand that version to every uv command, so PYTHON_VERSION=<version> make install now moves an existing environment to the version asked for, where it used to keep the environment's own Python without a word. The CI jobs that run another version set it for the whole job, and the matrix jobs check that each cell ran the version it names.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A hosted run refusing a local file names its reason: the request.unsupported problem pipelex run --hosted and pipelex-agent run --runner hosted report when the inputs name a local file and the method calls another by its address carries the parameters its code requires, field (inputs) and reason (local_file_with_address_dependency, LOCAL_FILE_WITH_ADDRESS_DEPENDENCY_UNSUPPORTED_REASON in pipelex.errors.unsupported_reasons), so a client can tell this refusal apart.
  • A file name's type is the same on every Python: mime_type_of_file_name answers text/markdown for .md and .markdown, application/yaml for .yaml and .yml, and the OpenDocument types for .odt, .ods and .odp on every supported Python, where Python 3.11's table knew no Markdown and only 3.14's knew the others, so a file of these types has the format key md, yaml, odt, ods or odp whatever the Python, and a bare zip named .odt, .ods or .odp is identified as that OpenDocument type.
  • A method edited between its listing and its load is refused: a run read its method's files again after listing them, so a file edited in between was loaded under a digest that named other bytes. Every file a load reads from a tree listed on this host, a bundle it parses, the requirements.txt it judges and the Python it scans, is now read against the hash the listing recorded, a load reads every file of a tree the run listed before it again, once per run, as it takes the tree, and the bundle text a CLI read for its run is checked against the listed file, so a bundle, a template or any other file of the tree edited, replaced or removed since the listing is refused before anything of the method is parsed, imported or run, with MethodTreeChangedError (pipelex.libraries.exceptions), coded method.package_invalid with the new reason tree_changed and the file's path in the tree; run, validate and fix report it as an invalid method whose item names that file. A requirements.txt that can no longer be read is this refusal too, where it was requirements_invalid. The checked reads are read_tree_file_as_listed, read_tree_bundle_as_listed, ensure_tree_files_as_listed and ensure_bundle_text_as_listed in pipelex.libraries.method_trees, MethodTreeListing.loading() marks a load reading a listing and ensure_unchanged() checks a tree a caller placed a bundle in, and MthdsParser.make_pipelex_bundle_blueprint takes the bytes it parses as bundle_data, beside the bundle_path that names them.
  • Method loads leave the event loop: every method load pipelex reaches from asynchronous code, a run's, a validation's and those of the commands that run a loop, runs in the method-load pool, where it ran on the event loop, the reading and parsing of the bundles it loads included, so listing and hashing a method's files, a sandbox's judgment of its requirements.txt and a fetch of a package it calls by address no longer hold up the other requests or activities the loop serves; the API server's run routes and /v1/validate also write a request's method tree to disk and remove it there, and judge its requirements there, so a client that disconnects never has the tree removed while the check still reads it, the crate routes resolve and project there, and the in-process validator reads a tree's entry pipe for its graph there too. A module imported by file while a method loads, such as one defining a structure class, is published and executed under a lock that the load's class discovery also holds, so two loads in parallel never take a module half executed, and a module that fails to execute leaves sys.modules rather than stay there half imported. /v1/validate of a method tree calling a package nothing shipped still resolves it as a run does, from the methods installed on the server and by a fetch on a miss, so its verdict matches the run's, and the fetch now runs off the event loop.
  • Where a method's Python travels, in the docs: the PipeFunc Requirements, PipeFunc and run pages say that the API server receives a method as a tree holding its bundles and its Python together and judges its requirements.txt from the tree's listing, that the runner never imports a method's Python, that a run's crate names each step's method tree by its digest and carries none of its files, that a PipeFunc call's files are read through the method file store the worker's host installs, and that a worker a method tree's validation is dispatched to checks the method's requirements again, where they said the server received a method's Python apart from its bundles, the Python was captured as text, the crate carried the method's Python sources and the worker never checked anything.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • resolve_crate_from_contents (Breaking): pipelex.pipeline.resolve_bundle no longer resolves a crate from bundle contents held as strings. A host resolves a method as /v1/resolve, /v1/codegen and /v1/pipe-io do, by writing its tree out and calling resolve_crate_from_method_dir, with the packages it ships in methods_dirs; a call into a package nothing shipped is then an unresolved_package_dependency item of the invalid verdict, never the request.unsupported refusal with the reason address_based_dependency, which no resolution of this release gives: its constant ADDRESS_DEPENDENCY_UNSUPPORTED_REASON (pipelex.errors.unsupported_reasons) is removed with ADDRESS_DEPENDENCY_REFUSAL_MARKER (pipelex.methods.address_dependencies), and a hosted run no longer reads that refusal from /v1/pipe-io, only the invalid verdict naming the package nothing shipped.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • aiohttp 3.14.5 in the API server image: the lock the pipelex/pipelex-api image installs from moves aiohttp past GHSA-494j-54xm-rwp3, GHSA-5wr8-gcqf-gqf3 and GHSA-2g87-pp6c-29x5, with yarl 1.25.1 alongside; the published pipelex wheel's own requirements are unchanged.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The Pipelex error registry: the codes Pipelex emits beyond the MTHDS core registry, under the pipelex extension prefix the core registry registers to it, are authored in one public file in the MTHDS error registry format, pipelex/errors/registry/pipelex-error-registry.yaml, each declaring its title, domain, retry verdict, steps, typed parameters, templates and status. The package ships its JSON snapshot, pipelex-error-registry.json, published under Pipelex's version, a pre-release's written in the SemVer form the registry format requires (0.88.0rc1 as 0.88.0-rc.1), which load_pipelex_error_registry() reads into a typed model, and every release attaches the snapshot to its GitHub release.
  • pipelex.errors.registry.pipelex_codes: PipelexErrorCode, a member per code of the Pipelex error registry, and for each code a closed, frozen and strict parameters model typed as the registry declares, with the code and its operator-only parameters as class attributes, PIPELEX_ERROR_PARAMS mapping each code to its model.
  • A documentation page per error code: docs.pipelex.com documents each code of the Pipelex error registry on its own page, under the Error Codes index at errors/, and its type URI, https://docs.pipelex.com/errors/<code>, leads to that page once a release documenting the code is the latest.
  • pipelex-dev generate-error-registry and pipelex-dev check-error-registry (make ger, make cer): generate the registry's snapshot, its typed Python and its pages from the source, refusing a source the format's JSON Schema, the typed model or the registry's rules refuse, or check that every derived file is what the generator writes; pipelex-dev write-error-type-redirects writes the redirects that make a code's type URI resolve, which every documentation deploy runs.
  • Every error carries its registry code: every PipelexError subclass declares in error_code the code it raises, a code of the MTHDS core registry or of the Pipelex error registry, or else an ErrorCodeSet its raise sites choose from with with_error_code(), its cause's code (InheritsCause, with a fallback), or ABSTRACT_ERROR for a base never raised itself. resolve_error_code() gives the code an error reports, the first one named along its cause chain, and runtime.unexpected when none is; pipelex.errors.error_codes reads any code's title, domain, retry verdict, status and steps (error_code_spec, parse_error_code).
  • PipelexError.with_items(): a raise site that finds several faults of one kind gives one problem item per fault, so a PipeParallel whose branches give several results of a multiplicity their fields do not declare names each one in its pipe.output_multiplicity problem's errors, beside the first in its sentence.
  • PluginRegistrar.declare_error_codes: a plugin, a closed one included, declares the public codes it raises while it registers, and a code neither the MTHDS core nor the Pipelex registry defines refuses the boot with PluginErrorCodeNotRegisteredError (pipelex.plugin.broken), naming the plugin and the code.
  • --error-format on pipelex-agent itself and on its inputs commands: the error format can be given before the command, pipelex-agent --error-format json validate bundle …, where a command's own --error-format still wins and its --format still serves when neither is given, so a caller forwards one flag whatever the command; the inputs commands take --error-format too, falling back to the program's and then to JSON, never to their --format, which is the template's serialization.
  • InputFreeValueError and the input-free rendering of a refusal: a pydantic validator raising InputFreeValueError (pipelex.tools.typing.validation_exceptions) declares that its message names nothing of the value it refused, which keeps its sentence wherever a refusal of a run's data is written, and format_validation_error_without_input() and describe_exception_without_input() (pipelex.tools.typing.pydantic_utils) write a ValidationError as its locations and reasons, never the values it refused.
  • PipelexRequestError: the runtime's own refusal of a request it cannot serve is a PipelineRequestError of the mthds package carrying the core code request.invalid (or request.unsupported) and its problem document, so a client reads the same refusal whether the runtime or the standard's client raised it.
  • Validation warnings as problem items: warning_problem_items() in pipelex.pipeline.validation_errors gives a valid report's warnings as problem items, each under the code its type names, a hint lint's method.hint_invalid naming its hint from the new ValidationErrorItem.hint_key and located at the declaration the hint is on, a concept at concept.<Concept>, a field of its structure at concept.<Concept>.structure.<field>, a pipe's input at the pipe and the input, and root_escape_of(), whose RootEscape gives both the reason a path leaving its root is refused and its rule, and path_refusal_error() in pipelex.core.bundle_resources.bundle_resource, which builds the refusal of a submitted file's path from that escape, with its code and its parameters, the rule of security.input_path_refused or the field resources of request.invalid.
  • The security event: a refusal coded in the security. or pipelex.security. family fails its run under that code and logs one record on its own logger, pipelex.errors.security_event, at warning level, with the message A security rule refused a request and event.name set to pipelex.security.refusal, naming the code, its domain, the kind of target refused, the class of destination when the rule knows it (loopback, private, link_local, metadata, scheme, foreign_storage_key, which the caller's problem states as the registry's private, since its sentence reads the class as a word), the run, the request and each of the run's extras as run.extras.<key>, which the API server reads off a request's analytics_groups as soon as its JSON body is parsed, on the diagnostic routes as on the run routes, and never the URL, path, template or any input value. The process that raises a refusal logs it, once: the pipe run for a refusal raised while it executes, its delivery included, the validation sweep for one a dry run meets before its pipe run starts, such as while its mock inputs are built, the runner for one before the run exists and for one raised in its own process that no pipe run logged, and the API server for one answered before any run, the refusals it authors itself included (a reserved object key, a callback URL the SSRF rule refuses, a resource path or a method file path leaving the method: absolute, naming a drive or a network share, or climbing with .., read with either separator, while a path of the wrong shape, empty or holding a backslash or a colon, logs none and is request.invalid as a key of resources or a file submitted beside a method, and method.package_invalid with the reason invalid_tree_path as a key of files or a member of bundle_b64), which keep their response, while a failure rebuilt from another process's report is never logged again, since the orchestrator that rebuilds it marks it, and no event names a run id a request body chose; pipelex.errors.security_event gives a host emit_security_event(), mark_security_event_emitted() and log_security_event(), and a raise site states the class of destination with PipelexError.with_security_target_class().
  • pipelex.test_extras.required_params_sweep: spy_on_problem_warnings, set before a test, and assert_problems_carried_required_params, run after it, fail a test that builds a problem or an item lacking a parameter its code requires, unless the test carries the builds_problems_without_required_params marker with its reason, and the library's unit tests and the API server's run under them.
  • pipelex.request.dependency_key_mismatch: a dependency a run or validation request keys by another address than the one its own METHODS.toml declares, such as its repository's address alone, is refused with this 422 code, whose key and address parameters give the key sent and the address to key it by, where it was a generic request.invalid.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The problem document replaces ErrorReport (Breaking): every PipelexError answers a problem document, PipelexError.to_problem(view=...) building a PipelexProblem (pipelex.errors.problem), where it built an ErrorReport: its type, title, status, domain, retry and next_step are its code's, its type the code's page (https://mthds.ai/errors/<code> for a core code, https://docs.pipelex.com/errors/<code> for a Pipelex code), its detail and its step are rendered from the code's templates and the parameters the error gives, the code's title standing in for a sentence a missing parameter leaves unrendered, a refusal of several faults lists them in errors, and the Pipelex members request_id, run_error and diagnostics join the standard's. A problem never writes a member a model declares as null, while a null an extension member or a free-form object holds is written as it was read, to_wire() writes back every problem a reader accepts however deeply an extension member nests, a parameter of a type its code does not declare, an infinite or NaN number and a value that is neither a JSON scalar nor a list of them included, is dropped and logged rather than raise in place of the error, and an item never carries a parameter its code keeps for the operator, whoever built it, the caller reading an item whose code this process does not know with no parameter and a generic sentence. ErrorReport, TracedFailure and the graph's ErrorSpec are gone, and error_type is no member of a problem: the operator reads the error's class as diagnostics.error_class.
  • The reader's identity picks the view of a failure (Breaking): a problem is read in the caller's view, its sentences rendered from the parameters a caller may read, or in the operator's, which adds diagnostics (the error's class and message, its causes, the model, the provider's answer, a migration, the runtime version and the trace) and the operator's own next step; DisclosureMode, the ERROR_DISCLOSURE setting and caller_facing_message are gone, and caller_view_of() projects an operator's problem to the caller's, giving a code this process's registries do not hold the generic step of its kind, report for an operator's code. The runner answers the operator's view to a request carrying its static API key (AUTH_MODE=api_key) or reaching it through a trusted proxy (AUTH_MODE=none with TRUST_FORWARDED_IDENTITY_HEADERS=true), which owes its own callers their caller view, and the caller's view to every other request, and a webhook receives the view its target's problem_view names, the caller's by default, the problem built only for a run that has a webhook and never replacing the run's own error when it cannot be built.
  • The runner answers each code's HTTP status (Breaking): an error response's status is its code's, from the error registry, where it followed the error's domain and a table of per-class overrides, so provider.unavailable answers 502, provider.timeout 504, model.unavailable 501, a method that cannot be fetched (method.fetch_failed) 502 where it answered 422, and a fetched method declaring Python structures (pipelex.deployment.python_structures_refused) 422 where it answered 403; Retry-After rides a 429 alone, and an exception that is not a Pipelex error answers runtime.unexpected, a 500.
  • An input refusal names the input and what is wrong with it: a refusal of a run's inputs carries the input in params.input and location.input, with the facts its code declares, the expected and provided counts of input.wrong_multiplicity, the declared and provided concepts of input.wrong_concept and the field at fault of input.invalid when the concept's structure names one, so its detail names the input and its fault; a refused file, whether its url is blank or malformed, its storage reference names nothing, its data URL or local path cannot be read, the run may not read it, or its format is one its input or its model cannot take, names the run's input as input and the path down to the file as location.field, such as documents[1], or documents[1].url for its url, which input.invalid also gives as its field. A CSV table input refused before it is read says what happened: a url that does not parse is input.file_unreadable, a url that is not a local path request.unsupported with the reason remote_table_url, and a concept with no structure class method.concept_invalid, where each was an input.invalid about the concept's structure, and every CSV refusal, before or while the table is read, is located on the input in location.input.
  • A run failure's problem names its pipe and path: the problem of a run that failed inside a pipe carries the failing pipe and the pipes leading to it as location.pipe and location.path, and fills the pipe parameter of a code that declares one, while a failure of the entry pipe before any step carries no location. The location also keeps what the errors between the run and its root fault know, such as the field and the file a pipe met an unknown model at, and the diagnostics keep the model and the backend a worker attributed the failure to on an error above the root fault, an inner router's stand-in for a foreign exception included. A parameter a wrapper above the error whose code the problem reports gave, and its code declares, fills the one that error gave none of, and the items a wrapper gave follow that error's own.
  • A graph node's error is its problem (Breaking): a failed node of a GraphSpec, and the trace event that ended its pipe, carry the problem in the caller's view in error, located at the node's pipe and path, and the stack trace, when the graph's data inclusion asks for it, in error_stack, capped at the same length on both, where error held error_type, message, stack and caller_facing.
  • Plugin API v9 (Breaking): an HTTP-error mapper registered with add_http_error_mapper(exc_type_provider=..., to_pipelex_error=...) returns the PipelexError a transport exception stands for, where to_error_report returned a report, and a bundle validator's validate_bundles returns a BundleValidationFailure, the refusal's problem in the operator's view with its validation items, as its invalid verdict, and a host plugin's carrier of a problem recovered across a transport boundary overrides PipelexError.recovered_problem() to return it rather than overriding to_problem(), which a located run failure no longer reads as a carrier; PLUGIN_API_VERSION moves to 9, so a plugin declaring targets_api = 8 is refused at discovery with PluginApiVersionMismatchError.
  • pipelex.test_extras.problem_parity (Breaking): the parity fixtures a distributed executor's tests share with the local runner's moved from pipelex.test_extras.error_report_parity, and their classes are ProblemParityTestData, SearchProblemParityTestData and JudgeProblemParityTestData.
  • A run failure reports its root fault's code (Breaking): the root fault a run failure's problem reports is the first error down its cause chain that declares a code of its own, and its code, title, type, domain and retry verdict are the problem's, with no runtime floor on the domain; a consumer that branched on the wrapper's error_type branches on code. A PipeFunc whose function raised reads pipe.function_raised whatever it raised, a coded error of a helper the function called included, which rides as the cause, while a failure of the executor running it, such as its timeout, keeps its own code, and an exception an executor lets through that is not a Pipelex error, such as an out-of-process executor's transport failure, reads runtime.unexpected. A failure below an exception that is not a Pipelex error lends the error above it no code, fact, location or advice.
  • The runner's own refusals are coded problem documents (Breaking): every error response of the API server, a 404 for a path no route serves, a 405 and a 413 included, is a problem document carrying a registry code, and the API's ErrorType is gone with the error_type, error_domain, retryable and instance members, the tree_refusal, missing_blobs and mismatched_blobs members becoming the code's parameters or the operator's diagnostics. A field the runner refuses is request.invalid naming it as params.field, with one item in errors per refused field up to a bound, which the operator's diagnostics.message keeps too, saying how many more faults there were, a rule over several fields naming the one to change, such as the second of two selectors sent or mthds_sources beside a method_ref, a body or a part of one it cannot parse request.malformed with a reason, a size limit request.too_large with its limit and the size in bytes, an encoded value measured by the bytes it carries, and a method tree it cannot read method.package_invalid with a reason, the standard's tree refusal code or one of the runner's own, one per rule and one per limit, so an archive past its member count reads bundle_too_many_files, while a body refused beyond its schema on /v1/execute or /v1/start (a bundle sent with mthds_contents, method_ref beside a bundle, resources or dependencies without their files, no run source, a hosted-only field such as method_id) answers a PipelexRequestError carrying request.invalid or request.unsupported; the API's ProblemDocument schema documents code, and request_id, taken from X-Request-ID or minted, is what correlates a response with the server's log.
  • The runner's refusals answer their code's status (Breaking): an orchestration-mode override the deployment forbids is a 422 where it was a 403, custom Python on a deployment that is not sandbox-hosted a 501 where it was a 403, /v1/start on a blocking-only deployment a 501 runtime.unsupported where it was a 400, a registry-form method_ref a 422 request.unsupported where it was a 501, invalid base64 and a client gone mid-upload a 422 where they were a 400, an archive past its file-count or decompressed-size ceiling and too many resources a 422 where they were a 413, a blob past the per-file limit a 413 where it was a 422, a forwarded X-User-Id that is not path-safe a 422 request.invalid naming the header where it was a 400, a body FastAPI could not parse, holding bytes that are not UTF-8 or an integer past Python's digit limit, a 422 request.malformed with the reason not_utf8 or integer_too_long where it was a 400, while the framework's own refusals, plain {"detail": …} bodies until now, keep their status under a code whose required parameters the runner can fill, a 400 as request.malformed with the reason unreadable, a 401 as auth.missing_credential keeping its WWW-Authenticate challenge, a 403 as auth.invalid_credential, a 413 as request.malformed with the reason too_large, a 429 as runtime.unavailable keeping its Retry-After, and any other, such as a 415, as request.malformed with the reason unreadable, a read_scope a jwt caller may not read a 403 auth.forbidden whose requirement is read_scope_under_caller where it was a 403 ReadScopeForbidden, and a token whose claims the runner cannot use a 500 where it was a 401; a 401 carries WWW-Authenticate: Bearer only where the deployment reads a bearer token (AUTH_MODE=api_key or AUTH_MODE=jwt), so behind a trusted proxy a missing X-User-Id is a 401 asking for no token.
  • Damaged stored bytes are a damaged stored file, never retried: bytes the API server's blob store holds under a hash that do not hash to it, or are not the size it holds them at, answer a 500 pipelex.storage.damaged, a new code of the Pipelex error registry, naming the kind of storage, plugin for a storage plugin's own, whose verdict is not to retry, since a retry reads the same damaged object, and which /v1/execute, /v1/start, /v1/validate, /v1/resolve, /v1/codegen, /v1/pipe-io and PUT /v1/blobs/{sha256} declare in their OpenAPI responses; the server's line naming the object to remove, Stored blob bytes do not match their hash, carries blob_sha256, blob_size_bytes, read_size_bytes and storage_scheme.
  • The /validate Markdown presents the verdict's items (Breaking): the opt-in rendered_markdown of an invalid verdict is rendered from the problem items its errors holds, in the same view, each under its code's title with its code, location, sentence, suggestions and suggested fix, so a caller reads no wording its view of the items leaves out, where it rendered the validation items' own messages; pipelex.pipeline.validation_render.render_invalid_verdict_markdown(items=..., message=...) replaces render_invalid_validation_markdown(report).
  • The diagnostic routes' verdicts carry problem items (Breaking): the invalid arm of /v1/validate, /v1/resolve, /v1/codegen and /v1/pipe-io carries errors, one problem item per finding with its code, detail, params and location and a suggested fix naming its file as file, where it carried validation_errors, the valid arm's warnings are problem items too, and a top-level member a verdict has no value for, such as default_pipe_ref or graph_spec, is absent rather than null. The OpenAPI artifact no longer publishes ValidationErrorItem or pipelex's SuggestedFix, and names every schema reachable from the standard's problem item with a Problem prefix, such as ProblemSuggestedFix and ProblemSetKeyOp.
  • Pipe selection refusals carry the code of their case: an entry pipe the selector names but no closure declares reads request.pipe_not_found, offering as its suggestions only pipes the caller may select, the method's own for a bare or domain-qualified code, never a pipe of the server's own library directories, and for an alias->… code the pipes that dependency exports, a bare selector matching pipes in several domains request.pipe_ambiguous, a request with no selector over a closure declaring no main_pipe, or several, request.pipe_unspecified, naming the declared ones as its candidates, a manifest main_pipe the closure lacks method.pipe_unresolved, naming the main_pipe declaration as its pipe and the nearest declared pipes as its candidates, and one it declares in several domains method.ref_ambiguous, all still a 422, a dependency's alias->code matching pipes in several of its domains naming them as candidates too; a run of a method on disk with no pipe named refuses several declared main_pipes and a manifest main_pipe several bundles define the same way.
  • PipeIOContractError is the method's (Breaking): a structure that cannot be projected into its IO contract answers a 422 carrying method.concept_invalid, naming the concept and the finding, where it answered a 500.
  • Storage and remote-file failures say whose they are: an S3 or GCS refusal of the deployment's credentials (AccessDenied, an invalid or expired key, Forbidden) carries pipelex.config.credential_refused, a bucket that does not exist pipelex.config.invalid and missing credentials pipelex.config.credential_missing, apart from an outage, pipelex.storage.unavailable, naming the kind of storage; a remote file that times out, refuses the connection or answers a 5xx, 408, 425 or 429 is input.url_unreachable, which a retry may cure, and any other failed fetch input.file_unreadable.
  • Builtins raised where a reader sees them are coded classes: refusals that raised a bare ValueError, RuntimeError, ImportError or NotImplementedError raise a coded PipelexError, such as RunParameterError for a run's metadata, extras or storage scope (still a ValueError), ExportedPipeNotFoundError and ExportedPipeAmbiguousError for a CLI pipe selector, BundleClosureEmptyError, StorageNotConfiguredError, UrlSyntaxError, LocalFileMissingError and UnsupportedImageMimeTypeError, and the classes that were rooted outside PipelexError (PipeValidationError, ConceptValueError, QualifiedRefError, SemVerError, MethodNotFoundError and the like) join it.
  • Inference failures carry the code their classification picks (Breaking): the classification of a provider's failure picks a code with its category, a ServiceErrorCode a plugin contributes names its error_code, and a category that repeats the call within the run must pick a code that invites a retry; an error built with a category alone reports the category's code (provider.unavailable for TRANSIENT, runtime.misconfigured for CONFIGURATION, provider.quota_exhausted for CAPACITY, provider.outcome_unknown for AMBIGUOUS). A provider 400 that carries no context-window or content-policy signal is runtime.unexpected, answered 500, where it was the caller's 422, and a local extractor's OSError is runtime.unexpected, no longer repeated within the run.
  • One rule for a request id (Breaking): a run's request_id holds ASCII letters, digits, _ and - alone, at most 128 of them, the rule the API server applies to an inbound X-Request-ID, now one function, pipelex.system.job_metadata.is_valid_request_id(), where a run accepted any printable ASCII, a space, a quote or an = that could forge a field of a key=value log line or a parameter of a header included; RunParameterError no longer quotes the refused value.
  • A truncated completion says which limit cut it: LLMCompletionTruncatedError carries model.output_truncated when the method's max_tokens cut the answer and model.context_exceeded when the context window did, both the method's to change.
  • ModelDeckPresetValidationError is spelt right (Breaking): the error a model deck preset that fails validation raises was ModelDeckPresetValidatonError, and its reports carried that error_type; a consumer that branched on the old name branches on the new one, or on its code, pipelex.config.invalid.
  • Usage statistics carry the error's code (Breaking): a failed command_completed or run_completed carries the code of its error in error_code and that code's domain in error_domain, now one of input, method, account, operator and runtime where it read input, config, runtime or other, and a model_used counts its failed calls by the domain of their code, in failures_input, failures_method, failures_account, failures_operator and failures_runtime, where it counted them by the runtime's inference category, which no event carries any more. A failed hosted run's command_completed carries the code and the domain the hosted API sent, and none when it sent none, and every surface reads a refusal a server answered by that rule, a run's run_completed reading the catch-all where nothing was sent rather than the code the client infers from the status. Every event's schema is 2, so a receiver tells these events from an earlier release's.
  • pipelex-agent reports a failure as its problem (Breaking): the agent CLI's error stream is the failure's problem in the operator's view, Markdown by default and JSON with --error-format json: its code, domain, retry verdict and next_step, its params, location and errors, its request_id and pipeline_run_id, and diagnostics with the error's class, the model and the provider of a failed call and a pending configuration migration, which rides diagnostics.migration where it rode migration, beside the command's own message and members. The envelope's error, error_type, error_domain, error_code, error_category, retryable, hint, validation_errors, error_source, and a failed run's pipe_code, pipe_stack, cause_type and cause_message, are gone, and so are AGENT_ERROR_HINTS, AGENT_ERROR_DOMAINS, AGENT_INIT_FAILURE_HINT, run_failure_fields() and extract_validation_errors(): an agent branches on code, an invalid verdict's items are the problem's errors, a failed run is located by location.pipe and location.path, and the advice an error's chain gives is a Markdown tip, a boot that fails with no advice of its own tipping the recovery path through doctor, migrate and init. A refusal the CLI makes itself carries its own code, client.argument_invalid for an argument, client.file_unreadable for a file it cannot read, the bundle file of every bundle command included, client.tool_missing when plxt is not installed, and pipelex.config.file_missing when init finds a configuration file it should have written missing, and an exception that is no Pipelex error reads runtime.unexpected, an error of the system that names no file, such as a refused connection or a timeout, included. A bundle file that is not UTF-8 text does not parse, so run bundle and fix bundle report it as validate bundle does, the invalid verdict with a method.syntax item, where run bundle read it as a file it could not read; fix bundle codes the errors left as validate bundle codes them, where an item no stage classified read method.schema_violation, and a fix it cannot write is client.write_failed. The Markdown lists the problem's items one per line, each with its code, sentence, location, suggestions and suggested fix, an invalid verdict's included, where it rendered a verdict's items as validate's category-grouped prose.
