A run on a runner (--runner hosted) that fails reports the problem the runner answered or the client decided, as it came, by the members the standard and Pipelex declare alone, in the caller's view: the runner's problem document with its errors, client.unreachable naming the base URL for a runner that cannot be reached, client.outcome_unknown for a server fault on the run request, and run.failed naming the run for a run that started and failed, the client's own sentence as message, nesting the run's own problem as run_error in the caller's view, read off its stored report whatever its shape; an answer in the shape that predates the standard's reads as the core code its status and the hosted plane's own code name, auth.invalid_credential, auth.missing_credential when no key was sent, auth.forbidden for an operation the platform refuses a key it accepted, under one of its authorization codes, request.not_found, run.not_found or method.not_found, or account.rate_limited with its retry_after, a runner's refusal of a method that does not validate lists its validation items under method.invalid, and any other such answer keeps the client's client.response_unreadable with the reason it gave; each takes the next step pipelex run --hosted gives, of the kind the answer's advice names when it gave one, and so does a failure the client meets on its own side; what the CLI refuses before sending it is a problem in the operator's view, and so is a failure of its own, under its own code, except a method run bundle refuses while reading it, a bundle that does not parse or validate or a bundle file or folder with no pipe to start at, which reads in the caller's view as the runner's refusal of the same method would, with its code, items, locations and next step and neither diagnostics nor message.
  • The pipelex error panels print the problem: a panel names the problem's title, its detail, its next step, its code with its domain and retry verdict, its location and its request id beside the fields it printed, and a run that fails, or any failure a command root catches, prints its problem the same way on stderr, where it printed one line with the message. Every panel, an invalid bundle's, an unavailable model's or a telemetry file's included, and the stack trace --traceback adds to it, now goes to stderr, where the panels and their stack traces went to stdout, so a command's piped output holds only what it produced.
  • A configuration refusal names its setting and its file: pipelex.config.invalid raised for a configuration that does not validate, a telemetry configuration, a tracing sink or what a former release left in the inference configuration names the setting, its file and the configuration it belongs to in the operator's next step, a file the refusal can single out, a former release's or one that does not parse (pipelex.config.syntax, where pipelex show config named pipelex.toml whichever layer failed), named relative to the working directory or as ~/… under the home directory, never with the home directory's account, and its advice, the tip a CLI prints, follows the pending migration, pipelex migrate when it would rewrite the files and a correction by hand when it would not, and else the refusal's code: pipelex init for a missing file, setting the variable for one that is not set, and pipelex doctor for a configuration that does not validate or parse. The refusal of what a former release left carries in diagnostics.migration what pipelex migrate would do about it, from the cleanup's dry run, so a JSON reader, who gets no tip, reads the remedy too.
  • A pipe's failure line carries its code, not its text: The execution of a pipe failed carries the problem's error.code beside error.type and no longer error.message, so a log query selects failed pipes by code, and the line holds neither the caller's own text, a function's message or a template's source, nor a refused host.
  • Jinja2TemplateSecurityError is a SecurityError (Breaking): the template sandbox's refusal at render time now derives from SecurityError, like UriReadRefusedError, SsrfBlockedError and UnsafeSchemaError, instead of ToolError, so a host catching SecurityError catches it too and an except ToolError no longer does; it stays a type of its own, apart from Jinja2TemplateRenderError, and its class name, which the operator reads as diagnostics.error_class, its code, security.template_refused on a method's template, its title and its classification are unchanged.
  • A security refusal is never a validation verdict (Breaking): a refusal a raise site coded in the security. family is let through by the bundle-validation cascade whatever its class, as a SecurityError always was, so a PipeDocGen step whose template_file climbs above its method tree's root fails validate and a run with security.method_path_refused and logs its security event, where it was a method.invalid verdict naming the pipe; a refusal a validation's dry run meets, such as a template the sandbox refuses at render, fails it the same way under its own code, every failure riding its items and the event logged once, where it was an item of an invalid verdict.
  • mthds 0.22.1 and pipelex-sdk 0.46.0 (Breaking): the exact pins move from mthds==0.22.0 and pipelex-sdk==0.45.0 to mthds==0.22.1, the release whose errors carry the MTHDS problem document read by its registry code, and pipelex-sdk==0.46.0, the release built on it; everyone downstream inherits those exact versions.
  • A problem carries every parameter its code requires: every problem and item the runtime and the API server build gives each parameter its code's registry entry requires, so its sentences state the occurrence rather than the code's generic wording: a model no catalog knows offers its suggestions, an empty list when none is near, an invalid identifier names its identifier_kind and name, a name declared twice, or a native concept declared again, names the name and the conflict in one item per bundle, each located on its own file and on the colliding declaration's path, such as concept.Rating, in a validation verdict and a run's refusal alike, while a batch item named as its list stays on its pipe and the field it collides on, input_item_name or a step's steps.0.batch_as, an unresolved concept and a selected pipe the method lacks offer the nearest declared ones, a pipe reference naming nothing the pipe whose body writes it and the nearest pipes it may name, of a dependency only those it exports unless the reference is written in that dependency, and beside a server's own library directories only the pipes of the bundles the request sent, a template the sandbox refuses names what it reached for as name when its own source spells it, the format string a .format call formats included but no other string literal, and is located on its pipe and the field the template is written in, while a name the run's data chose is withheld and its sentences say the template looked a name up from the run's data, a validation item gives the facts its check knows (the concept a pipe declares and those that would fit, the multiplicity it declares and the one its use expects, the site where an optional value escapes, the path a binding cannot follow), and method.package_invalid always gives its reason, tree_unreadable for a tree that cannot be listed among the new ones. A failure met while running names its facts too: a stored file gone and a storage outage name the kind of storage as scheme, which a storage provider's new storage_kind gives, plugin unless a provider says otherwise, a pipe added twice to a library, a duplicate branch output and a module the tree shadows name the name and the conflict, a file a model cannot read its format and model, a remote file that cannot be fetched its host or its reason, a completion the context window cut, and a prompt a provider refuses as over the context window, its limit, a Gemini image a filter refused its model, a model a provider does not know or refuses and a waterfall with nothing served the model_type and reason of model.unavailable, a PipeFunc past its deadline its function and timeout, a PipeJudge question that reads a file the step's input and the concept it declared, a requirement whose extra needs a missing or mismatched distribution that distribution with not_found or no_matching_version, a call to a pipe another domain of the package does not export the pipe and the package, one item per call located on the bundle, the pipe and the field that write it, and bundles declaring a reserved domain, which a package's METHODS.toml refuses as method.name_conflict too, or two declarations of one name whose bundles are unknown, one item each, on its own file. ValidationErrorItem and PipesAndConceptValidationErrorData carry those facts in params, and the problem builders log A problem lacks a parameter its code requires when a raise site gives fewer, except for a parameter withheld by rule, the refused name a template looked up from the run's data.
  • A refusal of one fault carries no errors list (Breaking): a problem whose only item restated its own code, such as /v1/models/check's refusal of a missing reference or a template the sandbox refused while validating, carries that item's parameters and location itself and no errors; a refusal whose single item has another code, such as method.invalid over one fault, keeps its list, and one whose single item carries suggestions or a suggested fix takes that item's parameters and location and keeps the item listed, so its fix reaches the caller.
  • A model no enabled backend serves is model.unavailable (Breaking): a method naming a model a catalog of the deployment knows but no backend it enables serves, such as claude-4.5-haiku with anthropic switched off, answers a 501 model.unavailable with the reason not_served, located on the pipe and its model field, when it is validated and when it runs, where it was the method's model.unknown verdict; a switched-off backend's model file that is missing, is not UTF-8 text or does not parse declares nothing and never stops the boot.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A model deck's own unresolved default or override is the deployment's fault: a deck default or override naming a model the deck does not define raises ModelDeckChoiceUnresolvedError, naming the deck setting and carrying model.unavailable, with the reason not_served, for a bare handle no backend serves, answered 501, and pipelex.config.invalid for a preset, an alias or a waterfall the deck does not define, answered 500, with the deck setting in the operator's diagnostics alone, where it read as the caller's unknown model, and a PipeJudge naming no model, whose default is resolved as its method loads, raises it rather than an unknown_model verdict item; a bad override is refused when the deck is built, and a handle the deck serves only as another type of model is model.capability_unsupported.
  • A host library that refuses to load is the deployment's fault: a method of a server's own library directories that refuses to load beside a caller's bundles raises HostLibraryLoadRefusalError, carrying pipelex.config.invalid, which an API answers with a 500 whose message reaches the operator's diagnostics alone, where it answered the caller a 422 verdict carrying the host library's text; the same refusal in the caller's own content, or in library directories the caller owns, stays the caller's 422 verdict.
  • A template error found only at render is a located refusal: a template naming a filter or a test that does not exist, which Jinja2 only finds when the branch renders, fails the run at the pipe with Jinja2TemplateInvalidError, naming the unknown filter or test and none of the template, coded method.template_invalid, a 422, when the template is the method's, in a PipeCondition expression, a PipeLLM prompt or system prompt and a PipeDocGen template, and runtime.unexpected when it is one of Pipelex's own, such as the deployment's structure prompt rendered in a PipeLLM step, where it failed as an unclassified 500. A filter refusing its argument, which may be a value of the run's data, is pipe.template_render_failed rather than the template's fault.
  • A failure's message is bounded: the error's message a problem carries in diagnostics.message, a provider's answer and every text parameter are cut at 2,000 characters, ending in […], so an oversized exception cannot swell a response, a stored run or a log line.
  • A dry run failing on a fault of the runtime's is no verdict: validating a method whose dry run fails only on faults that are not the method's, such as a storage outage or an unexpected error, answers the first of those faults' codes, every failure listed in errors, where it answered method.invalid and blamed the method; a verdict needs one failure in the method's domain, and the first fault is chosen with a no retry verdict before a retryable one, then the operator's before the account's, the input's and the runtime's, the answer's sentence rendered from the failure whose code it takes. A mock value a routed pipe cannot build, a pydantic or polyfactory refusal, stays the method's method.mock_unsatisfiable. A refusal met while loading that is not the method's keeps its own class and code in the same way, so pipelex run bundle and pipelex-agent run bundle on a folder whose bundles declare no single main_pipe print the run's refusal, request.pipe_unspecified or request.pipe_ambiguous, where they printed an invalid verdict. A hosted run whose inputs name a local file tells POST /v1/pipe-io's verdict on a method calling a package by its address that the request did not ship apart from a fault of the method by the verdict's method.dependency_missing item of the kind package, naming the package its params.name gives, where it matched the words of the item's message.
  • A provider's 408 is retried: a provider answering HTTP 408, that it gave up waiting, is a transient failure carrying provider.timeout, so the call is repeated within the run, a billed image call included, where it was read as the caller's input and the run failed on its first attempt.
  • A PipeFunc returning a list of anything but stuff contents fails its output: a function returning a list that holds a value other than a stuff content, such as a dict or a number, fails the step with FuncOutputTypeError (pipe.output_invalid), where a dict became an empty content and any other value failed as though the function had raised.
  • A CLI command's unexpected failure logs no run data: the root of pipelex run and of pipelex graph render logs an unexpected failure with the code of its problem, its class, the classes along its cause chain and the frames it went through, each by its module, line and function with no source line or local (error.frames), where it attached the exception, whose traceback printed the text of every chained exception, a foreign ValidationError quoting the values it refused or a method function's exception included; the traceback rides the record only under --traceback, and the terminal prints the failure's message capped.
  • A prompt over the model's context window reads model.context_exceeded: a provider 400, or another 4xx such as the 422 or 413 a gateway may answer, saying the inputs are over what the model can read, by OpenAI's context_length_exceeded code or by the wording OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Bedrock and Gemini give it, in the error's message or its body, is the caller's model.context_exceeded, answered 422, where it read runtime.unexpected, or input.too_large on a 413. A language model's window holds the prompt and the output requested with max_tokens together, and a 400 the max_tokens sent caused reads the same, so its next step is to shorten the input or lower max_tokens, or choose a model with a larger context window; an image, extraction, search or judgment model's next step names what it reads instead. A 400 about a malformed request still reads runtime.unexpected.
  • A structured output cut at max_tokens reads model.output_truncated: the Anthropic, OpenAI Chat Completions and Mistral workers turn instructor's IncompleteOutputException, raised for a structured answer cut at its output limit, into LLMCompletionTruncatedError, naming a structured output, the stop value, the output tokens and the max_tokens sent, where it escaped unclassified as runtime.unexpected. LLMCompletionTruncatedError takes an output_kind, a text or a structured output. When the Anthropic structured-output timeout lowered the limit that cut it, the error says so and advises a lower reasoning effort or a smaller output, never a higher max_tokens.
  • A Gemini image a safety filter blocked reads model.content_refused: the Google image worker reads the answer's finish reason, or the prompt's block reason when no candidate came back, and raises ImgGenGenerationError with model.content_refused, answered 422 with a next step to revise the prompt or its images, where an IMAGE_SAFETY or PROHIBITED_CONTENT answer read as an empty one, provider.response_invalid. The message names the reason Gemini gave and what it says, so an image stopped for recitation or for an unsupported language reads the same code without being called a safety block. An answer the model's output token limit stopped before it held an image (MAX_TOKENS) raises the new ImgGenOutputTruncatedError, model.output_truncated, answered 422 with a next step to simplify the prompt or choose another image model, where it read provider.response_invalid.
  • No error message carries a run's data: an error's message, which reaches the operator's diagnostics, the error tracker and the log lines, no longer quotes an input's value, a stuff's content, a model's answer or a value a pipe built: a refused input is described by its kind and size, a list item by its index and type, a URL by its scheme when it is one Pipelex reads, a date or a time by the form it expected, a pydantic refusal of a run's data, a provider's metadata included, by its locations and reasons, a stuff by its code and concept, and a file of unknown type by the number of bytes read. A PipeFunc whose function raised names the class of what it raised and never its text, as does any other failure of its executor, by its class and its code; a template that fails to render is described by the class Jinja2 raised and the template's line, never by Jinja2's text, which quotes a key of the data the template reached for, nor by its source, a name it reached for, the sandbox's refusals and the render budget's refusal of a call included, being named only when the parsed template spells it, a syntax error by its kind and line rather than the token Jinja2 quotes, and Pipelex's filters never quoting the argument they refuse; a structured generation instructor gave up on is described by the refused answer's reasons, located by the class it asked for, by the class of any other failure to parse the answer, a model's refusal included, or by the class of what ended its loop; an exception that is not a Pipelex error stands in a problem's diagnostics as its class alone, a run's and the API server's catch-all's alike; and no message names a refused or unreachable host, which input.url_unreachable takes as its host parameter, alongside the input the URL came from, which an extract worker, a prompt's image or document and a document's page views name, while a provider's file that could not be fetched is given no parameter its code does not declare. A failure following a pipe's own, a delivery's or the graph tracer's, is logged by its class and code, a webhook's transport failure is named by its class, a trace event log's refusal and the tracing assembly's errors are written by their reasons, and no sink writes instructor's log records, which quote the model's answers. A location never quotes a key of the value's own: a key of a dict, or one the model does not declare, is written <key> (entries.<key>.score), only what the validated type's schema names is written as it is, and a refusal whose model is not known is written by its reasons alone; every site that validates an input into its concept's class, an explicit envelope and a transported stuff included, locates its refusal by that class, an explicit envelope's naming the input and the field as input.invalid's parameters, and a refusal of a method author's own document is located as pydantic gives it (is_authored_input). A CSV input's refusal names the file by the input it was given as, never by its path, and quotes no cell nor a column the concept does not declare; its problem takes the input as its input parameter.
  • Pre-release documentation is published: a push to a pre-release/ branch deploys its documentation under the pre-release alias of docs.pipelex.com, where the deploy workflow called a make target with no recipe and published nothing.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• The per-class error pages (Breaking): the generated page every PipelexError class had under docs/errors/, pipelex-dev generate-error-pages (make gep) and pipelex.errors.error_pages_generator are gone; a problem's type is now its code's page, and docs.pipelex.com redirects each retired page to the page of its class's code, or to the Error Codes index when the class is gone or raises no single code.
  • Class-level error classification (Breaking): an error class no longer declares error_domain or retryable, PipelexError.title() and PipelexError.type_uri() are gone, and so is InferenceErrorCategory.error_domain: the class declares its error_code, which decides all four, and an inference failure's category, which stays inside the runtime, picks the code its worker raises. as_caller_fault() is gone too, since a caller reads the sentences a code renders and never an error's own message.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Callback URLs are held to the runtime's SSRF rule: the runner refuses a /v1/start callback URL with the rule the webhook delivery applies when it fires, pipelex.tools.network.host_rules, so a cloud metadata name spelled in capitals or with a trailing dot, and an address that is not publicly routable such as a carrier-grade NAT one, are refused with a 422 security.input_url_refused before the run, where the runner's own copy of the rule let them through to the delivery; a host of dots alone, such as http://./hook, names no host, and a host and port written with no scheme, such as localhost:3000/cb, opens no authority, so each is a 422 request.invalid naming callback_urls, with no security event, while a scheme-relative URL whose host the rule refuses, such as //169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data, is the rule's refusal, classed by its host.
  • The API server's error line quotes no exception (Breaking): every error line carries error.code and names the classes of the failure's exception chain in error.chain, and an error-level line adds error.frames, where the deepest exception was raised, in place of the traceback under exception, so no exception's text, which a foreign exception can fill with a run's inputs or a model's answer, reaches the log, and an exception the catch-all answered no longer reaches the server, whose log would print its traceback; the detail field is gone too. The error's message rides the operator view's diagnostics alone, which only a request the operator authenticated reads (AUTH_MODE=api_key, or a trusted proxy's forwarded identity), so every line names the problem's operator-only parameters as error.params.<name>, such as the component of a runtime.misconfigured, whichever view the response took. A refusal the runner answers in place of a framework exception, FastAPI's RequestValidationError, Starlette's ClientDisconnect or an HTTPException, names that exception's class after its own in error.chain, and a failure no handler recorded that ended a request after its response had started, the catch-all's own failure while a response streamed, is written as A request failed after its response had started, naming its path, the status already sent and its classes alone, where it was dropped unrecorded; so is a failure to send the answer the server built for a failure no handler answered, such as to a client already gone. A line's level says who has to act, from its status and its code's domain: a 4xx is a warning, a 5xx an error with frames only when its domain is the runtime's or the operator's, a 501, what the deployment does not offer, such as custom Python without a sandbox or /v1/start on a blocking-only orchestrator, a warning without frames, where every 5xx was an error, and a 404 or 405 for a request no route serves a debug line, where it was a warning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• resolve_crate_from_method_dir: pipelex.pipeline.resolve_bundle resolves a method's tree a host wrote out to a directory into the normalized crate, loading it as the caller's library directory the way validate_bundle loads a method_dir, with methods_dirs holding the packages shipped with it, under the same ValidateBundleError verdict and loaded-on-success contract as resolve_crate_from_contents. The resolution is static: a package the method calls by its address is loaded from methods_dirs alone, never from the methods installed on the host or by a fetch, and one they do not hold is an unresolved_package_dependency item of the verdict.
  • address_dependency_sources: LibraryManager.load_libraries and load_from_blueprints take an AddressDependencySources (pipelex.methods.address_dependencies), ANYWHERE by default, which looks for a package called by its address among the load's methods_dirs, then the installed methods, then fetches it when fetch-on-miss is on, or SHIPPED, which looks only in methods_dirs and reports a package they do not hold as an unresolved_package_dependency item raised from the new MethodDependencyNotShippedError.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Every command taking a method's folder reads it as its method tree (Breaking): validate bundle and fix bundle on both CLIs judge every bundle of the folder's tree, as the MTHDS protocol's validation does, instead of a bundle.mthds or the folder's only .mthds file, so a folder whose bundles declare several main_pipes, or none, is validated and fixed like any other, one holding no bundle exits with code 2 under EmptyMethodTreeError, one whose tree cannot be read is their invalid verdict naming the folder (FixBundleError on pipelex-agent fix bundle), and a fix writes anywhere in the tree from its root, the --diff preview proposing what the real run writes. pipelex-agent inputs bundle, pipelex build inputs bundle and pipelex build output bundle act, with no --pipe, on the pipe run bundle starts at, the METHODS.toml's main_pipe or, with no manifest, the one main_pipe its bundles declare, loaded with the rest of the method's folder, and refuse a folder that decides none with the MethodEntryError run bundle gives. pipelex-agent validate bundle <folder> --graph draws that same pipe, or the one --pipe names, and when the folder decides none it says why in graph_unavailable instead of failing the validation; on every command reading a folder, a configuration that does not validate, read before the boot for the tree's limits, is reported as the failed boot it would be.
  • Validating a method's tree judges only its own pipes (Breaking): validate_bundle(method_dir=...), and so POST /v1/validate on a method's files and validate bundle <folder>, dry-runs and reports only the bundles of the method's own tree; a nested package below it with its own METHODS.toml, the packages it depends on and the -L directories still load for its bundles to use, but their pipes are no longer judged with it.
  • /v1/resolve, /v1/codegen and /v1/pipe-io take the method tree (Breaking): the three routes take the method as /v1/validate and the run routes do, files being the MTHDS protocol's map of file entries with dependencies, resources and read_scope beside it, or a method_ref whose package's whole tree is loaded with the packages it ships, so a call into another package by its address resolves when that package was shipped, while one nothing shipped is the invalid verdict, never looked up among the runner's installed methods or fetched, and a METHODS.toml at the root of a sent tree names the default pipe of /v1/pipe-io, which reads it only for a request naming no pipe. A files list of {content, source} items is refused with a 422 InvalidMethodFiles, the tree's refusals and the custom-Python 403s are those of /v1/validate, include_files echoes the method's .mthds bundles as a map from tree path to text, and the request models MthdsFilesRequest, MthdsFileItem and MthdsPipeRequest are removed. The routes load the method in a worker thread, so a slow load never holds up the server's other requests.
  • A bundle validator receives the read scope, plugin API version 8 (Breaking): BundleValidatorProtocol.validate_bundles takes read_scope, the scope the host named for the validation, None when it named none, so a validator dispatching the validation to another process hands the method's trees to its worker through that scope's blob store and the worker reads them by digest under it, as a run's worker reads under the run's read scope. The API server's POST /v1/validate hands its validator the request's read_scope on every arm, never the caller's own id, and PLUGIN_API_VERSION moves to 8, so a plugin declaring targets_api = 7 is refused at discovery with PluginApiVersionMismatchError.
  • A PipeFunc package-offer factory receives the method's requirements, under plugin API version 8 (Breaking): a factory registered with PluginRegistrar.add_pipe_func_package_offer is called with a PipeFuncPackageOfferRequest, the pipe_func config and the requirements of the one method tree being judged, where it received the config alone, so a sandbox mode building an environment for each method states the environment it builds for them, or answers a PipeFuncPackageRefusal when none can hold them, which refuses the method with a MethodRequirementsNotMetError carrying the plugin's reason. Each tree judged in one check gets the offer stated for its own requirements, and the factory stays synchronous, so a plugin whose answer takes time caches it by the requirements. The requirements arrive with their markers unevaluated, and the new requirements_needed_in (pipelex.libraries.method_requirements) picks out those whose markers hold where the mode would run the method, the only ones a refusal may rest on; parse_requirements_text, RequirementLine and REQUIREMENTS_FILE_NAME move to pipelex.core.method_trees.requirements_file.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A main_pipe that is not a pipe code is an invalid bundle: a bundle declaring its main_pipe as another type, such as a list, is refused with a validation error located on main_pipe instead of crashing the parse with a TypeError, and a folder's entry rule refuses a main_pipe that is no pipe code, such as domain.pipe, a camelCase name or an empty string, with the same located error instead of reading an empty one as declaring none.
  • Load errors name a written tree's bundles by their tree paths: an error raised once the bundles of a tree the server wrote out have parsed, such as a concept declared in two bundles, names them by their tree paths instead of the directory they were written to, so a verdict of /v1/validate, a run or a crate route no longer discloses a path on the server.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• An auto-detected inputs file must be a regular file (Breaking): pipelex run bundle <folder> and pipelex-agent run bundle <folder> read the folder's inputs.json or inputs.toml only when it is a regular file, opened without following a link and judged on the descriptor its bytes are read from, and refuse a symbolic link, a directory or any other entry of either name with the new AutoDetectedInputsFileError, an input error pointing to --inputs; they used to follow a link the method's tree keeps out, such as one its .gitignore ignores, so a method you checked out could point its inputs at data outside its folder. An inputs file named with --inputs is read as given, a link followed.
  • A jwt caller's read_scope is bound to its own id (Breaking): on a deployment with AUTH_MODE=jwt, every route taking a read_scope (the run routes, /v1/validate, /v1/resolve, /v1/codegen, /v1/pipe-io and POST /v1/blobs/missing) refuses a scope that does not lie under the caller's token user_id with a 403 ReadScopeForbidden, so a caller holding its own token can no longer read another caller's blobs or run under another's scope. With AUTH_MODE=none or api_key, the caller is a trusted host or a single tenant, and the scope is taken as before.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• crate_fingerprint on the run answers: the API server's POST /v1/start acknowledgement and POST /v1/execute result, PipelexRunResultStart and PipelexRunResultExecute, carry the fingerprint of the library crate the run's method was loaded into, so a host records it on its run beside the digest of the method tree that ran; it is null for a run built from no crate.
  • StorageProviderAbstract.store_if_absent: a storage provider creates an object only when its key holds none and answers whether it did, never replacing an object already there, and checks the bytes against checksum_sha256_hex before writing, raising the new StorageChecksumMismatchError on a mismatch. S3 makes the condition with If-None-Match: *, sends the SHA-256 as x-amz-checksum-sha256 for S3 to check, and retries a 409 ConditionalRequestConflict a bounded number of times, GCS uploads on generation 0, and the local provider hard-links a temporary file to the key; a provider that does not override _store_if_absent, such as an external storage plugin, looks the key up and then stores.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The API server's blob store writes create-only (Breaking): every blob and tree listing the server writes is created only when its key is free, with its SHA-256 as its checksum, so a bucket refusing unconditional writes under blobs/ and trees/ refuses none of them. A blob held at another size than the bytes uploaded under its hash is no longer written over: the upload is a 500 BlobStoreCorrupted that leaves the object for the deployment's operator to remove, and the local storage's folder must sit on a filesystem that supports hard links.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • POST /v1/validate without a read_scope stores nothing: a validation of a files map records its tree in the blob store only under the read_scope its request carries, where it used to record the tree's blobs and listing under the caller's own id, a prefix no host lists or erases; hash entries still resolve in the caller's own scope.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text: A method is now its whole folder, its method tree, and every file of it travels with it. Pipelex lists each method as the MTHDS standard's method tree, so its templates, images, stylesheets, fonts, Python and requirements.txt reach its steps wherever it runs: locally, on the API server through the files map and the blob routes, or fetched by method_ref, and every run records the digest of the tree it read. A PipeFunc now names its function by import path, a method's requirements.txt is checked before any of its Python runs, and a relative URL in an HTML template names a file of the method.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• [interpreter.method_tree_limits]: the limits every method tree is listed under on this machine, max_files (10,000) and max_total_bytes (1 GiB) by default with max_file_bytes unset, so a folder handed over by mistake is refused before any file is hashed, with the advice to run the method's own folder or to raise the limits; these are not the hosted API's limits, which a deployment sets.
  • A run records its method tree: pipelex run bundle prints the digest of the method tree it read with its recap and writes method_tree.json (the digest, the tree's root, its entry and each file's path, hash and size) in its output folder, pipelex-agent run bundle adds method_tree_digest to its output file and to its --with-memory output, and every run's RunMetadata carries method_tree_digest, the digest of the tree its pipe belongs to, which changes with any byte of the method, beside crate_fingerprint, which changes only with the meaning of its concepts and pipes.
  • MethodTreeLoadError, MethodEntryError and HostLibraryTreeError: the error_type of a method tree that cannot be listed (a symbolic link, a tree past its limits), of a method folder with no single pipe to start at, and of a server's own library directory whose tree cannot be listed beside the bundles a caller submitted, a configuration fault whose message, naming the server's paths, never reaches the caller.
  • PluginRegistrar.add_pipe_func_package_offer: the plugin providing an out-of-process PipeFunc execution mode states, keyed by the same mode, the Python packages and the marker environment its sandbox offers (PipeFuncPackageOffer), which a method's requirements.txt is checked against; a mode stating none refuses every method declaring requirements with PipeFuncPackageSetUnstatedError, a configuration fault. MethodRequirementsFileError, MethodRequirementsNotMetError, HostLibraryRequirementsError, PipeFuncPackageSetUnstatedError and DuplicatePipeFuncPackageOfferError are new error_types.
  • pipelex fix function-names and pipelex-agent fix function-names: rewrite every flat PipeFunc function_name of a method folder as the function's import path and drop the argument of every @pipe_func(name=...) marker, reading the files as syntax trees without importing them or booting Pipelex, and keeping every comment and alignment; a flat name no module of the method's tree registers, or that two register, is left as it is and reported with the markers registering it, which keep their argument, and so is a marker whose name is not a string literal, the agent command's is_complete being false and both commands exiting 1, with --dry-run to preview.
  • pipe_func_function_refused and the method-tree Python errors: a PipeFunc whose function cannot be found or proven is refused at validation with the pipe_func_function_refused validation error type, located on the step's function_name, and the new PipeFuncFunctionError, TreePythonError, TreePythonHeldError, TreeModuleShadowingError and FunctionNamesMigrationError name the failures of a function, of a tree's Python and of the migration.
  • The method file store: a step reads a file of its method where reading is allowed, at the moment it uses it, through MethodFileStoreProtocol, whose read_tree_listing(tree_digest=..., read_scope=...) and read_blob(sha256=..., read_scope=...) return a tree's listing and a file's bytes under the run's read scope, each read checked against the tree's digest (pipelex.core.method_trees.method_files). The local store, LOCAL_METHOD_FILES, serves the trees this process's libraries hold, and a plugin whose activities run apart from the process that loaded the method claims HubSlot.METHOD_FILE_STORE with PluginRegistrar.claim_method_file_store; a file the store does not hold for the run fails its step with the new MethodFileUnavailableError. An orchestrator running a job out of process copies every tree the job's crate names into the store its workers read before its execute or start returns, since the runner may drop the files as soon as it does, and read_stored_trees(tree_digests=..., read_scope=...) reads them for that copy, each as a store keeps it, its listing under its digest and its files under their hashes. The local store finds a file by its hash in one lookup and reads a file on disk off the event loop.
  • Relative URLs in HTML templates read the method's own files: a relative URL in a PipeDocGen HTML template, inline or a template file, such as an image's src, a stylesheet's href, a font, or a url() inside a stylesheet the template links, names a file of the template's method tree, resolved by the MTHDS standard's rules against the template file, or against the bundle file of an inline template, and read through the method file store under the run's read scope wherever the document prints, so a logo, a stylesheet and a font travel with their method. Only images, stylesheets and fonts are read, by suffix, so a URL a run's input supplies cannot make a document carry the method's other files. A URL the template writes as it is is checked when the method loads, and a URL built from the inputs that climbs above the tree's root, names a folder, a missing file, a file the tree's membership rule keeps out or a file that is no asset fails the print with the new TemplateUrlRefusedError, an input error naming the URL and the template; a URL with a scheme, such as https://, data: or pipelex-storage://, is read as before.
  • RenderJob.base_url and the method-file arm of RenderResources.load: an HTML job whose template belongs to a method tree carries the URL a document engine joins the document's relative URLs to, under METHOD_FILE_URL_PREFIX (https://method-files.pipelex.invalid/, which never resolves), and RenderResources.load reads a URL joined under it, a stylesheet's own URLs included, from the document's method tree, with no media type; DocumentComposition.url_base carries the template's place in its tree to the print stage. They join plugin API version 7, and an engine that never reads base_url keeps refusing a relative URL.
  • StorageProviderAbstract.load_size: a storage provider reads an object's size without its bytes, from a file's metadata, an S3 HEAD or a GCS object's metadata, and a provider that does not override _load_size measures the object it loads, so an external storage plugin keeps working.
  • The API server's blob routes, POST /v1/blobs/missing and PUT /v1/blobs/{sha256}: the server keeps a blob store in its configured storage, under <scope>/blobs/<sha256>, declares it with blob_store: true on GET /v1/version, and serves the MTHDS protocol's blob routes, so a sender asks which of its method's files the runner lacks, uploads each one to the signed target the answer names, and then sends the method by hash; the scope is the request's read_scope, else the caller's id, the targets start with PUBLIC_BASE_URL when it is set, else with the URL the request arrived at, are signed with BLOB_UPLOAD_SIGNING_KEY (a key per process when unset) and expire after BLOB_UPLOAD_URL_TTL_SECONDS, and once the server has read a tree in full it records its listing under <scope>/trees/<digest>, so asking with that digest answers in one lookup for blobs of that tree. A blob counts as held only at the size the sender states, read from the storage's metadata, so bytes held short are asked for again and written over by their upload. BlobMismatch, BlobUploadNotAuthorized and BlobStoreCorrupted are new error_types.
  • files takes every entry form, beside dependencies: on /v1/execute, /v1/start and /v1/validate, each value of files is the file's text, {"base64": "…"} or {"sha256": "…", "size": n} naming bytes the blob store holds, so a method's templates and other binary files travel with it, and dependencies carries the method packages it calls by address, each a map of its own keyed by its address; /v1/validate also takes read_scope. A hash the server does not hold is a 422 MissingBlobs listing the hashes in missing_blobs, a hash it holds at another size than the entry states a 422 BlobMismatch listing each with its held size in mismatched_blobs, checked before any byte is read, and a tree over MAX_METHOD_TREE_FILES, MAX_METHOD_TREE_FILE_KIB or MAX_METHOD_TREE_TOTAL_KIB, the files resources joins to it included, or a method with more than MAX_METHOD_DEPENDENCIES dependency trees or more than MAX_METHOD_REQUEST_TOTAL_KIB across its trees, a 422 MethodTreeTooLarge.
  • method_provenance.tree_digest: a run by method_ref reports the digest of the method tree it loaded beside the commit it was read from (MethodProvenance.tree_digest).
  • Validating a method directory: validate_bundle, validate_bundles_in_process and BundleValidatorProtocol.validate_bundles take method_dir, a method's tree validated whole as the caller's, with methods_dirs holding the packages shipped with it, every .py file of the tree compiled for its syntax and refused by its tree path and line, and the graph drawn from the tree's entry pipe; write_method_tree and WRITTEN_METHOD_TREES (pipelex.libraries.written_trees) write a tree out and make every listing of its directory, while it is held, the tree as written.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Library directories load through their method trees (Breaking): a library directory's .mthds files are the bundles of its method tree and of the trees of the nested packages and repositories under it, each loaded as a method of its own, so a hidden, gitignored or virtual-environment .mthds file is no longer loaded, a symbolic link in the tree refuses the load, and [interpreter.scan] excluded_dirs now applies only to the scan for Python classes and functions; a hosted run sends the same bundles. A directory holding nothing but nested methods loads them, a nested package or repository holding no .mthds file is skipped before it is listed, and a dependency package whose tree cannot be listed is refused naming the package by its address, never the directory it was installed into.
  • -L <subdir> inside a package loads the whole package (Breaking): a library directory is listed as its method tree, which is rooted at the nearest METHODS.toml at or above it, so naming a subfolder of a package with -L, or as a library directory of a runner, loads every bundle of the package.
  • A .mthds file named alone belongs to its method tree (Breaking): a bundle file handed to run bundle, validate bundle or a runner is the member of the tree rooted at the nearest METHODS.toml at or above its folder, and with none its method is that one file, so a step naming any other file, such as a template_file, is refused with the advice to run the method's folder or to add a METHODS.toml.
  • template_file resolves in the bundle's method tree (Breaking): a PipeDocGen template_file read from disk is looked up among the files of its bundle's method tree, where a .. climbing to another folder of the tree is now allowed, and a file the tree does not hold (above its root, gitignored, hidden or in a nested package) is refused, the message naming each file by its path in the tree; a URL is refused when the bundle parses, and a bundle loaded from a string still reads only the files sent with it.
  • run bundle <folder> starts at the method's main pipe (Breaking): with no --pipe, pipelex run bundle and pipelex-agent run bundle on a folder, locally as on the hosted API, start at its METHODS.toml's main_pipe, or with no manifest at the one main_pipe its bundles declare, and refuse none or several, naming each bundle by its path in the tree; a bundle.mthds or a single .mthds file in the folder is no longer looked for. A hosted run names that pipe as domain.pipe_code, so it starts where the local run would when two domains of the method define the same code.
  • Run output folders hold a .gitignore: every folder pipelex run creates for a run's outputs holds a .gitignore ignoring everything in it, so a run started inside a method's folder leaves the method's tree, and its digest, unchanged; the folder is named after the pipe's own code even when the pipe was named as domain.pipe_code, on a hosted run too.
  • pipelex-agent run writes into an output folder (Breaking): its output file (live_run.json or dry_run.json) and its graph files go into a new numbered folder, results/<pipe_code>_output_<NN>/ beside the bundle it ran, else under mthds-wip/, holding the same .gitignore, instead of beside the bundle itself, so two runs of a method read the same tree, with the same method_tree_digest.
  • mthds and pipelex-sdk versions, MTHDS protocol 1.0.0 and standard 7.0.0 (Breaking): the pins move to mthds==0.22.0, the release that lists method trees, carries protocol 1.0.0 and implements MTHDS standard 7.0.0, and pipelex-sdk==0.45.0, the release built on it, so the runner and GET /v1/version report protocol_version 1.0.0, a crate pipelex normalizes is stamped mthds_version 7.0.0, and a METHODS.toml declaring mthds_version = "^5.0.0" now warns that the engine does not satisfy it. A dependency package fetched before is fetched again into the release's new cache layout, a package's METHODS.toml is found only at its root and manifest discovery stops at any .git entry; everyone downstream inherits those exact versions.
  • A method's requirements.txt is checked when it loads (Breaking): a method tree holding Python and a requirements.txt at its root is refused before any of its Python is imported, naming each requirement, when the environment its PipeFunc steps run in does not meet it, or when the file holds a line the MTHDS standard refuses (a URL, an option such as -r or -e, a comment after a requirement, a continued line). A package a method calls by its address is checked the same way, named by its address. Locally the environment is the interpreter Pipelex runs in and the refusal gives the uv pip install command that fixes it; on a sandbox-hosted deployment it is the package set the deployment states for its sandbox, a run is refused with a 422 and a validation by method_ref with an is_valid: false verdict located on the line, naming no path on the server. A method of a server's own library directories whose requirements are not met is the server's fault, a 500 HostLibraryRequirementsError whose message never reaches the caller. Pipelex never installs anything. A project root loaded as a library directory is such a tree, so hand over the folder holding the methods instead when the root's requirements.txt is an application's.
  • A PipeFunc names its function by import path (Breaking): function_name is the function's import path from the root of the step's method tree, such as funcs.totals.compute_totals for the function compute_totals of funcs/totals.py, and a flat name is refused as the bundle is read with the advice to run pipelex fix function-names. Validation locates the module among the tree's files and proves, without running any Python, that the function is a top-level def or async def the module defines carrying the @pipe_func() marker; the module is imported under its real name, the tree's root first on the import path, when the step first runs, where its signature and return type are checked. A bundle passed as content imports locally from the process's import path, and on a sandbox-hosted deployment from the Python submitted with it. The runner's OpenAPI document gives the PipeFunc blueprint's function_name its import path pattern and PipeValidationErrorType its pipe_func_function_refused value.
  • One method tree's Python per process (Breaking): a run holds the Python of the tree it imports from until its library is torn down, and a step of another tree that would load its Python meanwhile is refused with TreePythonHeldError naming both trees by a bundle each holds and the start of its digest, never by a path of the host, so a run whose own steps and a dependency package's steps both call Python is refused locally; once no run holds a tree, its root leaves sys.path and the next tree evicts every module imported from a file of it, whatever imported it. A top-level module of a tree named like a standard-library module or like a module importable outside the tree is refused at validation, structures excepted, and on a sandbox-hosted deployment, whose sandbox holds its own packages, only a standard-library name is, and while a tree is held, importing a file its membership rule keeps out, such as a .gitignored module, is refused naming the rule, and no bytecode is written into the tree.
  • The function registry is retired and @pipe_func() takes no argument (Breaking): FuncRegistry, func_registry, FuncRegistryUtils, FuncRegistryError, RuntimeHub.get_func_registry and the name= argument of @pipe_func are removed, no function is discovered or imported while a library loads, and is_marked_pipe_func(func=...) tells a function carrying the marker.
  • Kernel func ops take the function (Breaking): pipelex.kernel.func_ops.call_registered_function becomes call_function(function=..., memory=...), and run_func takes the function itself in place of function_name.
  • Plugin API version 7 (Breaking): PLUGIN_API_VERSION moves to 7, so a plugin declaring targets_api = 6 is refused at discovery with PluginApiVersionMismatchError: a bundle validator's validate_bundles receives submitted_files in place of bundle_resources and takes method_dir and methods_dirs, its mthds_contents becoming optional, a PipeFunc executor's transported request names its tree by tree_digest and carries no files, the transported entrypoint takes the directory the call's files were unpacked into, an orchestrator running a job out of process copies the job's trees before it returns, and claim_method_file_store joins the registrar's menu.
  • LibraryCrate names its method trees by digest (Breaking): python_sources, bundle_resources and host_bundle_files give way to tree_bundles, which names each pipe's bundle by its tree's digest and its tree path (TreeBundleRef), so a crate carries no file's bytes, no listing and no path of the host that assembled it, a pipe built from it resolves a file its bundle names lexically and reads nothing, a Temporal workflow loading it included, and its fingerprint ignores the trees. Bundles loaded from content strings sit at the root of the tree of the files submitted with them, which the files of a library directory whose own tree holds no bundle join; two directories submitting different files at one path refuse the load with BundleResourcePathError, naming the path in the tree alone and joining none of their files, and a structure class is refused in every tree the load lists, a package or repository nested in a library directory included. A load that validates a crate builds each pipe as a member of its tree when a library of this process holds the tree under the digest the crate names, so a PipeDocGen HTML template file is checked as it was where the crate was assembled, and refuses such a step with the new PipeDocGenTemplateFileUncheckedError when no library holds its tree, rather than passing its template unchecked; a load skipping validation still reads no file. LibraryCrate.concepts_only() gives the crate's concepts and domains without its pipes.
  • A PipeFunc call names its method tree (Breaking): PipeFuncExecutionRequest.tree_digest names the tree of the called step, and the process running the call reads its files, every one but the .mthds files and a generated structures module, through the method file store under the run's read scope (read_pipe_func_call_files). The direct executor's transported run writes them into a temporary directory, generates structures unless the method shipped one, imports the function by its import path under the process's hold on that directory and unloads its modules before removing it; the transported entrypoint takes as a required third argument the directory a sandbox client unpacked the files into, since a sandbox reaches no method file store, and runs DirectPipeFuncExecutor.run_pipe_func_transported_at on it. Only the called step is built in the tree written for the call, which holds none of the tree's bundles: load_from_crate and rehydrate_library_and_memory take written_pipe_trees, keyed by the step's pipe ref, and every other step, a PipeDocGen of the same tree included, is built as the crate names it, its template file named by the crate's digest. The transported library's id is public, TRANSPORTED_LIBRARY_ID.
  • A PipeDocGen template file is read where the document prints (Breaking): DocumentComposition.template_file, a ComposedTemplateFile naming the file by its tree's digest and tree path (MethodFileRef), replaces template_path and template_resource, and the print stage reads it through the method file store under the run's read scope, renders an .html one with the step's data, carried as a TemplateRenderContext (the stuffs the step's inputs name, the concepts and domains of the run's crate with none of its pipes, the crate's fingerprint, and the run's runtime parameters), through the template file stage the interpreter installs at boot, a dry print included, in the run's own library where this process holds it and otherwise in a library loaded from the concepts, which the process keeps for later prints (RenderLibraryCache), and hands an office one's bytes to its engine, whose template check moves from the step's dry run into the dry print. An .html template file whose bytes changed after its tree was listed is refused at load, never read from the disk unchecked. make_render_job is synchronous again and takes the rendered html or the template's bytes; an inline template is still rendered where the step runs.
  • Files submitted with content strings make one method tree (Breaking): PipelexMTHDSProtocol, validate_bundle, validate_bundles_in_process, acquire_library, pipeline_run_setup, resolve_crate_from_contents and BundleValidatorProtocol.validate_bundles take submitted_files, a mapping from the path a step names to the file's bytes, in place of bundle_resources, and LibraryManagerAbstract.add_submitted_files replaces add_bundle_resources. The run names their tree by its digest and carries none of the files, so nothing is stored under the run's assets/bundle/ before it leaves the process, the 512 KiB bound on .html template files is lifted, and files that cannot make one tree, such as two paths equal once case-folded, raise BundleResourcePathError. A step names a submitted file by any spelling of its path, so templates//invoice.docx reads the file submitted as templates/invoice.docx.
  • A relative URL in an HTML template names a file of the method (Breaking): a literal relative URL of an HTML template, or of a stylesheet it links, that names no image, stylesheet or font of the method's tree now fails the method's load, pipelex validate and dry runs included, where it loaded and failed only at print. A relative path such as images/logo.png that an engine printing HTML hands RenderResources.load as written now resolves in the template's method tree, and is refused with TemplateUrlRefusedError when the template belongs to none, where an unscoped run read it from its working directory; a root-absolute local path, and every URL of a document printed from the auto-layout or an office template, read as before.
  • A method sent to the API server is a method tree (Breaking): files and bundle_b64 are read as one map under the MTHDS standard's tree rule, so a key holding a dot file or directory (.mthds/ included), an empty, . or .. segment, a backslash or a colon, a key given twice, or two keys naming one file is a 422 InvalidMethodFiles carrying the standard's tree_refusal (code and names) in place of InvalidBundle, and a package the method calls travels in dependencies beside files, while a bundle_b64 archive still carries it under .mthds/methods/<name>/. The whole tree is written out and loaded as the caller's library directory, so a template beside its bundle needs no resources entry and counts against the tree's limits rather than those of resources, an image, stylesheet or font only a template's relative URL names travels with the method, a file sent in resources joins the tree with no step needing to name it, a bundle that does not parse is a 422 naming it by its tree path, and with no pipe_code the run starts at the tree's entry pipe by the protocol's rule.
  • method_ref is read from its commit and run as a tree (Breaking): a package fetched by address is read from the git objects of the commit it resolved to, never from the clone's working tree, and runs or validates as a tree sent in files does, its template files and Python included, the packages it ships under .mthds/methods/<name>/ becoming dependency trees that /v1/validate now loads too; its entry pipe is its manifest's main_pipe, so a manifest declaring none answers default_pipe_ref: null.
  • /v1/validate validates a method tree whole (Breaking): a method sent as files or fetched by method_ref is validated as it would run, every .py file of it compiled for its syntax, a file that does not parse or is not UTF-8 making the verdict is_valid: false with an item at its tree path and line, and its default_pipe_ref and graph follow the tree's entry pipe, both null for a tree with none; mthds_sources accompanies mthds_contents alone.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The local storage provider publishes a write whole: LocalStorageProvider writes to a temporary file beside the key, flushes it, then renames it onto the key, so a full disk or a killed process never leaves a file cut short under a key, and two writers of one key each land whole.
  • A bundle file that is not UTF-8 text is a located diagnostic: a .mthds file read from disk that does not decode is a parser error naming its source and the line and column of its first undecodable byte, so a method tree sent to the API server holding one is the caller's 422 on a run and an invalid verdict on /v1/validate, never a server error.
  • Python a method tree holds that cannot parse is its diagnostic on every interpreter: a .py file holding a NUL byte, which Python 3.11 refuses with a ValueError where later versions raise a SyntaxError, or one nested too deeply to parse, is an invalid verdict located at its tree path, and a PipeFunc whose module is such a file is refused as one that does not parse.
  • A template_file no sent file could be keyed by is a blueprint item at its step: a bundle loaded from content strings, as the API's routes and validate_bundle load one, whose PipeDocGen step's template_file holds a .. segment or a NUL character, or names no file, is refused when it parses, whatever files the request sends, as one blueprint_validation item with field_path pipe.<code> whose message names the field and not the path, instead of a load refusal saying the file was not supplied. A bundle read from disk still resolves a .. in its method tree.
  • A method_ref package's template files reach its steps: a PipeDocGen step of a package run or validated by method_ref reads the template file the package holds beside its bundle, where the run before had no way to read it.
  • A request's own method that does not load is the caller's 422: a method sent to the API server whose bundle does not parse, or whose tree cannot load, is refused as the caller's fault, naming each file by its tree path, instead of a 500 naming the server's temporary directory.
  • A TOML syntax error names the bundle's source: a bundle read from a file under a source the caller gives names that source in its TOML syntax error, never the file's path on the host.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • Bundle resources and their dispatch (Breaking): BundleResource, BundleResources, make_bundle_resources, BundleResourceReadStage, MAX_LOAD_STAGE_RESOURCES_BYTES, prepare_job_for_remote_dispatch, relocate_run_resources and does_pipe_run_leave_process are removed, InterpreterHub.set_pipe_run takes the pipe run alone, and BundleResourceError and BundleResourcesTooLargeError are no longer error_types: no template file rides in a run's payloads, so none is bounded by them, and a method file a run cannot read raises MethodFileUnavailableError.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • A scoped event log captures usage events: a usage event emitted while runtime_hub.scoped_event_log is set now goes into the scoped event log and nowhere else, ahead of an event log registered with ReportingManager.set_event_log and of the per-process runner fallback, including inside an isolated sub-execution such as a Temporal activity, where it always went to the fallback. Code running a leaf inside an activity can therefore scope a fresh InMemoryEventLog around it and return the leaf's usage events with its result, which is how a backend with no shared tracing store, such as Mistral Workflows, collects a run's usage; with no scoped event log set, usage events are routed as before.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text: A run's trace now records each decision as it is made and names every pipe by its place in the method. A condition's chosen outcome and a batch's width are written before anything runs under them, and every trace event carries its invocation path, its mode and the attempt of the execution that wrote it, so a graph built from a run's events names each pipe the same way in every run, live or dry, and shows a retried step once.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• condition_resolved and batch_fanned_out trace events: a live PipeCondition writes condition_resolved the moment its choice is final, before anything runs under it, with the rendered_value its expression rendered and the selected_outcome key of the outcome map it matched, null when it took the default outcome, and a chosen pipe whose inputs are missing fails the condition with no outcome recorded; both graph builders derive from that event and the start of the chosen pipe the selected_outcome edge from the condition, labelled with that key, which no run drew before, whichever workflow the chosen pipe started in. A PipeBatch writes batch_fanned_out once it knows its width, before any item starts, with item_count, branch_pipe_code, the bare code of the pipe each item runs, branch_pipe_ref, its qualified reference, and branch_pipe_type. A dry run resolves no condition, so it writes no condition_resolved, and both graph builders build the same graph from a run's events.
  • step_count and branch_count on pipe_start: a PipeSequence's start event states the number of steps its author wrote, the binding of a dotted batch_over not among them, and a PipeParallel's the number of its branches; both are null on every other pipe.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Every trace event states its mode (Breaking): each trace event carries mode, live or dry, the mode the run's pipes run in, which the run's TraceContext carries as the new run_mode, so a usage event an activity writes states it too, and a live run a keyless boot (needs_inference=False) forces dry states dry on its trace context, its events and its graph, and, like every dry run, opens no OpenTelemetry trace; an event stored without mode by an earlier version is refused with EventLogSchemaMismatchError rather than read as live, and a consumer that builds trace events passes it. Callers follow new signatures: TraceContext.run_mode is required, with no default, and so is run_mode on GraphTracerManager.open_tracer and on the tracers' setup (GraphTracerProtocol, GraphTracer and GraphTracerNoOp), where it replaces mode: GraphSpecMode, so a workflow opening a tracer of its own for part of a run passes the run_mode of the context it received, and PipelexKernel.make refuses, with TraceContextRunModeError, a trace_context stating another mode than the one its run takes, which the new runtime_hub.resolve_effective_run_mode gives, dry on a keyless boot. GraphSpecAssembler.assemble no longer takes mode and raises the new TraceEventModeError on a set of events that mixes modes or holds none, and assemble_tracing and assemble_tracing_on_output no longer take run_mode: the graph states the mode its events state, so a dry run assembled from its events in a durable workflow gets a dry graph where it got a live one, and assemble_tracing reports a TraceEventModeError as the run's graph_assembly_error.
  • Controllers register their execution data as they decide (Breaking): a PipeSequence registers step_count as it starts, now the number of steps its author wrote; a PipeParallel registers its branch_count, add_each_output and combined_output_concept before its branches run, a PipeBatch its item_count and branch_pipe_code before its items run, and a live PipeCondition its evaluated_expression and selected_outcome once its choice is final, before the chosen pipe runs, where each used to register them once it had finished. GraphTracerProtocol adds register_batch_fan_out and register_condition_resolution, and add_selected_outcome_edge takes selected_outcome: str | None in place of outcome_value.
  • Trace events and graph nodes name their invocation (Breaking): every trace event carries path, the invocation path the hosted progress contract defines, which names a run of a pipe the same way in every run of the method, live or dry, on every engine: the entry pipe's pipe_ref, then one segment per controller level, step_<n> as the author numbered the steps, binding steps included, branch_<n>, item_<n> counting the items from 1, and outcome_<key> or default for a condition's outcome group, the outcomes that run one pipe as the library resolves it, however they spell it, named by the first key that runs it, percent-encoded, so filings.review_filings/step_3/item_2/step_1, and a dry run runs each group's pipe once; a binding step's events carry null. Every NodeSpec carries the same path, pipe_start carries pipe_ref, pipe_end_success, pipe_end_error and pipe_end_skipped carry pipe_code, pipe_ref and pipe_type, and a failed node's ErrorSpec carries caller_facing, true when its message was written for the caller, or the error's text with caller_facing false when the error's report cannot be built, a fault the tracer logs while the run still fails with the pipe's own error. A controller hands each pipe its place through JobMetadata.for_child_at; since tracing never fails a run, a pipe started without one is traced with a null path and the tracer logs the fault, the new InvocationPathError, as an error, while an inactive tracer and the no-op tracer derive no path; GraphTracerManager.on_pipe_start and the tracers' on_pipe_start require pipe_ref, on_pipe_end_error takes caller_facing, and TraceContext.copy_for_child requires invocation_path. An event stored without these fields by an earlier version is refused with EventLogSchemaMismatchError, and a consumer that builds trace events passes them.
  • Trace events name the attempt of the execution that wrote them (Breaking): every trace event carries attempt, the attempt of its execution counting from 1, and lineage, the {execution, attempt} entries it was dispatched under, empty for the run's own execution, beside workflow_id, which names the execution, direct in direct mode. GraphTracerManager.open_tracer takes attempt and received_context, the trace context a dispatched workflow received, which it continues: its parent node, its path and, when it names the workflow's place as a batch item's does, its chain as the workflow's lineage; workflow_id must be the id the engine keeps across attempts, and TraceContext carries the new parent_path, child_segment and chain, the last required with no default, so a host building a context of its own states it, make_direct_chain() in a single process. Node and edge ids name the chain that minted them, <graph_id>:<workflow_id>:attempt_<n>:node_<k>, followed after the attempt by a digest of the lineage for a dispatched workflow, so two attempts of one workflow never mint the same id; direct mode keeps <graph_id>:node_<k>. ReportingManager.set_event_log no longer takes workflow_id: a usage event takes its execution, attempt and lineage from the chain of its trace context, on the registered path as on the runner fallback. A trace event is frozen, and one whose workflow_id is empty is refused with EventLogSchemaMismatchError. The event logs keep every attempt's events, and every one of them, the DynamoDB and buffering logs included, returns a run's events deduplicated on the event's chain, writer, kind and sequence and ordered by chain, sequence and writer; the DynamoDB log's sort key becomes EVENT#<chain digest>#<writer_id>#<sequence>, the chain digest being the SHA-256 of the chain key, so the key stays within DynamoDB's limit however deep the lineage, and the NDJSON log writes one file per attempt of each execution, wf_<workflow_id>__c_<chain digest>.ndjson, __w_<writer_id> added for a writer other than primary. GraphSpecAssembler builds the graph, and dates it, from current events only: a higher attempt of an execution supersedes the earlier one and everything it dispatched, so a retried invocation appears once at its path, a lost attempt leaves no failed node, and a superseded attempt's usage counts in the run's total as unattributed usage.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Trace events written to DynamoDB expire (Breaking): the DynamoDB event log now writes every event with a ttl in epoch seconds, its write time plus the new runtime.tracing.dynamodb.retention_days (30 by default, at least 1), so a table that expires items on ttl deletes a run's events, full output data included, where it used to keep them forever. Only events written from this version on carry a ttl, so the rows an earlier version wrote stay until they are deleted or given a ttl by hand. DynamoDBEventLog takes retention_days and now takes all its arguments by keyword; make_event_log reads the setting from the configuration.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A PipeDocGen document's name is one the hosted API serves: a rendered filename holding a letter outside ASCII or a dot, such as Zoë Ångström — Q3.2026, was stored under a pipelex-storage:// URI the hosted API refuses to serve, so the completed document could never be downloaded. The name is now spelled in ASCII where it can be, accents dropped and letters such as ø, æ, ł, ß, đ, þ, œ and ı transliterated, every other character, an inner dot included, becomes a hyphen, repeated separators collapse, and a name that leaves nothing, one written wholly in Greek, Cyrillic, Han or Arabic for one, falls back to the pipe's code, so that name is Zoe-Angstrom-Q3-2026.pdf, on a local run as on a hosted one.
  • The files a run stores from what it was sent are named and typed for their readers: the copy of a .docx, .xlsx or .pptx template file a run stores under assets/bundle/ before it is dispatched now carries its Office Open XML content type, named in code, where a host whose mimetypes table did not know the extension stored it as binary/octet-stream, and its name follows the rule a document's name follows, so Modèle trimestriel.v2.docx is stored as Modele-trimestriel-v2.docx. A local file input stored under assets/ that its bytes and type do not identify keeps its own suffix only when it is plainly letters and digits, and is stored as .bin otherwise.
  • The refusals of the files sent with a bundle say a retry cannot succeed: BundleResourceNotNamedError, BundleResourcesTooLargeError and BundleResourcePathError now carry retryable: false in their error report, and so in the API server's problem document, as InvalidResourcePath already did. A PipelexError subclass declares it with the new class attribute retryable, which its report carries and the generated error reference shows; a wrapper raised from such an error inherits it, as it does error_domain.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text: A method that prints with a template file now runs wherever it is sent. A PipeDocGen step's .xlsx, .docx, .pptx or .html template file travels with its bundle, as resources on the API server's routes, inside a bundle_b64 or files bundle, or as bundle_resources in Python, so a caller with no local pipelex can validate, dry-run and run it, and a bundle loaded from content strings never reads the runtime's own disk.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• resources on the API server's routes: POST /v1/validate, /v1/execute, /v1/start, /v1/pipe-io, /v1/resolve and /v1/codegen take the files a bundle sent as content reads, such as a PipeDocGen step's template_file, as a map from the path the step names to the file's bytes in standard base64, so a caller with no local pipelex can validate, dry-run and run a method that prints with an .xlsx, .docx, .pptx or .html template file. A key that cannot name a file inside the bundle answers 422 InvalidResourcePath, a file no step names 422 BundleResourceNotNamedError, a value that is not base64 400 InvalidBase64, and a request over MAX_RESOURCES_PER_REQUEST, MAX_RESOURCE_FILE_KIB or MAX_RESOURCES_TOTAL_KIB (32 files, 5 MiB each and 10 MiB in all by default) 413 PayloadTooLarge; resources beside a method_ref is a 422. A method bundle sent as bundle_b64 or files may ship such a file instead, beside the .mthds file whose step names it, and it reaches the step the same way, under the same limits; two different files under one path, shipped twice or shipped and sent, answer 422 InvalidResourcePath, as two spellings of one key do before any value is decoded. On an orchestrator other than direct, such as Temporal, a run stores each office template file under its storage_scope at assets/bundle/ before it is dispatched, so the job carries a pipelex-storage:// reference rather than the bytes, while the .html template files, which travel inline with the method, may total 512 KiB at most, a fixed bound refused with 413 BundleResourcesTooLargeError once the bundle is parsed.
  • Template files sent with a bundle loaded from content strings: PipelexMTHDSProtocol, validate_bundle, validate_bundles_in_process, acquire_library, pipeline_run_setup and resolve_crate_from_contents take bundle_resources, built with make_bundle_resources from the bytes of each file keyed by the path its step names. The library holds them and its LibraryCrate carries them, outside its fingerprint, so a PipeDocGen step finds its template file wherever the bundle is loaded: an .html one is checked against the inputs at load, the engine's template check runs on an office one at validation and in the dry run, and the print stage reads it, from the run's storage when the crate carries a reference. Before a run, live or dry, leaves the process, prepare_job_for_remote_dispatch stores its office template files under the run's storage scope; PipelexMTHDSProtocol.execute calls it when the hub's pipe run is a boot orchestrator's, and a dry run's template check reads a stored file under the run's read scope, as the print stage does. A step of a bundle the runtime read from its own disk, such as the host's library, still reads only beside it, so a file sent under the same path never stands in for its template. A file no step names raises BundleResourceNotNamedError, a path outside the bundle BundleResourcePathError, and .html template files totalling more than MAX_LOAD_STAGE_RESOURCES_BYTES (512 KiB), which travel inline with the method wherever it runs, BundleResourcesTooLargeError.
  • Template-check warnings in the validation verdict: a warning the engine's template check finds in a PipeDocGen step's office template file, such as an Excel defined name or a PowerPoint shape name that matches no input field, now rides the verdict's advisory warnings on pipelex validate, pipelex-agent validate and the API server's POST /v1/validate, where it was only logged. It is a dry_run item with the new error_type template_check_warning, the step's pipe_code and domain_code, and two new optional locators of ValidationErrorItem, template_file and template_location, the latter unset when the engine names no place, which the server's OpenAPI schema publishes, a step of the server's own library directories naming no file of theirs; an error finding still fails the validation, validate pipe <code> on both CLIs carries these warnings alone, and a dry run that returns no verdict, such as pipelex run --dry-run, pipelex fix bundle or pipelex build inputs, still logs them.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
