• BundleValidatorProtocol.validate_bundles takes bundle_resources (Breaking): a bundle validator registered for an orchestration mode receives the files sent with the contents, or None, and hands them to the validation it runs, so a remote validator implements the parameter and carries the files to its worker.
  • InterpreterHub.set_pipe_run takes leaves_process (Breaking): whoever sets the hub's pipe run says whether it hands each job to an orchestrator outside the process, as a boot orchestrator's does, which does_pipe_run_leave_process reads back so a run's submitted files are stored before it leaves.
  • DocumentComposition.make_render_job is asynchronous (Breaking): it takes the run's storage_provider, since a composition's template file may be a BundleResource read back from storage, and a TEMPLATE_FILE composition carries either template_path or template_resource. A stored template file's URI is among the composition's referenced_uris(), so the run's read scope authorizes it before the print stage reads it.
  • A PipeDocGen step's template_file must be a path inside its bundle (Breaking): an empty or absolute path, a Windows root, a drive, a UNC share, a .. segment, a backslash or a colon is refused when the blueprint validates, by the rule the files sent with a bundle are keyed by, so every template file a step names can be sent with its bundle; an absolute path naming a file inside the bundle's directory, a path such as templates/../invoice.docx and a file name holding a colon used to load. The refusal does not repeat the path, so a host library's step can no longer put the host's own path into a caller's verdict through its template file. Beside a server's own library directories, the verdict also withholds the template files their steps name, as their bundle files already were, both when such a step is refused while they load and when the engine's template check refuses its template in the dry run of a caller's pipe that runs it; a template file the caller's own content names is kept.
  • A string-loaded PipeDocGen step without its template file says it was not supplied: the load refusal now names the path the file is expected under and says to send it with the bundle, where it used to say the bundle was not loaded from a file on disk.
  • build_advisory_warnings and collect_advisory_warnings take the sweep's dry_run_result (Breaking): the composition point of the advisory warnings reads what the dry runs found from the per-pipe status map, so a caller passes the map its validation sweep returned. DryRunOutput carries those findings in its new warnings when the sweep is asked to collect them with the new collect_dry_run_warnings of validate_bundle, BundleValidator.validate_pipes and BundleValidator.validate_current_library; a sweep that is not asked leaves them to the log, as before.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Contents named by bundle_uris read their template files beside their file: a bundle passed as mthds_contents with the path of the file it was read from in bundle_uris, to PipelexMTHDSProtocol, acquire_library or pipeline_run_setup, and not already loaded from the library directories, now loads as read from that file, so a PipeDocGen step's template_file is found beside it, where it was refused as if the bundle had no directory, and an address-based reference is looked for in a .mthds/methods/ directory above it.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • A bundle loaded from content strings never reads the runtime's disk: a PipeDocGen step of such a bundle read its template_file beside whatever its source named, so a caller's mthds_sources on /v1/validate, a files[].source on /v1/resolve, /v1/codegen or /v1/pipe-io, or a source key written on the step in the bundle's text could make the runner read a file from its own disk, and an address-based reference searched .mthds/methods/ directories above that label too. Both now start only from a bundle file the runtime read itself, which the parser records as PipelexBundleBlueprint.host_bundle_file and the crate carries as LibraryCrate.host_bundle_files, outside its fingerprint and its normalized form; a content-string bundle reads only the files sent with it, and a step's source is overwritten whenever the pipe is built.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text: pipelex now reports anonymous usage statistics, on by default. Commands, runs, validations and code generations are counted with closed-list properties only, never a method, a prompt, an input or an output, and DO_NOT_TRACK, PIPELEX_USAGE_STATS=0, pipelex usage-stats disable or [usage_stats] enabled = false in a project turn them off.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Anonymous usage statistics: pipelex now reports anonymous counts of its use to Pipelex, on by default: a command_completed per command of the pipelex and pipelex-agent CLIs, a run_completed per run however it ended, with a model_used per model when the run's usage events were read, a method_validated per validation and a code_generated per code generation, whatever started them. Every property is a count, a boolean or a value from a closed list: no method, pipe code, concept name, prompt, input, output, file name, error message or argument is ever sent, and a model outside the backend tables pipelex ships is sent as other. The first command with statistics on prints a notice on stderr, once per machine, except where stderr is a machine contract (pipelex-agent with JSON errors), and pipelex init shows the same text on stderr whenever statistics are on, once per run. Statistics stay off under DO_NOT_TRACK, PIPELEX_USAGE_STATS=0, pipelex usage-stats disable, the mthds CLI's former DISABLE_TELEMETRY opt-out, [usage_stats] enabled = false in a project's .pipelex/pipelex.toml or in the packaged configuration, a ~/.mthds/usage-stats/ pipelex cannot look into, and the pytest integration mode; the usage statistics page lists what is collected. A dedicated client sends them to PostHog's EU region, from a detached sender after a CLI command and from a daemon thread in a Python program or the API server; telemetry.toml and the telemetry you configure are untouched.
  • pipelex usage-stats: status (with --format json), disable, enable and reset-id show and change the statistics of every Pipelex tool on the machine, through the state they share in ~/.mthds/usage-stats/. PIPELEX_USAGE_STATS_DEBUG prints each event to stderr as a JSON line instead of sending it, and PIPELEX_USAGE_STATS_ENDPOINT sends to a loopback origin for tests. Each queued file names the endpoint its events were queued for, and a sender posts the files naming its own origin and those naming none, so events queued under the variable never reach PostHog.
  • [usage_stats] enabled: a new pipelex.toml section, true in the packaged configuration. Set to false in a project's .pipelex/pipelex.toml it turns statistics off for everyone working in the project; it is read from the project's own file, never from ~/.pipelex/, and a file that cannot be read turns them off too.
  • Token usage names the backend that served the call: LLMTokensUsage, ImgGenTokensUsage, ExtractTokensUsage, SearchTokensUsage and JudgmentTokensUsage gain backend_name, set by the job from the backend whose worker ran it, so a run's usage events credit each call to its own backend even when two backends call the model by the same id, as after a fallback. A synthetic report no backend made, a dry run's, leaves it None.
  • @default-judgment-vision: the judgment deck names a second alias, for a judgment model that reads images, beside @default-judgment, which stays TypeSafe's text-only jev-1.13.0. It points at OpenAI's gpt-6-luna, which judges through OpenAI's Decisions API; no inference backend of Pipelex calls that API yet, so on your own keys a PipeJudge naming the alias finds no model when it runs. Run pipelex update to bring the alias into an installed deck.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • ConceptLibraryAbstract.list_own_concepts (Breaking): the concept library declares the concepts a loaded method declares itself, without the natives and the concepts of its dependency packages, so a custom implementation of ConceptLibraryAbstract implements it.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • A {% filter %} block prints its result as a {{ }} tag does: a filter block whose filter returns something other than text, such as {% filter markdown %}…{% endfilter %} in a document template or {% filter length %}, now prints its result as a {{ }} tag prints a value, through the environment's finalize and then as text, where it used to fail the render with a type error naming a Python type. A block whose filter returns text prints as before, and the printed result is charged to the render's budget like any printed value.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • uv.lock refreshed past the open Dependabot alerts: the lock the pipelex/pipelex-api Docker image installs from now holds patched releases of anyio, datamodel-code-generator, multidict, oauthlib and urllib3, and a development checkout also gets patched docling, transformers, torch, accelerate, fsspec and setuptools through the docling extra and a patched Werkzeug through the dev extra. No pyproject.toml range moved, so an application installing the pipelex wheel picks these releases up through its own resolution.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • LLMCompletionTruncatedError and LLMCompletionRefusedError: two subclasses of LLMCompletionError, the first for a text completion cut at its output limit or its context window, the second for one the model declined to write or a safety filter stopped. Both are content errors in the input domain, not retryable, answered with HTTP 422 and caller-facing under STRICT disclosure, and carry model_handle, pipe_code and the provider's stop_reason, a truncation also carrying the limit it hit as truncation_limit, max_tokens or context_window, the output_tokens used and the max_tokens sent; the message names the model, the pipe and those values, never the partial text. Each ends with a change_input next step fitted to what stopped the text: revise the prompt or the input after a refusal, raise the pipe's max_tokens or shorten its input at the output limit, set the pipe's max_tokens up to the model's limit when the request sent none, and shorten the input, lower the reasoning effort or choose a model with a larger window, never a higher max_tokens, at the context window.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The Bedrock client's chat returns a BedrockChatResult (Breaking): BedrockClientProtocol.chat returns a named result holding the text, the token usage and Converse's stopReason, in place of a (text, usage) tuple, so a custom Bedrock client returns read_converse_response(response=…) or builds the result itself.
  • A lowered Anthropic structured-output limit is said: when a structured generation on an Anthropic model lowers max_tokens to fit its structured-output timeout, the call logs it, at warning level when the pipe set the limit and at debug level when it is the model's default, and an error the lowered limit can explain, a structured output that failed validation or came back incomplete, or a timeout, ends with a sentence saying the limit was lowered and to what, never a rate limit, an authentication failure, an overload, a server error or a lost connection.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • A truncated, refused or filtered text no longer passes for a result (Breaking): every LLM worker, OpenAI chat completions whether direct or behind a gateway such as Portkey or OpenRouter, the OpenAI Responses API, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock and Mistral, now reads its response's stop value before it returns a text, so a text that stopped short fails its pipe with LLMCompletionTruncatedError or LLMCompletionRefusedError where it used to come back as a successful output, empty or partial, its billed usage still reported and recorded on its span. Each provider's vocabulary is read, including a gateway's pass-through of another provider's value such as max_tokens or content_filtered, an unknown value being logged at warning level and taken as normal, except that an incomplete Responses API answer is a truncation whatever its reason; a Gemini prompt blocked before any candidate is a refusal, and structured generation keeps its configured re-asks. A Bedrock answer is read for every text block it holds, so one holding none fails with an LLMCompletionError where it used to raise an IndexError when its message was empty, or a KeyError when its first block was not text.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Rating carries the label of its level: the Rating native has an optional label, which the MTHDS standard's native set pinned at 5.0.0 defines as the name of the selected level when the scale declares labels, held in RatingContent.label and stated by the input-form descriptor, the I/O contracts and the generated Python and TypeScript types. A PipeJudge whose levels carry labels fills it with the label of the level it chose, while a PipeLLM whose output is Rating, or any other producer, may fill it like any optional member; either way a Rating renders in a prompt as its label when it has one and as its level otherwise, so $severity reads Workaround available for a rating carrying that label and 1 for one carrying none, and its JSON rendering carries the label only when present. Since a crate materializes the pinned definition, a crate whose methods use Rating gets a new normalized fingerprint, and types generated before this release gain the field when pipelex codegen types regenerates them.
  • A log line's advice in user_action: a log call puts what its reader should do in a user_action field, one imperative sentence, and the console sink prints it whole on a line of its own under the record, after →, in cyan, while every other sink writes it as a field like any other. Pipelex's own warnings carry their advice there, such as Run pipelex migrate to update it on a stale configuration file, so their message says only what happened.
  • A PipeJudge asks several questions in one request: a PipeJudge may set questions instead of question, a table of questions keyed by name, each holding its question and its own options, levels, criteria and threshold, checked under the single form's rules with a refusal naming the question, and the judging model answers them all in one request over the same evidence; the verdicts fill the output's structure, whose fields must be exactly the question names, each holding its question's YesNo, Choice or Rating or a concept refining it, which the load checks field by field (inadequate_output_concept). A question the model declines leaves its field holding nothing when the field may hold nothing, being neither required nor given a default_value, or, in a structure class, typed to admit None, with a warning naming it under judgment_question and its refusal in the step's execution data, and fails the step with JudgmentRefusedError naming the question otherwise, since a default would read as a verdict the model never gave. The kernel's run_multi_judgment does the same for a programmatic caller, taking the questions as AskedQuestions and the output's content class, and returning a MultiJudgmentResult with each question's outcome; a class whose fields are not the questions' names is refused with JudgmentOutputFieldsError before the model is called.
  • package_prefix chooses which console lines name their package: a setting under [runtime.log.rich_log] decides which lines the console sink starts with their logger's top-level package name, dimmed. libraries, the default, keeps the rule that names another library's package and leaves a line from pipelex or a pipelex_ package bare; all names every line's package, so pipelex:, pipelex_api: and a plugin's name tell apart which component spoke; none names none. A line logged on the root logger never carries one.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• MTHDS standard 5.0.0 (Breaking): pipelex now requires mthds==0.21.0 and pipelex-sdk==0.38.0, the releases that report MTHDS standard 5.0.0, so everyone downstream inherits those exact versions and a project that pins either package itself has to move with them. pipelex --version prints mthds-standard 5.0.0, every crate pipelex normalizes is stamped with mthds_version 5.0.0 and materializes the native set the standard pinned at 5.0.0, and a package whose METHODS.toml constrains mthds_version to ^4.0.0, ~4.0.0, 4.* or exactly 4.0.0 now logs a warning when it loads, which >=4.0.0 or ^5.0.0 does not. PipeJudge judges the evidence of its prompt with two-sided criteria and labelled levels, and asks several questions in one request, as the standard's 5.0.0 PipeJudge defines.
  • PipeJudge judges the evidence of its prompt (Breaking): prompt is now required and holds the evidence, a template rendered exactly as a PipeLLM's prompt is with its images and documents presented to the judging model as files, beside a required question: prompt is no longer a synonym of question, a pipe writing its question there is refused with a message saying where each goes, and a pipe is rewritten as prompt = "@message" beside its question. The model sees an input only as the two templates render it: every declared input must be read by the prompt or the question (extraneous_input_variable), an image or a document read by the question is refused (input_stuff_spec_mismatch), the model's file capability is checked against what the prompt reads, an absent optional input renders as its guard says, such as @?note, and a Dynamic input renders as text. criteria takes both yes and no, a one-sided or empty table being refused; a level of levels may be a { label, description } table, labels all or none and distinct, and the Rating verdict then carries the label of the level chosen; a model that declines the question fails the step with the new JudgmentRefusedError, a content error naming the pipe and the model, where no verdict is ever read off a refusal.
  • The judgment worker contract carries a rendered prompt (Breaking): JudgmentJob and JudgmentAssignment carry a JudgmentPrompt, the rendered text with its images and documents, in place of the state, images and documents keyed by input name, and JudgmentState is gone; YesNoQuestion carries one optional criteria of type YesNoCriteria with both sides in place of yes_criterion and no_criterion; RatingQuestion.levels is a list of RatingLevel, each with a label, a description or both; and JudgmentWorkerAbstract.judge returns a JudgmentOutcome per question, an answer or a JudgmentRefusal. The judgment contract a backend plugin implements, with the family's errors a worker raises, is published in the Inference SPI table, and the kernel's run_judgment takes the evidence as a UserPromptContent, build_judgment_material and material_value being gone.
  • Console lines without the emoji prefix or the path column (Breaking): a line logged under the pipelex package or a pipelex_ one, the runtime's, the API server's or a plugin's named that way, and a line logged on the root logger start with their message, and a line another library logged starts with that library's top-level package name, dimmed, such as httpx:, where every line used to start with an emoji or a bracketed logger name. The column naming the source file and line of each record is off by default; set is_show_path = true under [runtime.log.rich_log] to show it, is_link_path_enabled still making it clickable. The pipelex.tools.log.log_formatter module is gone with its EmojiLogFormatter, so code that formatted records with it uses the stdlib's logging.Formatter.
  • Log messages are one short sentence (Breaking): Pipelex's log messages, and its API server's, say what happened in one sentence that starts with a capital and ends with no period, and at INFO and above hold no identifier and no backtick in at most 80 characters, the advice they used to append now riding user_action. Warnings about one event became one: whichever kind of inference job carried no usage, the line is An inference job reported no usage with inference_job_type; a stale configuration file is A configuration file is out of date and was migrated in memory only whatever its remedy; and a PipeBatch over a large list is A PipeBatch fans out over a large list without durable execution, bounded or not, with max_concurrency absent when the fan-out is unbounded. What breaks is a log query or an alert written against an old message.
  • The API server's refusals of a caller's credentials log at DEBUG (Breaking): a request with no bearer token, an expired or invalid token or a wrong API key logs A caller's credentials were refused at DEBUG, with auth_mode and auth_refusal_reason (missing_bearer_token, expired_token, invalid_token or api_key_mismatch), since the error line the server writes at WARNING for every 401 already records the refusal. A token that verifies but whose user_id claim is missing, not a path-safe segment or the reserved single-tenant id still logs at WARNING, its user_action telling the token issuer what to fix, and an unset JWT_SECRET_KEY or API_KEY logs at ERROR with the variable's name in env_var. An alert on the old authentication warnings counts the 401 error lines instead.
  • Exceptions ride as fields at every level: a DEBUG or VERBOSE line about a handled exception, such as a Google client that could not be closed, has a fixed message and carries the exception's class and text as error.type and error.message, as the lines at INFO and above already did, rather than splicing them into its text. The retry line names the class of what the attempt raised under error.type rather than exception_type.
  • make check-log-calls holds a message's wording and its exceptions: the log-call guard also refuses, at every level, a message that starts with a lowercase letter, ends with a period or an ellipsis, holds a backtick or splices a handled exception into its text, through an f-string, a %, a .format() or a task's exception(), and, at INFO and above, a message that holds an identifier, a word with an underscore or a call such as setup(), or runs past 80 characters. The rules are lowercase-start, trailing-period, backtick, spliced-exception, identifier and length, specified on the log-call guard's page of the contributor documentation, and every call in the tree passes them with an empty baseline.
  • A refused enum value names the valid ones: a validation error for an unknown enum value, in a configuration file or anywhere else Pipelex formats pydantic's errors, now lists the values the field accepts, invalid enum value 'inptu', expected 'input', 'input_cached', …, where it used to name only the refused value.
  • A field that never holds nothing refuses null (Breaking): a structure field with a default_value is generated as X = Field(default=…) rather than X | None, and a required field naming native.Anything as NonNullAny (pipelex.core.stuffs.non_null_any), any value but None, so a value setting either to null, an input or a model's answer, is refused, and a binding step reading such a field never records an absence its static analysis ruled out. Leave the key out, or leave its CSV cell empty, to get a field's default. The codegen projections follow: a defaulted field is X = Field(default=…) in python-pydantic and python-structures and a bare .default(…) in ts-zod, typed T rather than T | null. The JSON schema of a defaulted field, the one a pipe's IO contract publishes as an input's json_schema and a model is asked to fill, drops its null arm: {"type": "string", "default": …} rather than {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": …}.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• An absent optional image or document is left out of its prompt: a PipeLLM or PipeImgGen whose prompt read an optional image or document behind its guard, such as @?photo or {% if photo %}, failed with "Could not find image 'photo' in context" when the input was not given, dry runs included. The file is now left out, taking no number and reaching no model, while an absent required file is still refused. A template reading a name aliased to a slot later resolved absent no longer fails with a KeyError either: the alias holds nothing, as its target does.
  • A Google client's close at teardown is no longer garbage-collected: when a Google LLM or image-generation worker was torn down inside a running event loop, nothing but the loop referenced the background task closing its async client, and a loop holds its tasks weakly, so the task could be collected before the client was closed, with the asyncio error Task was destroyed but it is pending!. Each close task is now held until it is done.
  • A condition whose outcome may be skipped declares it: a PipeCondition routing to an outcome pipe that takes plainly an input the condition declares optional must declare its own output optional, and is refused with optional_not_handled otherwise, since a run without that input skips the outcome and resolves the condition's output absent; an outcome the condition's expression chooses only with that input present declares it forced (!) instead, since validation does not read the expression. Every name such an outcome always stores in its caller's memory counts as maybe-absent too, so a sequence binding one into a plain output is refused where it used to validate and then resolve absent; the outcome is listed in liftable_pipes under its condition, and a ! input on an outcome counts in the optional_force_redundant lint.
  • A sequence step that may be skipped keeps what its run may store: a step an absent input may lift, whose pipe stores a name on some runs only, now leaves that name maybe-absent when a run may store an absence there, so a sequence binding it into a plain output is refused with optional_not_handled rather than validating and then resolving absent.
  • A configuration value of the wrong type is a validation error (Breaking): a model's costs, listed_constraints, valued_constraints or rules in a backend file or in a plugin's internal model, a backend's constraints in backends.toml, and package_log_levels in pipelex.toml no longer crash the boot with a bare AttributeError or TypeError naming nothing when written as a value of the wrong shape, such as costs = "free" or a date; the boot fails with a message naming the field, the model, the backend and the file, or the plugin, and an empty inference.dry_run.image_urls is reported the same way. A plugin may set an internal model's costs to None. Some values that used to be accepted are now refused: a table as listed_constraints, a string as interpreter.scan.excluded_dirs, a price that is nan or infinite, and a max_tokens setting that is neither an integer nor "auto", which used to fall back to the model's default.
  • A construct path holding nothing leaves a defaulted field to its default: a PipeCompose construct field fed { from = "doc.note" } where note holds nothing is left unset when the target field refuses null but has a default, so it takes that default rather than failing the composition; a target field that admits null still receives it.
  • A model's null on a defaulted field is refused where it can be asked again: the class a worker rebuilds from a structure's JSON schema keeps a defaulted field non-nullable, so a model answering null there is asked again rather than failing when its answer reaches the caller's class. A model answering null on a required native.Anything field is asked again in process, but across a worker boundary its schema stays open, so the step fails there.
  • A field whose Literal lists None may hold nothing: a Python class field typed Literal["a", None] or object is read as one that may hold nothing, so a binding step reading it declares a possible absence and a PipeCompose path holding nothing gives it None rather than its default.
  • Binding and batch refusals name what the author wrote: a binding step carrying a pipe step's fields proposes the remedy that applies, a dotted batch_over for a dotted from, a plain batch for a bare name, or moving nb_output and multiple_output to a pipe step, and a sequence step's refusal of its batch or count fields names the step rather than blaming the pipe the step runs. At run time, a batch over a dotted batch_over names that path, never the private _bound_ name the sequence binds it under, in its message and in the error's variable_name, and a value there that is not a list is refused with PipeRunInputsError rather than an uncaught WorkingMemoryTypeError.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• ConfigModelError and ConfigModel's conversion helpers (Breaking): ConfigModel.transform_dict_str_to_enum, transform_dict_of_floats_str_to_enum, transform_dict_keys_str_to_enum and transform_list_of_str_to_enum are gone, and with them ConfigModelError, which only they raised. A configuration model holding enums in a container annotates them with LaxEnum from pipelex.system.configuration.config_model, list[LaxEnum[MyEnum]], and pydantic converts the strings itself.
  • [inference.gateway_test] (Breaking): the maintainer-only section whose config_id_substitutions map swapped the Pipelex Gateway's model configurations is gone, with its GatewayTestConfig model and the gateway_test field of InferenceConfig, as nothing has read it since the Gateway backend left in 0.73.0. Migration: run pipelex migrate, which deletes the section from the file on disk (ledger entry pipelex-config@8).

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • The API server refuses to start on an unknown AUTH_MODE (Breaking): a value that is not exactly none, jwt or api_key, such as jwtt or JWT, now stops the server at startup with InvalidAuthModeError, whose message names the valid modes, where the server used to log a warning and serve every /v1 route without authentication. An unset or empty AUTH_MODE still means none. A deployment that booted on a mistyped mode sets it to the mode it meant.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Formatted Markdown for document engines, and a markdown filter for plain-data templates: the document engine contract gains format_markdown in pipelex.cogt.doc_gen.formatted_markdown, which reads a Markdown text by the rules the built-in PDF engine prints it by and returns a FormattedMarkdown, plain data of paragraphs, headings, list items with their marker and the paragraph or heading they open with, code blocks, rules and tables whose cells carry their column's alignment, every block with the list depth and the quote depth it sits at and holding text spans with their bold, italic, strikethrough, code and link, whose str() is its plain text and which is false when the text formats into nothing, so an engine prints Markdown formatted in its own format. make_plain_data_template_environment() registers a markdown filter that returns one, {{ invoice.notes | markdown }}, which is false for an empty or a blank text, so {% set notes = invoice.notes | markdown %}{% if notes %}…{{ notes }}…{% endif %} converts the text once to test and print it, and takes an optional finalize through which an engine prints it, a value printing its plain text without one. Inside a template render the conversion is charged to the render's budget; called from an engine's own code it spends from a budget of its own, as large as one render's, and an overdraft raises MarkdownFormattingBudgetError.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • A PDF of deeply nested emphasis prints: the built-in PDF engine no longer fails with a RecursionError on a Markdown text whose emphasis nests hundreds deep, such as four hundred *a before a word and four hundred c* after it; inline markup nested past fifty levels is dropped and its text printed.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The console shows a log call's fields and renders named layouts: the console sink prints a record's fields after its message as a key=value suffix, Scanned the inputs files=7, each value on one line and cut short past 80 characters, a string or the JSON of a list or a mapping before it is quoted so a quoted value keeps both its quotes and a cut one leaves no unbalanced quote or bracket, a path or a list of paths (a field named file.path or ending in _path, _paths, _dir, _dirs, _file or _files) at its start so the last file's name stays, a handled exception's error.message and a PipeDocGen template finding's text only past 2000, leaving out the run identifiers, and colours a value by its field's name, a pipe code red and a concept bold green, with any other field dimmed. A call can name a console layout with layout=, a Rich template over its fields in which every value is escaped, starting with LogLayout.PIPE_RUN for the pipe-run tree; every other sink writes the plain message and the fields.
  • Log-call conventions and their guard: the logging documentation states how Pipelex's own log calls are written, a fixed message with its values in fields named from a shared vocabulary, an exception carried by the record rather than spliced into the text, no run identifier, payload, markup or emoji, and what each level promises. make check-log-calls (pipelex-dev check-log-calls), part of make agent-check and CI, refuses an interpolated or non-literal message at INFO and above and a Rich markup tag in a message at any level, against a committed baseline of the existing calls that only shrinks: --against <ref> and --against-merge-base <ref> refuse an entry the baseline at the base revision does not list, which CI runs against a pull request's base and make against the merge base with origin/dev. pipelex.tools.log.error_fields gives a handled exception's class and text as the error.type and error.message fields of a line that carries no traceback, a pydantic ValidationError's text as its locations and reasons without the values it refused or the name of a key the model forbids, and any message that may quote the input, a custom validator's or one of pydantic's own templates', such as an unknown discriminator tag, as its error type alone.
  • Summary events for inference calls and pipe runs: every inference call, an LLM call, an image generation, an extraction, a search, a judgment or a document print, a call its checks refuse included, ends with one INFO event, Inference call ends, carrying the operation under gen_ai.operation.name, the model under model_handle, backend_name, sdk, gen_ai.request.model and gen_ai.response.model, the tokens under gen_ai.usage.input_tokens and gen_ai.usage.output_tokens and the price under cost_usd where the call recorded them, duration_ms, and outcome, success, error with error.type, or cancelled for work stopped from outside, logged by the worker bases so every provider's and plugin's worker gets it. Every live pipe run ends with Pipe run ends, logged as the pipe's own span closes and carrying its ids, with the announcement's fields, duration_ms, outcome and error.type, so a run's json output alone gives latency and cost per operation and model; an event that cannot be built is replaced by the warning A summary event could not be logged and never changes the work's outcome. The console draws each on one line through LogLayout.INFERENCE_CALL_END and LogLayout.PIPE_RUN_END; a document engine overrides render alone, and the print stage that calls it logs the event.
  • Request- and page-priced usage: a usage says what its counts are in pricing_unit (PricingUnit in pipelex.cogt.usage.pricing_unit), token, request or page, and a worker billed by the request or by the page records it with record_unit_priced_usage (pipelex.cogt.usage.usage_cost), as the Linkup workers and the extraction page fallback now do, so the summary event carries the call's cost and no token counts.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Log lines carry a fixed message and their values as fields (Breaking): every INFO, WARNING, ERROR and CRITICAL line of Pipelex and of its API server has one fixed sentence for its message and carries what varies, a pipe code, a model handle, a file path, a handled error's error.type and error.message, as fields named from the vocabulary in the logging documentation, so a log store groups a line by its message and filters it by its fields, and the baseline of make check-log-calls is empty, every call being held to the conventions. A line nobody can act on moved down to DEBUG, a lost inference usage record up to ERROR, an exception logged and then re-raised, a cleanup's failure while another error propagates and a swallowed ValidationError carry no traceback, whose text could quote a run's inputs, so a failed pipelex run prints one, and pipelex run and pipelex graph render log an unexpected failure at ERROR with its traceback, which the console renders under the line without its local variables and a structured sink writes to the log store, while the command's own output names the exception's type and message whatever the sink and the level. What breaks is a log query: the API server's error record drops its event: api_error field and renames route, user_id, error_type, status, provider and model to url.path, user.id, error.type, http.response.status_code, backend_name and model_handle, the API server no longer writes a refused user_id claim or X-User-Id header under user.id, the claim's type riding claim_type instead, and the warning that a configuration file is out of date is one line per stale file, the file in file.path, where it used to list them all in one.
  • Debug and verbose log output: the DEBUG and VERBOSE lines are fewer and shorter, each naming what it is about rather than narrating every step, and none carries a payload any more: no base64 data, prompt, rendered template, raw response or model dump. An LLM call's reasoning settings are logged once per call, at DEBUG with each setting sent as a field, rather than twice at VERBOSE, and the error for undecodable base64 input gives the input's length instead of its first bytes.
  • The pipe announcement is a plain message with fields: every live pipe run logs Pipe run starts with pipe_type, pipe_code, output_concept and pipe_depth as fields, where the json, otlp and gcp sinks used to receive Rich markup inside the message, and the console draws the same coloured pipe tree from those fields through LogLayout.PIPE_RUN. The warning that a model's fixed temperature replaced the requested one carries its values as fields in the same way: model_handle, backend_name, sdk, the model's handle under gen_ai.request.model and the provider's model id under gen_ai.response.model as on the LLM call's span, the requested temperature under gen_ai.request.temperature, and fixed_temperature; the verbose line saying a model's settings were not checked, since its backend's SDK is not installed, carries the same model fields.
  • The default output logs every inference call and every live pipe run: at the default INFO level an application embedding pipelex now gets an Inference call ends line after each inference call and a Pipe run ends line after each live pipe run. To quiet either, raise its logger's level in [runtime.log.package_log_levels]: pipelex-cogt-inference-inference_call_summary = "WARNING" for the inference event, and pipelex-pipe_machinery-pipe_abstract = "WARNING" for the pipe-run end, which quiets the pipe announcement too, since the two share that logger.
  • log.set_level_by_name takes only Pipelex level names (Breaking): it accepts a LogLevel name in any case and raises ValueError for any other, so the stdlib spellings WARN, FATAL and NOTSET it used to accept are refused. Pass WARNING for WARN and CRITICAL for FATAL; NOTSET has no counterpart, VERBOSE being the lowest level.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Model descriptions and credential errors carry no backslashes: a model's description in an error message or a log line, such as gpt-5 → SDK[openai]•Backend[openai]•Model[gpt-5-2025], no longer has a backslash before each bracket, and the error naming a backend's missing credentials tells you to add enabled = false under [openai] rather than \[openai]. pipelex run prints a failed run's message exactly as written rather than reading it as markup.
  • No HTTP request line per inference call: at the default INFO level an inference call made through openai 3.x no longer logs an HTTP Request: POST https://… "HTTP/1.1 200 OK" line, carrying the provider's endpoint URL and the HTTP status, on the console or in the json sink. The defaults under [runtime.log.package_log_levels] now give httpx2 and httpcore2, the HTTP client forks openai 3.x sends its requests through, the levels httpx and httpcore already had, WARNING and INFO; set httpx2 = "INFO" there to see the line again.
  • An empty list's output panel says so: the title of the panel showing an operator pipe's output ends with [empty list] when the pipe produced an empty list, a label the console used to drop, as it already showed [1 item] or [3 items].

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• The DEV log level (Breaking): LogLevel.DEV, LOGGING_LEVEL_DEV and log.dev() are gone; the levels are VERBOSE, DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL and OFF, and code calling log.dev() calls log.debug() instead. A configuration file naming DEV, as default_log_level or as a level under [runtime.log.package_log_levels], is migrated in memory at boot by ledger entry pipelex-config@6, which reads it as INFO, the level that lets through the same records now that nothing logs at DEV, and the boot warns that the file is out of date. Migration: run pipelex migrate, which rewrites DEV to INFO in the file on disk.
  • Logging helpers nothing called (Breaking): FuncRegistry.log() and FuncRegistry.set_logger(), with the func_registry logger they wrote to, InferenceManager.print_workers() and LogLevel.from_int() are gone, with no replacement. Code that needs a LogLevel from a stdlib level number maps it itself.
  • Cost helpers outside pipelex.cogt.usage.usage_cost (Breaking): compute_tokens_usage_cost is imported from pipelex.cogt.usage.usage_cost rather than pipelex.cogt.usage.cost_registry, CostRegistry.compute_total_cost is gone for compute_total_cost in the same module, and the TokensUsage alias of pipelex.reporting.reporting_types is gone: import TokensUsage from pipelex.cogt.usage.usage_cost, where it is a plain union of the usage types without the old discriminator, or use the discriminated AnyTokensUsage, which stays in pipelex.reporting.reporting_types.
  • is_markup_enabled (Breaking): the console reads no log message as Rich markup, so the [runtime.log.rich_log] key that switched it is gone, along with VERBATIM_MARK in pipelex.tools.log.log_fields. A message now prints exactly as written, so a list[int], a bracketed path, the [myapp.jobs.nightly]: prefix of a logger named in lowercase and the [cycle] marker of a circular content no longer vanish, while a message of your own that relied on markup for its colour shows its tags and should put its values in fields. Migration: run pipelex migrate, which deletes the key from the file on disk (ledger entry pipelex-config@7).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• MTHDS standard 4.0.0 (Breaking): pipelex now requires mthds==0.20.0 and pipelex-sdk==0.37.0, the releases that report MTHDS standard 4.0.0, the language this runtime has implemented since v0.75.0, so everyone downstream inherits those exact versions and a project that pins either package itself has to move with them. pipelex --version prints mthds-standard 4.0.0, every crate pipelex normalizes is stamped with mthds_version 4.0.0 while crate fingerprints stay the same, and a package whose METHODS.toml constrains mthds_version to ^3.0.0, ~3.0.0 or exactly 3.0.0 now logs a warning when it loads, which >=3.0.0 or ^4.0.0 does not.
  • Stored names are plain input names (Breaking): every name under which a step stores a value in working memory, a PipeSequence step's or a PipeParallel branch's result, the batch_as of either, and a PipeBatch's input_item_name, must now be a plain input name matching [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, as a binding step's result already had to, and a name in any other form, such as Pages, doc.pages or _pages, is refused as invalid_input_name wherever a bundle loads, and by the MTHDS JSON Schema, which now carries the input-name pattern on these fields. Rename such a name to a plain one, such as pages, along with every input, binding path and batch_over that reads it; a plain batch_over is still refused only when it starts with the reserved _bound_.
  • Hosted-run guidance in messages and help: the next step of a refused Pipelex API key names pipelex login and the working directory's .env rather than a shell export, which a .env file setting the key overrides, and pipelex login names [run] execution = "hosted" rather than pipelex init to make hosted runs the default. A CLI run missing a provider key, and the pipelex doctor report, offer the hosted Pipelex API as a way out; a failed pipelex-agent boot points at pipelex-agent migrate and pipelex-agent init rather than the interactive pipelex init config; and FormerReleaseConfigError carries its remedy, pipelex migrate, as its user_action. The run help of both CLIs names hosted runs, catalog ids, local method directories and TOML or inline inputs, and pipelex-agent --help describes the program rather than printing an internal note.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • The json log sink keeps each field's type: a field value JSON refuses outright, a mapping with a non-string key or a circular reference, is written as its repr alone, where it used to turn every other field on the line into its repr as well, so a number or a boolean beside it arrived as "7" or "True" and a query over that field missed the line. The other fields now keep their JSON types, as they already did under the gcp sink.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The wait_and_retry advice says to run again: the user_action.detail of a transient inference failure said "the system will retry automatically", which no longer held by the time anyone read the failed run's report, and now says to wait, at least the provider's Retry-After delay when it gave one, then run it again; the advice on an empty or malformed Mistral response says the same.
  • A malformed Retry-After is no delay: a provider's Retry-After that is negative or not a finite number (inf, nan, 1e999) is ignored rather than taken as a delay, so the advice says to wait a moment instead of naming an impossible wait.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text: Run any method on the hosted Pipelex API with nothing but a Pipelex API key. pipelex run --hosted sends your bundle, a published address or a catalog id (mt_…) to the hosted API and saves the outputs where a local run would, with no provider key and no inference configuration on your machine. pipelex login gets the key through your browser, pipelex init offers the hosted API as its default, and Python code runs there directly with pipelex-sdk's PipelexAPIClient, which now ships with pipelex.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Hosted runs with --hosted, --local and [run] execution (Breaking): pipelex run method|pipe|bundle and pipelex-agent run run on the hosted Pipelex API under --hosted and on this machine under --local, the new [run] execution setting (default local) choosing when neither is given, and --base-url or PIPELEX_BASE_URL naming another server. A hosted run boots nothing locally, uploads the local files its inputs name, prints the run id as soon as the run is acknowledged and names it in any later failure, Ctrl-C included. The agent CLI's --runner pipelex|api becomes --runner local|hosted, on pipelex-sdk's PipelexAPIClient, which pipelex now pins exactly.
  • pipelex login: gets a Pipelex API key through the browser, or from a hidden prompt with --paste, checks it against the hosted API and saves it to ~/.pipelex/.env as PIPELEX_API_KEY without ever printing it. It warns when a working-directory .env would override the saved key, and PIPELEX_APP_URL aims it at another Pipelex app.
  • pipelex init asks where runs execute: Enter takes the hosted Pipelex API, which signs you in and needs no provider key, while the other answer sets up local backends and credentials as before; the answer is saved as [run] execution. pipelex doctor and pipelex-agent doctor judge a hosted setup by its API key, pipelex doctor --fix takes the hosted default only for a brand-new home, and pipelex-agent init accepts "execution": "hosted" in --config.
  • pipelex migrate removes what a former release left for the Pipelex Gateway: a configuration written for the Pipelex Gateway is refused at boot with the new FormerReleaseConfigError, which points at pipelex migrate. That command, pipelex-agent migrate (under former_release), pipelex init and pipelex doctor --fix remove the Gateway's backend, routing profiles, routes and files, keeping Pipelex Manifold's and a copy of every file they change.
  • Shared helpers in the document engine contract: pipelex.cogt.doc_gen.layout_display (display_scalar, is_numeric_column, markdown_as_html) and pipelex.cogt.doc_gen.template_environment (make_plain_data_template_environment()) give a plugin's engines the value display, Markdown conversion and sandboxed, strict Jinja environment of the built-in PDF engine, without importing ReportLab or Pipelex's internals.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • RenderResources.load returns the media type with the bytes (Breaking): a document engine's load returns a LoadedResource holding data and the mime_type its source declares (an https:// response's Content-Type, a data: URL's type, or the storage provider's type for a pipelex-storage:// key), else None. PLUGIN_API_VERSION moves to 6, so a plugin declaring targets_api = 5 is refused at discovery until it is rebuilt to read .data.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A partial home configuration directory gets the kit's missing files: every boot copies into ~/.pipelex/ (or PIPELEX_HOME) each kit file it lacks, never overwriting a file or writing through a symbolic link, the inference files as one unit only when inference/backends.toml is absent. A directory holding anything at all, such as an earlier release's pipelex_service.toml, was left as it was, and every boot then failed with "Config files are missing for the inference backend library".
  • The internal backend's models are served whatever the routing profile: a profile routing a model's name to no enabled backend left the internal models (reportlab-pdf, pypdfium2-extract-pdf, docling-extract-text and those plugins add) unserved, so local extraction and document steps were refused at load, as under the default all_enabled_backends profile with only the internal backend enabled. The internal backend now serves such a name, while a route sending it elsewhere still decides and disabling the backend still withholds its models.
  • pipelex-agent init --help prints list[str]: the --config help showed the schema's "backends": list[str] as list, because Rich read [str] as markup.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
A client can ask the runner what a model reference means. GET /v1/models/check answers whether a reference resolves, as what kind, and to the model a run would call, from pipelex's own parser and deck, so a client keeps no grammar of model references of its own.

A handle names one model per model type. One handle can be an LLM and a judgment model at once, and a pipe naming a model served only as another type is refused when the method loads rather than at its first call.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Claude Haiku 5.5 on the anthropic backend: claude-5.5-haiku (model id claude-haiku-5-5) takes text, images and PDF, produces text and structured output, and reasons with adaptive thinking, with up to 128K output tokens. It costs $0.10 / $0.50 per million tokens for a prompt up to 100,000 tokens and $0.50 / $2.50 above, of which the backend file records the first. It refuses temperature but, unlike Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, accepts a forced tool_choice, so structured output keeps instructor/anthropic_tools.
  • One handle, one model per model type: two models of different model types may share a handle, so gpt-6-luna can be an LLM and a judgment model at once, and each pipe reaches the one its family asks for. A backend file declares the second model of a handle on a table of its own with the new handle key, which may not appear in [defaults], and a file declaring one handle twice as the same type fails to load, naming both tables. A plugin may declare an internal model under a name internal.toml already declares as another type.
  • GET /v1/models/check, the model reference check: the server answers whether one model reference (?reference=, optionally in one ?type= category, doc_gen included) resolves on this runner, as a 200 verdict discriminated on resolution (resolved or not_found) that carries the reference's kind and name, one match per category where it resolves with the model a run would call (resolves_to, null where its binding reaches no model the runner can call) and its target, description, fallbacks or via, and, on not_found, the suggestions, other_kinds and other_categories a failing validation of the same reference offers, written as references. It answers from pipelex's own parser and the deck lookups a validation runs, so a client no longer keeps its own grammar of model references, and it is a Pipelex API extension, not tagged x-mthds-protocol. A missing or repeated reference or a repeated type is a 422 ValidationError, a reference that is blank, a sigil or a namespace alone, or longer than 199 characters once trimmed is a 422 of the new error_type InvalidModelReference, and an unknown or empty type is a 422 InvalidModelCategory. The library serves the same check as check_model_reference in pipelex.cogt.models.model_reference_check, and the suggestion rule as find_model_alternatives in pipelex.cogt.models.model_suggestion.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• A model served only as another type is refused when the method loads (Breaking): a pipe naming a handle the deck serves only as another model type, such as a PipeJudge naming an LLM, is refused by pipelex validate, POST /v1/validate and a run's load as an unknown_model item saying the deck serves the handle but not as the type the pipe needs, whose suggestions list only models of that type, where it passed validation and failed at its first call; a deck preset naming one is reported at boot in the same words (a warning, or a refusal under missing_presets_reaction = "raise"), and an LLM override naming one refuses boot. A bare name resolves as a model of the pipe's type, then an alias of that type, then a waterfall of that type, an order the validation and the run's lookup share, so a handle served as another type no longer hides an alias or a waterfall of the same name, and the validation and the setting a pipe's model field is read into accept the waterfall only while model fallback is on. ModelDeck gains is_bare_handle_resolvable, is_reference_defined, get_presets_for_type and peek_inference_model, the run's model lookup without its logs.
  • Model specs are keyed by model type and handle (Breaking): InferenceBackend.model_specs and ModelDeck.inference_models are the new ModelSpecIndex, read through get(model_type=…, handle=…), handles_of_type, all_specs, all_handles and types_serving, and InferenceBackend.get_model_spec takes model_type and handle. InferenceBackend.list_model_names, InferenceBackendLibrary.list_all_model_names and InferenceBackendLibrary.get_all_models_and_possible_backends are removed. PluginModelDeclarations.internal_models is a tuple of PluginInternalModel, which carries its name, and DuplicateInternalModelError names the model_type two plugins both declared.
  • Usage is reported per model type and name (Breaking): a run calling both kinds of one handle reports two rows in the cost table and the agent CLI's cost summary, and two entries in the graph's usage attribution, where they merged into one row typed by whichever call came last. AggregatedCosts.grouped_by_model is keyed by the new ModelUsageKey, and its model_types is removed.
  • handle: reads no sigil (Breaking): a handle: reference writes a bare name without reading a sigil in the validation, the run and the check alike, so handle:@name is the bare name @name, not the alias name, and like any bare name it resolves as a model, then an alias, then a waterfall of that name, a validation refusing it where the deck has none.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A ~name model reference runs the waterfall: a pipe naming ~name or waterfall:name called a model or an alias that shares the waterfall's name, because its setting kept the bare name, and every model type's setting now keeps the sigil, so a run calls the model the validation and GET /v1/models/check name; the resolved_model every pipe reports, and a PipeLLM's resolved_model_for_object, now write such a waterfall ~name, and so does a refusal of a file input naming one.
  • A waterfall step that leads back to itself or runs out serves no model: an alias and a waterfall leading to each other, or a waterfall listing its own name, overflowed the stack, and a step naming another waterfall, directly or through an alias, none of whose models is served failed its waterfall with that inner waterfall's error. Such a step, whether it leads back to an alias or a waterfall being resolved or reaches a waterfall that runs out, now serves no model, so the waterfall goes on to its next step, and a run fails with the waterfall's own error only when none of its steps serves a model.
  • pipelex-agent models --backend lists past a binding no backend serves: an alias or a preset bound to a waterfall none of whose models the deck serves failed the listing with ModelWaterfallError, and it is now left out like any binding of another backend, the listing reading the deck without a run's logs.
  • pipelex-agent check-model applies the validation's rule: a bare alias name, or a bare waterfall name while model fallback is on, is now valid, as pipelex validate and GET /v1/models/check answer, and --type takes doc_gen as the check does.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 on the anthropic backend: claude-5.5-opus (model id claude-opus-5-5, $4 / $20 per million tokens) and claude-5.5-sonnet (model id claude-sonnet-5-5, $2 / $10) take text, images and PDF, produce text and structured output, and reason with adaptive thinking, with up to 128K output tokens each. Both refuse temperature and a forced tool_choice, so structured output uses instructor/anthropic_reasoning_tools, as claude-5.1-fable does.
  • GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna on the openai and azure_openai backends: gpt-6.1-sol ($2 / $10 per million tokens) and gpt-6-luna ($0.10 / $0.50) take text, images and PDF, produce text and structured output, reason with a manual effort and fix their temperature at 1, like the rest of the GPT-6 series. On azure_openai their model ids are the deployments gpt-6.1-sol-2026-09-29 and gpt-6-luna-2026-09-22. The shipped deck is unchanged.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A reasoning setting reaches a structured output: a pipe whose model setting carries reasoning_effort or reasoning_budget, the deck's $deep-analysis, $quick-reasoning and $retrieval-premium presets included, now generates its structured output with that setting on every provider, where every language-model worker refused it with LLMCapabilityError "does not support reasoning parameters for structured generation". A model refuses a reasoning setting on a structured output only where it refuses it on text, or on Mistral where its structure method is not instructor/mistral_tools, whose JSON parsing cannot read a reasoning reply; a structured call on an Anthropic tool method with thinking on leaves the tool choice to the model, since a forced tool choice cannot carry thinking.
  • A manual thinking budget leaves room for the answer and stays in the model's range (Breaking): an Anthropic or Gemini thinking budget, resolved from an effort or set explicitly, is cut to leave a quarter of max_tokens for the answer, where it could take all but one token of it, and held within the range the model declares with the new min_thinking_budget and max_thinking_budget valued constraints. The kit's Anthropic models declare the API's minimum of 1,024 tokens, so the 512 that minimal maps to is raised to it, and its Gemini 2.5 models declare their ranges, so max effort's 65,536 tokens, which every Gemini 2.5 model refused, are cut to the model's maximum even without a max_tokens. A max_tokens too small to hold the model's minimum beside the answer reserve is refused with an LLMCapabilityError naming the numbers, where the request was sent, and a reasoning effort of none on a Gemini model that always thinks, which the kit marks with the new thinking_cannot_be_disabled listed constraint, is refused rather than sent as a budget of 0 that Gemini answers with a 400; a project that copied the kit's anthropic.toml, bedrock.toml or google.toml gets the bounds by declaring them in its copy.
  • Mistral reasoning is sent as reasoning_effort: a reasoning effort on a Mistral model is sent as reasoning_effort = "high", the only reasoning value Mistral's reasoning models accept, where it was sent as prompt_mode = "reasoning", which every current Mistral model refuses, so any reasoning effort on Mistral failed. The reasoning level of [inference.llm.mistral.effort_to_level_map] is unchanged.
  • A model setting its model refuses is refused when the method loads (Breaking): a PipeLLM or PipeStructure whose model setting the model it resolves to cannot take, such as a reasoning setting on a model declaring thinking_mode = "none", a reasoning budget on an OpenAI or Mistral model, a thinking budget its max_tokens cannot hold, or a structured output on a Bedrock native model, is refused by pipelex validate, POST /v1/validate and a run's load as an item of the new PipeValidationErrorType value llm_setting_refused_by_model on its model or model_to_structure field, where it validated as runnable and failed at its first call. The check is the new check_request classmethod of the LLM workers, which LLMWorkerAbstract now runs before every provider call and which an LLM backend registers for validation through the new optional check_llm_request of PluginRegistrar.add_inference_backend, whose CheckLLMRequestFn, LLMJobParams and LLMCapabilityError the Inference SPI table publishes; a backend registering none, an external plugin's included, is held to the rule every worker shares, that a model declaring thinking_mode = "none" takes no reasoning setting. The item names the model by its deck handle and is shown even under strict error disclosure, so an external plugin's refusal is shown as written only when the plugin raises it as caller-facing copy with as_caller_fault(), and by its title otherwise.
  • A structured output on Google without a system prompt no longer fails: a structured call on the google backend whose prompt has no system text failed with TypeError "generate_content() got an unexpected keyword argument 'system'", and is now sent with no system instruction.
  • A model listing temperature_unsupported gets no temperature on any SDK: a model whose backend file lists the temperature_unsupported constraint is now called without a temperature on the OpenAI Responses, Google, Mistral and Bedrock-native SDKs too, where those sent one anyway and only the Anthropic and OpenAI chat-completions SDKs honoured the constraint. The model spec answers it as the new accepts_temperature property, and a Bedrock client's chat now takes temperature=None to send none.
  • A binding step survives a kajson round trip: BindingStepBlueprint is encoded under from, the key it validates, where kajson wrote its field name from_path, which decoding refused as an extra field. A library crate holding a sequence with a binding step can now cross a process boundary, so a run of such a method no longer fails to start on a Temporal worker with "Could not instantiate pydantic BaseModel … BindingStepBlueprint".

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• A run request carries the method packages its bundle calls (Breaking): a files or bundle_b64 request to /v1/execute or /v1/start may ship each package its bundle calls by address under .mthds/methods/<name>/ at its root, with its METHODS.toml, and the server searches them before its installed copies and fetch-on-miss, for that run alone, so a shipped package wins over an installed copy and runs with fetching off; a package fetched by method_ref that ships its own .mthds/methods/ is handled the same way. Those files no longer join the bundle's own .mthds content or its library directory, any other .mthds path in a bundle is refused with a 422 InvalidBundle naming the entry, as are two shipped packages declaring the same address and name without regard to case, and on a sandbox-hosted deployment a shipped package declaring a Python structure class is refused with 403 MethodStructuresRefusedError. The engine takes these directories as the new keyword-only methods_dirs of PipelexMTHDSProtocol, pipeline_run_setup, acquire_library and LibraryManagerAbstract.load_from_blueprints, which every implementation of the abstract must accept.
  • The MTHDS Test Corpus covers a sequence step's multiplicity: the invalid entry invalid_input_stuff_spec_mismatch_step_multiplicity has a step read as a single Page the pages an earlier extraction stored as Page[], and fails with input_stuff_spec_mismatch; the valid offline entry controller_sequence_house_rules declares house_rules = "Markdown" for a sequence whose first step reads it as Markdown and whose second reads it as Text, and runs it.
  • The MTHDS Test Corpus covers the markdown template filter: the new hand-maintained feature.markdown_filter tag names the filter of HTML templates that turns Markdown held in a plain text field into HTML, and the offline-tier entry feature_markdown_filter_cake_order_slip covers it with a PipeCompose run that pins its output, raw HTML in the source shown as text and only a URL with a scheme made a link.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The documentation no longer describes the Pipelex Gateway: Configure AI Providers offers your own provider keys or a local model, says that the shipped defaults run as they are on OpenAI or Azure OpenAI and must be repointed for any other provider, OpenRouter included, and points to the Quick Start for running on the hosted API; the MTHDS language tutorial no longer runs pipelex login. The telemetry, logging, feature and under-the-hood pages describe only the telemetry streams you configure yourself and the backends the runtime ships, without the Gateway stream, its backend or its plugin.
  • A call into a method package that cannot be resolved is a verdict item (Breaking): when a bundle names a pipe of another package by its address and the package is not installed and cannot be fetched (fetch-on-miss off, an address this runtime cannot fetch, a failed fetch), the load is refused with one item of the new PipeValidationErrorType value unresolved_package_dependency per package, on the first pipe naming it, with the reference as written in missing_pipe_code, where it raised MethodFetchDisabledError or MethodDependencyFetchError and the API answered a no-verdict 500. POST /v1/validate now answers 200 with is_valid: false and the run routes a 422, every package of the bundle is tried before the refusal, a failed clone's message no longer names the runner's temporary clone directory, and the remedies name no directory on the host and include shipping the package with the bundle under .mthds/methods/<name>/. The MTHDS Test Corpus covers it as invalid_unresolved_package_dependency.
  • A package bundle that does not parse refuses the load (Breaking): when a bundle of a package the consumer calls by address does not parse, the load is refused with the parser's items, each naming the file as <address>/<path inside the package> and never by its path on the host, whether the package was shipped with the bundle, installed or fetched. It used to be skipped with a warning, so the caller learned of it from a later refusal about a pipe.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A validation message no longer names one concept as both required and provided: the (required: …, provided: …) suffix of a validation item is left off when the provided concept is among the required ones, since the disagreement then lies elsewhere, so a step reading one Page where an earlier step stored Page[] no longer ends its message with (required: native.Page, provided: native.Page).
  • A provenance sidecar that is not UTF-8 no longer breaks method discovery: an installed or shipped method package whose .provenance.json is not valid UTF-8 is discovered with no recorded provenance, as one that does not parse already was, where discovery raised UnicodeDecodeError and a run calling the package answered a 500.
  • A files entry holding a lone surrogate is refused as an invalid bundle: a name or a text in a run request's files map holding an escaped lone surrogate such as "\ud800", which JSON carries but UTF-8 cannot encode, is refused with a 422 InvalidBundle naming the entry, where the server answered a 500.
  • A bundle naming one path twice is refused: a run request whose bundle holds two entries for one file, spelled differently in a files map (a/./b beside a/b) or twice in a zip, or a file that is also the directory of another entry, is refused with a 422 InvalidBundle naming the path, where the engine silently took the last copy of a file named twice and the server answered a 500 for a file that is also a directory.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The binding step: a PipeSequence step { from = "invoice.total", result = "total_amount" } binds a deep copy of the value at a path in working memory to a new name, as a fresh stuff whose concept is derived from the declared structures the path walks, a path crossing a list binding one flattened X[], and a later step reads it under that plain name. The sequence checks a step reading a binding, or a binding ending it, against the derived concept and multiplicity, a path reaching nothing records an absence under the optionality model, and the execution graph draws each binding as a node of the new NodeKind binding. A malformed step is refused as the new PipeValidationErrorType value binding_step_invalid, which the MTHDS JSON Schema refuses too, and a path the declared structures cannot walk as binding_path_unresolved; the MTHDS Test Corpus covers both under the feature.binding_step tag, and its offline-tier entries now run with their inputs.json in the test suite.
  • pipelex fix bundle deletes a dotted input key beside its root: the new rule delete-redundant-dotted-input removes a key such as "page.page_view" = "Image" from a pipe's inputs when the same table declares its root page, which already supplies every field a template reads through it. The fix is safe, and applied, only when the root's declared concept holds the field the key names and the root keeps the presence marker and multiplicity the table gave it: a root declared with a concept that lacks the field, such as data = "Number" beside "data.text" = "Text", or a key that set the markers otherwise, such as "data.text" = "Text!" declared after data = "Text?", gets an unsafe fix that pipelex fix bundle never applies, and both the fix and the refusal name what differs, with the edit that settles it on the root (here, replace ? with ! on data). A lone dotted key gets no automatic fix, since nothing states its root's concept, and its refusal names the two remedies instead.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• GraphAnalysis.stuff_producers lists every producer (Breaking): it maps a digest to a list of node ids, get_producer is replaced by get_producers, and the new shared_stuff_controllers names the controller a stuff with several writers belongs to, a parallel or batch controller combining or aggregating into the stuff counting as one of them. The Mermaid graph draws such a stuff once, inside that controller, with an edge from each producer.
  • InferenceBackendLibrary.load takes credentials (Breaking): its lenient flag is replaced by credentials: CredentialResolution, REQUIRE or SKIP. A backend a SKIP load built records what it left unresolved in InferenceBackend.unresolved_credentials, and ModelManager.get_required_inference_backend refuses it with an InferenceBackendCredentialsError of type not_resolved_on_keyless_boot that names the variables.
  • A routing profile naming a disabled backend is refused on every boot (Breaking): a boot without inference, such as pipelex validate, now refuses a routing profile whose default or routes name a backend that is not enabled, as a boot with inference already did, and load_active_routing_profile loses its lenient argument.
  • A variable in a field that describes a model is refused on every boot (Breaking): a ${…} placeholder may stand only in a value a call sends, which means api_key, endpoint and a backend's extra keys, or a model's model_id, endpoint_path and request headers. A placeholder in a field such as model_type, sdk, thinking_mode or the constraints is now refused with an error naming the field, where a boot with inference substituted it and a boot without inference could not, so the two gave different verdicts.
  • An unknown variable prefix is refused wherever it stands in a fallback chain (Breaking): ${env:KEY|secrte:KEY} is refused for its secrte prefix whether or not KEY is set, where a boot read the candidates in turn and accepted the chain whenever an earlier one resolved. A boot without inference, which resolves nothing, refuses it too, so a file gets the same verdict on its syntax on every boot and every machine.
  • pipelex show backends lists every backend with its credential variables: a backend whose key is unset is listed instead of hidden, a new column names the variables each backend reads its credentials from, and an endpoint read from a variable is shown as not resolved.
  • An input name is a plain name (Breaking): every key of a pipe's inputs, on every operator, controller and signature, and a PipeBatch's input_list_name must match [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, so a dotted name such as "invoice.total" = "Number" or a malformed one such as InvoiceTotal is refused when the bundle is parsed, as the new PipeValidationErrorType value invalid_input_name, which also replaces PipeJudge's own refusal that reached callers with no error_type. Its message names the remedies: declare the root with its whole concept (invoice = "Invoice") and read the field in the template ($invoice.total), which every operator handles by the concept the path reaches, so @page.page_view with page = "Page" is still attached as an image, or have the calling sequence bind the field with a binding step ({ from = "invoice.total", result = "total_amount" }). The generated MTHDS JSON Schema refuses the same names, through patternProperties on every inputs table and a pattern on input_list_name, and the corpus vocabulary records error.invalid_input_name with fails_at = "schema". The dotted-input fold goes with them: InputStuffSpecs no longer rewrites an input key to its root, NamedStuffSpec.requirement_expression is gone, pipelex.pipe_machinery.validation drops is_variable_satisfied_by_inputs, validate_input_name and the dotted_input_supplies_its_path argument of check_inputs_match_variables and check_variables_are_declared, in favour of validate_input_names and check_input_list_name, and build_judgment_material no longer walks a dotted input name as a path.
  • A sequence's steps include binding steps (Breaking): PipeSequenceBlueprint.steps holds BindingStepBlueprint beside SubPipeBlueprint, and PipeSequence.sequential_sub_pipes holds BindingStep beside SubPipe, so code reading pipe or pipe_code off every step reads the new pipe_steps property instead. A PipeParallel's branches keep the pipe-step shape.
  • Names a nested controller stores (Breaking): a name a nested sequence, a condition's outcomes or an add_each_output parallel always stores in the caller's memory counts as stored by the step calling it, so it is no input of the caller, and a sequence that declared such a name only to pass validation is now refused as extraneous_input_variable: remove the declaration. A nested sequence or condition skipped for an absent plain input now records an absence for every name it always stores, so a later step finds a value or an absence there, never nothing.
  • Every sequence step is checked against what it reads (Breaking): validation follows a PipeSequence step by step and refuses, as input_stuff_spec_mismatch, a pipe step whose pipe reads a name as a concept or a multiplicity the value stored there does not have, whether the sequence declared it or an earlier step stored it, so a step reading cv_pages = "Page" where an extraction stored Page[] now fails before anything runs: declare Page[]. A declared input every step reading it accepts validates even when it differs from what the last one reads, so a sequence whose first step reads note as Markdown and a later one as Text declares note = "Markdown", which the sequence's inputs check used to refuse for not being the last step's Text, and that declaration is what the sequence needs from its caller, so a step calling it with a Text under note is refused. A step calling a nested controller is checked against the inputs the controller declares. A value a pipe step stores as Anything or Dynamic, as a condition whose outcomes produce different concepts declares its output, is assumed to be the concept a later step reads, its multiplicity still checked, while a sequence's own input declared Anything and a binding's value are checked as any other, also where a condition whose outcomes do not all store the name may leave them in place. A batched last step yields X[] whatever nb_output it asks for, so a sequence ending with one declares a variable list, where a fixed count or a single output used to pass. PipeLibraryAbstract and ConceptLibraryAbstract gain the abstract property state_token, which every change to a library replaces, so a sequence builds its typed flow once per state of the libraries it resolves in.
  • A dotted batch_over is a binding followed by a batch (Breaking): a sequence step's batch_over = "catalog.pages" binds the list at that path under a private name, _bound_catalog_pages, by every rule of a binding step, then batches over it, so a list root such as catalogs.pages batches over the pages of every catalog, the sequence needs the root as its own concept, and the execution graph draws the binding feeding the batch. A path deriving a single value is refused before the run as input_stuff_spec_mismatch, as a batch over a value that is not a list is, and a path outside the path grammar, or a dotted batch_over on a PipeParallel branch, as binding_step_invalid, which the MTHDS JSON Schema refuses too. The file-format check before the run follows each item of the bound list back to where it sits, as it does after an explicit binding step, so a document at cases[1].transcripts[0] that the batched pipe's model cannot read is refused before the batch starts. The _bound_ prefix is reserved for these private names, since a nested sequence binds in its caller's working memory and would otherwise overwrite a caller's value stored under one: a pipe step's or a PipeParallel branch's result, batch_as or plain batch_over, or a PipeBatch's input_item_name, starting with _bound_ is refused as invalid_input_name, which the MTHDS JSON Schema refuses too.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
