• A batched step's other inputs: a sequence now needs every input a batched step's pipe reads besides its item even when an earlier step stored the list, where it needed them only for a list the sequence received, so declaring one was refused as extraneous_input_variable and leaving it out failed the run inside the batch.
  • A PipeBatch branch gets its own copy of its item: each branch's item is taken from the branch's own copy of the batched list, so a branch that rewrites its item in place, as a PipeFunc can, no longer changes the batch's input list.
  • A dry-run condition's output is one stuff every outcome produces: in the graph of a dry run, every outcome of a PipeCondition now carries the condition's output digest, so the step reading the condition's result is wired to all of them rather than to the outcome whose pipe code sorts last, and when the outcomes write or declare different outputs, the condition's declared output types that stuff on every node outside the outcomes: the condition, the controllers whose output it is, such as a sequence ending on the condition, and the steps reading it, while each outcome keeps the concept it writes. Each outcome but the last now runs on a copy of the memory the condition received, so an outcome reading the condition's slot reads the value from before the condition rather than a sibling's output, and the default outcome runs last, so the steps after the condition read its value.
  • Validation and dry runs no longer depend on which keys the machine holds: a boot without inference (Pipelex.make(needs_inference=False), used by pipelex validate, pipelex run --dry-run, pipelex show and the agent CLI's validation) now loads every enabled backend with its models and constraints and resolves none of their credentials, where it dropped every backend whose key was missing. A method using a search preset or pinning a bare handle such as model = "gpt-4o-mini" now validates on a machine or CI runner with no key, and such a boot no longer reads the backends' keys or requests a Vertex AI token.
  • Linkup uses the key its backend names: the Linkup search and fetch workers take the key from the [linkup] table's api_key, like every other provider, where they read LINKUP_API_KEY themselves and ignored a configuration naming another variable. A Linkup backend with no api_key is refused with LinkupError when its worker is built.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • PIPELEX_HOME relocates the home configuration directory: when set and not empty, it names the directory Pipelex uses in place of ~/.pipelex, for the configuration layers, the inference files and their overrides, the credentials .env, the first-boot copy of the kit, pipelex init, pipelex doctor, pipelex update, pipelex migrate and the agent CLI's --global. It must be in the process environment before Pipelex is imported, a relative value is resolved against the working directory at import, and a PIPELEX_HOME line in a .env file is ignored. The first boot now fills the home directory from the kit when it exists but is empty, as it already did when it was missing, so an empty volume mount or a mktemp -d works as it is.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • A reference to a package's private pipe is refused as unexported: a consumer naming a pipe that a loaded dependency package declares but does not export is refused at load with the new PipeValidationErrorType value unexported_pipe_dependency, whose item names the referring pipe in pipe_code and the reference in missing_pipe_code.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The hosted-only inference provider plugin is no longer shipped (Breaking): its built-in plugin, its sdk tokens, its error classes and their reference pages, and the PipelexBackend member naming its backend are removed, leaving PipelexBackend.INTERNAL alone. A project config that still declares the hosted backend disabled, or a routing profile that names it but is not active, keeps booting; a model spec naming one of its sdk tokens now fails when its worker is built, unless a plugin of your own registers that token.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A dependency package's pipes call their own sub-pipes: a sequence, parallel, condition or batch inside an installed package now reaches the package's own pipe, stored as alias->domain.code, where it used to look the plain domain.code up in the consumer's library. A package whose controllers call its own pipes, such as github.com/Pipelex/methods/documents from 0.1.3, no longer fails to load with PipeNotFoundError, and a consumer pipe of the same domain and code is no longer run in the package's place.
  • An exported pipe can call its package's private pipes (Breaking): a package with [exports] loads every pipe its exported pipes and main_pipes reach, not the exported ones alone, and a private pipe nothing public reaches is not built. Exports are read by domain, so exporting x from one domain no longer exports a pipe named x in another, and PipeLibrary.add_dependency_pipe takes is_exported.
  • A missing pipe of a loaded package is refused at load: a reference to a pipe a loaded dependency package does not have is refused as unresolved_pipe_dependency, naming the package, where it was skipped and reported as an extraneous input with a wrong suggested fix. A dependency's own reference to another package is not checked against the consumer's packages, since a dependency's dependencies are not loaded.
  • A pipe wrapping another package's pipe of the same domain and code reports its inputs: the recursion guards of the needed-inputs, signature and file-input walks tell two pipes of the same domain.code apart by object rather than by pipe_ref. A consumer pipe calling a dependency's pipe of its own domain and code, or one package's pipe calling another's, was taken for an already-visited pipe and reported no inputs, so a correct bundle was refused with an extraneous-input error.
  • A bare reference into a package ignores its private pipes when an exported one matches: a consumer's alias->code that matches an exported pipe and a private pipe of the same code in another domain resolves to the exported one, where it was refused as ambiguous.
  • A dependency pipe that fails to build is refused naming why: a reference to a pipe the package declares but could not build, such as a PipeFunc naming an unregistered function, is refused with that build error, where it was reported as a pipe the package does not have. A bare alias->code matching such a pipe is refused the same way, rather than resolved to another pipe of that code.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Service error codes, contributed by the plugin that speaks to the service: a plugin declares each error code its gateway or hosted service emits on its own as a ServiceErrorCode, with its category, its user action, its advice and whether it means an unknown model, and hands them to PluginRegistrar.add_service_error_codes. classify_inference_error consults the booted plugins' codes ahead of the HTTP status ladder and render_inference_error renders the matched entry's advice; a code two plugins contribute fails the boot with DuplicateServiceErrorCodeError, and one the runtime classifies itself with ReservedServiceErrorCodeError.
  • Request extras on the Anthropic worker: AnthropicLLMWorker takes an optional extras_factory, the BackendExtrasFactory the OpenAI-substrate workers already take, whose headers and body additions join every text and structured call, and AnthropicFactory.make_anthropic_client takes an sdk_variant, so a plugin can register an sdk token of its own over the Anthropic protocol.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The completions image worker's fixed output format comes from its registration: OpenAICompletionsImgGenWorker takes fixed_output_format, the one image format a service answers in, rather than inferring it from the backend's name; a request for another format is refused before the call, and a URL answer from a worker built without one is refused as unreadable.
  • The Inference SPI table lists every symbol a provider plugin builds on: docs/under-the-hood/inference-backend-plugins.md now publishes, one module per row, the worker contracts with their jobs and outputs, the OpenAI- and Anthropic-protocol factories and workers, the image-generation and prompt-preparation helpers, the error pipeline and the runtime accessors, and parse_retry_after_seconds and error_code_from_body_code_first become public in pipelex.cogt.inference.error_classification for a plugin that distils a plain-HTTP failure itself.
  • The Anthropic worker no longer adds a backend's headers by backend name (Breaking): a worker built without an extras_factory sends nothing extra, whatever its backend, so a backend that relied on the worker adding its request headers must register its own sdk token with an extras factory and name that token in the sdk of its model specs, local overrides included; a model left on anthropic keeps answering, without those headers.
  • The gateway refusal families leave the core classifier (Breaking): GatewayRequestLimit, GatewayUnresolvedReference and GatewayRoutingRefusal, the matching properties of ProviderErrorMetadata and fields of ClassificationResult, and MANAGED_GATEWAY_BACKEND_NAMES are removed; a gateway's own codes now reach ClassificationResult.service_error_code through the plugin that contributes them, and Portkey's model_not_allowed_error is read by ProviderErrorMetadata.is_model_not_allowed and ClassificationResult.is_model_not_allowed. Errors raised by the hosted-only provider plugin now report the type and title of their generic family, such as extract-job-failure-error, rather than pages and titles of their own.
  • The default extractors run on your own keys (Breaking): @default-extract-document takes the first of Mistral OCR and pypdfium2-extract-pdf that an enabled backend serves, and @default-extract-image and @default-premium take Mistral OCR, where all three named Azure Document Intelligence, which no shipped backend serves any more. A PipeExtract step naming no model therefore runs on Mistral OCR with your own key or, for a PDF, on its text layer read locally, which recovers no text from a scanned page; a project's managed 3_extract_deck.toml takes the new aliases with pipelex update.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A Manifold failure on the extract and search routes reports the service's own message: extract_manifold_metadata takes the message from the response body's error.message, or else its top-level message, so a refused key now reads Portkey Error: Invalid API Key. Error Code: 03 rather than httpx's Client error '401 Unauthorized' for url …; a body carrying neither, a body that is not JSON and a network failure keep the exception's own text. Because the quota check reads that message, a 429 on those routes whose body names a quota, such as Monthly quota exceeded, now classifies as quota exhaustion, to be fixed in billing, rather than as a transient rate limit to retry.
  • A kernel-only boot over a stale configuration file stays kernel-only (Breaking): the boot-tolerance replay no longer loads interpreter modules into a RuntimeBoot process, because the fix-op applier, the file transaction and their errors moved from pipelex.pipeline to the new kernel-layer pipelex.fix_ops package; import FixWriteConflictError and FixTransactionError from pipelex.fix_ops.exceptions, and the applier and transaction from pipelex.fix_ops.applier and pipelex.fix_ops.file_transaction.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• The builder: pipelex-agent concept, pipelex-agent pipe, pipelex build runner and pipelex.builder (Breaking): the two agent commands that converted a JSON concept or pipe spec into MTHDS TOML, and pipelex build runner bundle and pipelex build runner method, which wrote a Python script running a pipe, are gone with the spec layer behind them, ConceptSpec, PipeSpec, PipelexBundleSpec and the ConceptSpecError, PipeSpecError and PipelexBundleSpecBlueprintError classes; write a method in MTHDS directly and check it with pipelex validate, and take a runner's typed structures from pipelex build structures or pipelex codegen types --target python-structures. The pipelex.builder package no longer exists: the modules the runtime still uses moved, pipelex.builder.conventions to pipelex.pipeline.default_file_names, pipelex.builder.operations.models_ops to pipelex.cogt.models.model_listing and pipelex.builder.operations.inputs_ops to pipelex.pipeline.inputs_template, and the others are deleted with the helpers only they used, force_include_dirs on pipelex.tools.misc.file_utils.find_files_in_dir among them, which only forced the builder package into library loading. The circular_dependency_error validation error type, which only the spec layer's pipe sorter raised, leaves the error_type registry and the API server's OpenAPI schema.
  • The Pipelex Gateway backend is gone from the runtime (Breaking): pipelex_gateway leaves the shipped backends.toml, its backends/pipelex_gateway.toml override file and the generated pipelex_gateway_models*.md references leave the kit, the all_pipelex_gateway routing profile is gone, and the pipelex-gateway provider plugin is deleted along with its gateway_* SDKs, its error classes and their docs pages. A backends.toml that still enables a [pipelex_gateway] table, as the previous release's kit did, is refused at boot, because an enabled backend whose file declares no model is now an error rather than a backend every routed model silently goes missing from: disable or remove the table, and move a routing profile naming it, the previous default all_pipelex_gateway included, to another backend. The shipped default routing profile is now all_enabled_backends, which needs no Pipelex account: it sends each model to the first enabled backend that serves it, in the order its fallback_order lists. pipelex init pre-selects OpenAI, whose one key serves every default language-model and image-generation tier of the shipped model deck, and no longer sets all_pipelex_gateway when several backends are chosen; pipelex-agent init given no backend list keeps the template's routing profile rather than demanding a primary_backend. The pipelex/pipelex-api image enables openai in its place and boots on OPENAI_API_KEY, which serves every default language-model and image-generation tier of its deck. Every bring-your-own-keys backend is untouched.
  • The Gateway terms of service and the first-run check are gone (Breaking): GatewayTermsNotAcceptedError, the [agreement] section of pipelex_service.toml, pipelex init agreement and the pipelex-agent accept-gateway-terms command are removed, and pipelex-agent init no longer reads accept_gateway_terms from its config. The check that stopped a live run on a Pipelex-managed backend until inference setup had been recorded is removed as well, with InferenceSetupRequiredError, its CLI handling and IntegrationMode.requires_terms_acceptance, so a server, a container or a test suite boots with no setup recorded at all.
  • The Pipelex-owned telemetry stream is gone (Breaking): the runtime no longer reports to Pipelex's PostHog on the Gateway's behalf, so GatewayApiKeyMissingError, GatewayDoNotTrackConflictError, GatewayTelemetryManagerInjectedError, TelemetryManagerAbstract.is_pipelex_telemetry_enabled, IntegrationMode.is_test_harness and the maintainer-only [pipelex_gateway] section of telemetry.toml (with its is_pipelex_gateway_portkey_* knobs) are removed; TelemetryFactory.make_telemetry_manager and TelemetryManager take only the user's telemetry_config. The user's own opt-in telemetry under [custom_posthog], [langfuse] and [[otlp]] is untouched. Migration: run pipelex migrate; ledger entry telemetry-config@3 deletes the [pipelex_gateway] table from every telemetry.toml and telemetry_*.toml file in ~/.pipelex/ and in each project .pipelex/, keeping one timestamped backup per file. Nothing else needs deciding, since the section only ever configured the stream that no longer exists.
  • pipelex login is gone (Breaking): it wrote a PIPELEX_GATEWAY_API_KEY that nothing reads any more, and it also leaves _CORE_COMMAND_ORDER and the setup-command set that skips the readiness check — an order list naming a command the CLI does not register makes pipelex --help itself exit non-zero. The credential flow for the hosted service is rebuilt separately.
  • The check-gateway-models and update-gateway-models dev commands are gone, with their make ugm / make cgm aliases and the ticc config-coverage target that ran the Gateway's Portkey configs.
  • The runtime no longer downloads a remote config, and the hosted-only inference backend is no longer shipped (Breaking): the boot fetches nothing, so PIPELEX_REMOTE_CONFIG_URL, the ~/.pipelex/cache/remote_config.json cache, the cache priming in pipelex init and pipelex-agent init, the remote fetch in pipelex doctor and make regenerate-test-models, and the RemoteConfigFetchError, RemoteConfigValidationError, RemoteConfigUnavailableError, GatewayUnknownModelError and GatewayConfigMergeError classes are gone, with the warnings array the agent CLI added to a success envelope for a stale cache. Every backend now reads its model specs from its own file under inference/backends/, so model_specs_section is no longer a backend setting, and the kit no longer ships the hosted-only backend's backends.toml table, its file under inference/backends/ or the routing profile that sent every model to it; a project config that still declares them keeps booting while that backend is disabled, since a disabled backend is skipped and only the active routing profile loads. An enabled backend whose backends.toml table still carries model_specs_section is refused at boot, naming the key: list its models in its backends/<name>.toml and remove the key, or disable it. pipelex_service.toml is retired with its PipelexServiceConfig and PipelexServiceError classes: pipelex-agent init no longer writes it or reports inference_setup_completed, cache_primed or cache_priming_error, and a copy an earlier release left behind is ignored, by pipelex migrate too. The needs_model_specs argument of Pipelex.make, which only chose whether to fetch, is removed.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
PipeJudge brings judgment into MTHDS methods: a step asks a model one closed question about its inputs and gets back a typed verdict with the probabilities behind it. A yes/no question returns a YesNo, a choice among declared options returns a Choice, and a position on a declared scale returns a Rating, so a PipeCondition can route on the verdict or gate a step on how sure the model was.

TypeSafe's Jev is the first judgment model Pipelex runs. Jev answers closed questions with calibrated probabilities rather than free text: install pipelex[typesafe], set TYPESAFE_API_KEY and name @default-judgment in the step.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• PipeJudge, an operator asking a judgment model one closed question about its inputs: a step declaring neither options nor levels asks a yes/no question, which may carry criteria and a threshold, and outputs a YesNo; one declaring options outputs a Choice; one declaring levels outputs a Rating, each verdict carrying the probabilities the model measured. Every declared input is sent to the model as material whether or not the question reads it, and prompt is read as a synonym of question. A step is refused when the method loads if it names no model while the deck names no default for judgments, if its output disagrees with its kind of question (Dynamic included), if an input name reaches into a field with a dot, or if it has an image or a document input its model does not read, and a document a run is given in a format its model does not read is refused before the run starts. The builder and pipelex-agent pipe write it with question, and the MTHDS Test Corpus gains operator_judge_urgent_message and the operator.judge tag.
  • A judgment inference family: a new family beside llm, img_gen, extract, search and doc_gen, for models that answer a closed-form question over some material — yes or no, one option out of a declared set, or a position on a declared scale — and report how sure they are. The worker contract is batch-shaped (one state, a map of questions, a map of answers), every measure of uncertainty is optional so a backend that measures none can still serve the family honestly, and usage is reported as real input and output tokens priced per million. A JudgmentJob and its JudgmentAssignment carry images and documents keyed by input name, which a scoped run's read authorization sees, and a judgment worker refuses files its model does not read with JudgmentCapabilityError before calling the provider. The deck gains a [judgment] section in a new managed file, 6_judgment_deck.toml, which pipelex update installs, and a deck installed before it keeps loading with no judgment model; it ships with no choice_default, because the family's models come with your own key and a default the Pipelex Gateway does not serve would fail every boot, so a judgment names its own model. pipelex-agent models lists the new category, and so does the MTHDS protocol's model list, GET /v1/models on the API server, where a judgment preset is an entry typed judgment and ?type=judgment filters on it; a judgment pytest marker joins the inference markers.
  • TypeSafe, the judgment family's first backend: a built-in typesafe plugin, installed with the new pipelex[typesafe] extra, serves the family from TypeSafe's System One API and is reachable as @default-judgment, pinned to the versioned model jev-1.13.0. Set TYPESAFE_API_KEY to use it: the default routing profile sends jev-* models to the backend whenever it is enabled, because the Pipelex Gateway does not serve them. A rating scale longer than ten levels is refused by this backend before any request is made, and a response answered by a model other than the pinned one is reported as a warning.
  • Log sink settings can name secrets: the values of headers under [runtime.log.otlp] and credentials_file_path under [runtime.log.gcp] accept the ${…} placeholders the inference backends use, resolved through the configured secrets provider, so a collector's token is written "Bearer ${OTLP_AUTH_TOKEN}" and the key path "${GCP_CREDENTIALS_FILE_PATH}". The configuration keeps the placeholders, and one that does not resolve stops the boot with LogSinkVariableError naming the section, the key and the variable. A header value that holds a line break once resolved, as a secret read from a file often does, stops the boot with LogSinkHeaderValueError rather than installing an exporter that refuses every batch. pipelex doctor gains a Secrets Provider row, checks.secrets_provider in pipelex-agent doctor.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• mthds version, MTHDS protocol 0.7.0 and standard 3.0.0 (Breaking): the pin moves to mthds==0.19.0, which carries protocol 0.7.0, whose model list adds the judgment category beside llm, extract, img_gen and search, so the runner and GET /v1/version report protocol_version 0.7.0, and which implements MTHDS standard 3.0.0. A crate pipelex normalizes is stamped mthds_version 3.0.0, and a METHODS.toml declaring mthds_version = "^2.0.0" now warns that the engine does not satisfy it. PipelexModelDeck inherits the release's open ModelInfo.type, typed ModelCategory | str | None, though pipelex itself only ever emits a protocol category; everyone downstream inherits that exact mthds.
  • The native concepts are pinned at MTHDS 3.0.0: YesNo gains a probability, and Choice and Rating are added (Breaking): YesNo carries an optional probability, which a PipeLLM whose output is YesNo may fill with the model's own estimate; Choice (an option key, with optional confidence and probabilities) and Rating (a level index, with optional confidence, probabilities and position) are new natives, so a bundle declaring a concept named Choice or Rating must rename it. A YesNo written to the wire carries "probability": null when none was reported, the output-form descriptor states a YesNo result as an object carrying yes_no and probability while an input stays a bare boolean, and a crate's normalized fingerprint changes wherever it materializes YesNo. Python callers read the new verdicts with main_stuff_as_choice and main_stuff_as_rating. Every measure is a strict number, so a boolean or a numeric string is refused rather than read as 1.0 or 0.9; and a PipeDocGen office template or auto-layout sees a verdict as its verdict alone, while a pdf template reads it whole.
  • The method-app template and the SDK references link Pipelex/pipelex-sdk: the SDKs and the method-app templates now live in the Pipelex/pipelex-sdk repository, so the README and the documentation's Quick Start link the method-app template to its method-apps/ directory, the webapp's by-hand commands clone it and copy method-apps/webapp-js/, and the @pipelex/sdk and pipelex-sdk references point at its js/docs/ and python/docs/ directories.
  • Boot builds the secrets provider before the log sink, and a sink factory receives it (Breaking): a LogSinkFactoryFn is now called as factory(log_config, secrets_provider=…), and the plugin API version moves to 5, so a plugin declaring targets_api = 4 is refused at discovery and is rebuilt against this release. A secrets provider that fails to build now reports on stderr, redacted, rather than through the configured sink.
  • pipelex-agent inputs names the pipe pipe_ref, qualified (Breaking): the JSON success envelope of inputs bundle, inputs pipe and inputs method is {success, pipe_ref, inputs}, as mthds-agent prints on the API runner, where it was pipe_code. The value is the qualified domain.pipe_code of the pipe that was resolved, so a bare --pipe summarize answers doc.summarize and a dependency pipe keeps its alias-> prefix, and a pipe that declares no inputs names its pipe too, where it printed null when --pipe was omitted, and no longer adds a message key. That pipe's message, the TOML comment here and the line pipelex build inputs and pipelex codegen inputs print, now reads Pipe '<pipe_ref>' declares no inputs.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• An image worker refusing a model's spec reports a configuration fault: a worker refused a model with no rules, no model_choice or endpoint_path where it needs one, or on the Google Gemini paths an aspect_ratio taxonomy that is missing, unknown to this release or of another family, with ImgGenParameterError in the content category, so a server answered 422 and told the caller to change their input; and a rule value this release does not know escaped the OpenAI, Azure, fal, Hugging Face and gateway image workers as a bare ValueError. Each now raises ImgGenParameterError in the configuration category, naming the model, and answers 500, while a ratio or size the model's grid refuses is still the caller's 422.
  • A bare value is refused where it reads as a concept the input does not accept (Breaking): an input declared as a container native (Html, Page, TextAndImages, SearchResult, Composite), as Choice or Rating, or as a concept refining one, built a bare string as a native.Text and handed that text on, so the step reading the input met a text where it declared another concept. The value is now refused with StructureValidationError naming the concept it read as; send it in its {concept, content} envelope. The concept's own content sent without that envelope, such as {"choice": "billing"}, is refused with the same advice, where it was told to redeclare the input as JSON, and so is a bare number or boolean at a Rating or Choice input, such as a level 2 sent alone, where it was told to redeclare the input as Anything. A Dynamic input still keeps whatever its value reads as.
  • A name a template sets is read where Jinja binds it (Breaking): the input check of PipeLLM, PipeCompose, PipeSearch, PipeImgGen and PipeDocGen, PipeDocGen's field check and the optional-input guard now treat a {% set %} name as the template's own inside the loop, macro or block that sets it and after an {% if %} every branch of which sets it, so a template setting a name in a loop body or in each branch of an if and reading it there is no longer refused as reading an undeclared input. A name only some branches set is still read from the input of that name. Newly refused: an input declared only so that such a set would load, which is now never read, a macro called before its {% macro %}, an optional input read unguarded in a macro argument's default, and a name a loop or a macro binds read inside a {% block %} without scoped, which Jinja reads from the input of that name.
  • File inputs are checked against the models that read them (Breaking): run setup now identifies every image and document input from its first bytes, refuses an Image input holding something other than an image with PipelineInputNotAnImageError, and refuses a document certain to reach a PipeExtract or PipeLLM step whose model does not read its format with PipelineInputFormatUnsupportedError, both 422 input errors naming the input, the step, the model and the formats it reads; a step reached only through a condition refuses the file itself with ExtractInputFormatError or PromptDocumentFormatError. A PipeLLM document its model does not read now raises PromptDocumentFormatError where it raised LLMCapabilityError, so a consumer branching on error_type must follow. docling-extract-text now declares the Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML, Markdown, CSV, plain-text, WebVTT and email files it already extracted, which pipelex update installs.
  • Markdown with unclosed emphasis is converted in memory proportional to its length: the Markdown parser behind the markdown filter, the Markdown concept's HTML and the built-in PDF engine held memory growing with the square of the text when emphasis or strikethrough markers were left unmatched, about 1.5 GB for 64,000 characters of **a; it now joins the text they leave behind in one pass, and renders the same HTML.
  • Routing profiles no longer rewrite their own routes: matching a model merged the enabled optional_routes into the profile's declared routes in place, so after the first match a route declared optional had become an unconditional one in the loaded profile. Only the enablement checks each match repeats kept that from changing a routing decision.
  • The logging documentation no longer promises that a server refuses the console sink: the log-sink, logging, logging-configuration and Rich-imports pages said a server installed without the cli extra stops at boot when it selects the console sink or the rich pretty-print mode. The core dependencies typer and instructor install Rich anyway, so such a server boots on the Rich surface; the pages now say a server selects json and a Rich-free mode in its own configuration, since nothing at boot makes that choice for it.
  • pipelex doctor checks the backends against the configured secrets provider: the backend-file probe and the Models row resolved credentials from environment variables whatever [runtime.secrets] method selected, so a deployment on another secrets method was diagnosed against secrets it does not use. Both now use the provider the configuration selects, and say they could not run when it does not build; a provider that raises on a lookup, an unreachable vault or a missing SDK, is reported in the Models row rather than stopping the doctor.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • The API server's /v1/build/* routes (Breaking): pipelex-api no longer serves POST /v1/build/inputs, /v1/build/output, /v1/build/runner, /v1/build/concept or /v1/build/pipe-spec, which now answer 404, and the MAX_AGENT_SPEC_KIB setting that bounded the last two is gone. A client reads a pipe's I/O from POST /v1/pipe-io and projects an inputs template from its input_form with the mthds packages' projection (renderInputsTemplate, which @pipelex/sdk re-exports, or mthds.protocol.inputs_template in Python), as mthds-agent inputs does; the output representation, the runner script and the concept and pipe spec conversions have no HTTP replacement.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Every template render spends from a budget (Breaking): a render is charged for what it reads, allocates and prints, and an operation that would overdraw its budget, such as 'x' * 10 ** 9, a huge format width, lipsum(n=10 ** 9), nested empty loops or a runaway recursive macro, is refused before it allocates and raises Jinja2TemplateBudgetError. Converting Markdown to HTML, with the markdown filter or by printing a Markdown value in an HTML template, is charged for every character and table cell of its source, so one render converts at most about 65,000 characters of Markdown. Template arithmetic stops at 64-bit integers, and a template can no longer call str.encode or int.to_bytes. A filter or test registered on a template environment needs a cost in the render budget's tables, or the first compile raises a TypeError naming it, and Pipelex now requires jinja2 below 3.2.
  • pipelex doctor redacts the failures its rows quote: the log-sink row printed a sink's failure as raised, so a credential an exporter or a client quoted in its error reached the terminal and the JSON of pipelex-agent doctor. That row, the new Secrets Provider row and the Models row, which quotes a secrets provider's own text when a backend's credential does not resolve, now scrub the text with the patterns the log redaction uses, the configured extra_patterns included.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • A symlink in a fetched package is a 422 on the API server: MethodPackageSymlinkError, raised when a package fetched by method_ref carries a symlink, is now answered as a 422 the method's author can act on, where it was a 500 server fault.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • Locating a fetched package never follows a symlinked METHODS.toml: when pipelex run <address>, fetch-on-miss or the API server's method_ref scans a fetched repository for its packages, a METHODS.toml that is a symlink, or is not a regular file, is now skipped and reported without being opened. A repository could commit one linking to a file on the fetching machine and get that file's values back in the error message, even under strict error disclosure, or link it to /dev/zero and make the read run without end. The read now also stops at the manifest size ceiling whatever size the file reports, and a manifest that is not valid UTF-8, or a directory named METHODS.toml, is skipped and reported instead of failing the whole fetch.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text: The Pipelex API server and its pipelex/pipelex-api image now ship from the pipelex repository, so they take pipelex's version number. The image's last standalone release was 0.33.2, on the server's own release line, and its next tag is 0.71.0, the same version as the pipelex and pipelex-api packages published beside it.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• PipeDocGen generates a document file: a new operator turns its inputs into a stored Document named by its filename expression, which pipelex run copies into the run's results folder. A pdf without a template is printed by a built-in engine on ReportLab from the auto-layout of the inputs, and a pdf with an HTML template or any xlsx, docx or pptx step is refused when the method loads, with an error naming the Pipelex document generation plugin. A template's field paths are checked against the inputs' concepts at load, and its templates and filename render strictly, so a missing value fails instead of printing as empty text.
  • Document engines are models: the engine that prints a PipeDocGen step is a model of a new doc_gen family, which a step names with model = "pipelex-pdf" or leaves to the default for its format and source in the new deck file 5_doc_gen_deck.toml, and whose worker a plugin registers with add_inference_backend(family=InferenceFamily.DOC_GEN, …), declaring its model with add_internal_model and its deck defaults with add_doc_gen_default. A step whose engine is not in the deck, does not print its format from its source, or has no installed worker is refused when the method loads, so a runtime that disables the built-in reportlab plugin in [runtime.plugins] disabled refuses every PipeDocGen step. An engine receives a RenderJob of plain data, reads the files its document names through RenderResources under the run's read scope, and may check a step's template file at the dry run. pipelex update now also refreshes backends/internal.toml, backing up a locally edited copy first, so run it to get the deck file and the built-in reportlab-pdf engine.
  • The markdown template filter: an HTML template turns Markdown held in a text field into HTML with {{ order.notes | markdown }}. Raw HTML in the source is shown as text, and only URLs with a scheme become links.
  • The Markdown native concept: Markdown refines Text and holds a text written in Markdown, which a PipeLLM with output = "Markdown" writes as free text and a Markdown input takes as a string or as {"concept": "Markdown", "content": "…"}; Pipelex defines it ahead of the MTHDS standard. A Markdown value is accepted wherever a Text is, while a Text, or any concept refining Text, is refused where a Markdown is required. pipelex run --save-main-stuff saves it verbatim as main_stuff.md, an HTML template prints {{ report }} and $report as HTML with raw HTML escaped, and Stuff.as_markdown and PipeOutput.main_stuff_as_markdown read it from Python.
  • The Pipelex API server ships with pipelex: the FastAPI runner now lives in the api/ directory, as the pipelex-api member of a uv workspace, and runs the pipelex of the same commit instead of a pinned release. Every release publishes it under pipelex's version, as the new pipelex-api package on PyPI, which pins pipelex to that same version, and as the pipelex/pipelex-api image on Docker Hub, whose tag therefore jumps from 0.33.2, the server's last release on its own, to this version. The image keeps its name, its port and its /root/.pipelex configuration mount, and Pipelex/pipelex-api keeps the server's earlier history.
  • x-pipelex-metadata header on Pipelex Manifold calls: every inference request the Manifold backend makes (chat completions, responses, image generation, extraction, search, and Claude over the Anthropic SDK) carries one JSON header holding the run's extras as they are, plus the run's user_id and pipeline_run_id and the step's pipe_run_id, pipe_code and content_generation_job_id when set, so the service can attribute each call's spend and log it. On a key collision the run's own id wins over the extras entry, and no other backend receives the header.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Markdown is a reserved native concept code (Breaking): a bundle declaring its own concept named Markdown is refused with native_concept_redeclaration; rename it, or use the native.
  • A string under a concept refining Text keeps the concept's class: a bare string or a {"concept": …, "content": "…"} envelope for such a concept now holds the concept's own content class where it held a plain TextContent, as the YesNo, Date and Time envelopes already did.
  • markdown-it-py replaces markdown in the dependencies: the markdown package, which pipelex no longer imported, is dropped, and markdown-it-py with its linkify extra renders the Markdown of PipeDocGen, the markdown filter and the Markdown concept.
  • The API server's import package is pipelex_api (Breaking): the server's package api is renamed pipelex_api, so an application wrapping the server imports pipelex_api.main and serves pipelex_api.main:app, and the logger field of the server's log records reads pipelex_api.….
  • The API server's documentation is part of docs.pipelex.com: its pages are the API Server section of the Pipelex documentation, versioned with each release, in place of the separate site at pipelex.github.io/pipelex-api, and the committed OpenAPI artifact is published beside them as api-server/openapi/pipelex-api.openapi.yaml.
  • The API image is built from the pipelex repository: docker build -f api/Dockerfile . at the repository root installs pipelex and pipelex-api from that commit, with the dependency versions of the repository's lock, which moves some provider SDKs to the versions pipelex is tested with. The container starts uvicorn from its virtual environment rather than through uv run, and carries no uv.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The API server refuses a deeply nested body the same way on every Python: a JSON request body whose arrays and objects nest deeper than 128 levels, its own envelope included, is now refused before it is parsed, on every route that takes one, with a 422 InvalidJSON saying it is nested too deeply. On Python 3.14 whether the run routes refused such a body depended on the size of the thread's stack, so it could reach validation and fail as a ValidationError or be accepted, and the other routes answered it with a bare 400 rather than a problem document.
  • A client leaving mid-upload is a 400 in the API server's logs: when a client disconnects before its request body arrived in full, the server answers a 400 BadRequest and logs it at warning level, where the run routes logged a 500 server fault with a traceback.
  • The API image runs methods by address: the image carries git, which fetching a method named by method_ref needs, where the 0.33.2 image removed it with the build tools and failed every such run.
  • A workflow action the organization does not allow is caught on its pull request: GitHub rejects a whole workflow at startup when one of its actions is outside the organization's Actions policy, and pull-request CI never loads the release workflows, so such an action surfaced only as a release that published nothing. make check-actions-allowlist (alias caa), which make agent-check and the Lint (actions allowlist) CI job run, now refuses any workflow action outside the policy mirrored in .github/actions-allowlist.toml; see Actions Allowlist.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text: This release hardens pipelex for running methods it did not write. Every template now renders in Jinja's sandbox, a run with a read scope reads only under that scope and never the local disk, a URL fetch refuses private and metadata addresses, and a sandbox-hosted load no longer imports a method's Python into the loading process. Validation gets stricter too: PipeCompose, PipeSearch and PipeImgGen refuse an input their templates never read, and a concept whose field names a concept nobody declares is refused at load.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• read_scope is a required run parameter (Breaking): RunMetadata, pipeline_run_setup, prepare_pipe_job, PipelexKernel.make, shape_inputs, InputShaper.shape, WorkingMemoryFactory.make_from_pipeline_inputs, StuffFactory.make_stuff_from_stuff_content_or_data, normalize_data_urls_to_storage and the runtime bridge's PipelexPipeRunInput take a read_scope with no default: a host serving several tenants passes the tenant's prefix, which must contain the run's storage_scope, and None states that the run is unscoped. PipelexMTHDSProtocol defaults it to None, which is the truth on a laptop.
  • Dry-run mocks of images and documents carry readable URLs: a mocked ImageContent carries one of inference.dry_run.image_urls and a mocked DocumentContent a blank one-page PDF as a data: URL, where both carried a random string that reads as a local path; and a model nested two levels or more inside a mocked structure now gets the same field providers as a shallower one.
  • A structure field naming a concept that cannot be found refuses the load (Breaking): a concept whose field names a concept that no bundle it can see declares now raises LibraryLoadingError at load, naming the concept, its bundle and the missing structure class, where it loaded and failed with pydantic's "not fully defined" error at first use. A concept declared only by a bundle loaded afterwards cannot be found either. load_from_crate does not refuse, since a crate carries no dependency package, and neither does a method package's own load, since its own dependencies are never loaded; a concept holding a method package's concept left incomplete that way is not refused either.
  • PipeCompose, PipeSearch and PipeImgGen refuse an input they never read (Breaking): as PipeLLM already did, validation refuses a declared input that none of the pipe's templates reads (the template or the construct of a PipeCompose, the prompt of a PipeSearch, the prompt or negative prompt of a PipeImgGen) as extraneous_input_variable, naming the input: reference it in a template, or remove it from inputs. A variable a PipeImgGen's negative_prompt reads without declaring it is refused when the bundle is parsed, and UnusedInputError, which nothing raised, is removed.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Concepts holding other concepts are complete: a method package's concept holding another of the package's concepts, a field typed by a method package's concept (address->domain.Concept), a field typed by a concept that an earlier load put into the same library, a field typed by a concept backed by a Python class (structure = "ClassName"), and a field typed native.Anything, which holds any value, now resolve, where each loaded and failed with pydantic's "not fully defined" error at first use. A method package whose concepts form a cycle is refused as a bundle's own concepts are, naming the package's bundle.
  • The input errors of the template operators carry their type and names: a missing or unread input of a PipeLLM, PipeCompose, PipeSearch or PipeImgGen is reported with its error_type and with variable_names holding the plain names, sorted. A PipeCompose template reading an undeclared variable was an uncategorized item, the PipeSearch and PipeImgGen items carried no names, and PipeLLM's unread names arrived quoted ('platform').
  • A template read through a subscript, a call or a set counts as a read: an input a template reads only as {{ items[0].text }}, {{ (items|first).text }} or {{ record['meta'].title }}, or reassigns with {% set topic = topic|trim %}, is seen as read, where PipeLLM refused it as unread, and such a read of an undeclared variable is refused as missing. A read placed before a top-level {% set %} of the same name, and a for loop's iterable or else branch, read the input. The name a top-level {% set %}…{% endset %} block assigns, a call to one of Jinja's globals such as range(count) or namespace(), and caller, varargs and kwargs inside a macro are no longer demanded as inputs, while an input named like a global, such as range, is read wherever the template reads the name without calling it. The images and documents PipeLLM attaches, and the reference images PipeImgGen attaches, are found under the same scopes, so an image read after {% set image = image %} or as the iterable of a loop named after it is attached.
  • A generated object's storage key names its own format: the extension of a key under generated/ follows the whole MIME type the object is stored under, so a fetched image/svg+xml is stored as .svg, and a type with no extension of its own gets .bin, where both used to get .jpg. The MIME type's parameters and case no longer change the extension.
  • An include in a method template is a render error: {% include %}, {% extends %} and {% import %} in a template rendered without a loader raise Jinja2TemplateRenderError, where they leaked Jinja's own TemplateNotFound.
  • A template reads a Composite's parts by name: {{ combo.summary }}, {{ combo['summary'] }} and combo.get('summary') resolve the named parts of a Composite output, and iter_keys lists them; they used to render empty, and only the raw _content, now refused, reached them. Like any private name, a part whose name starts with an underscore is refused when a template reads it on an input.
  • A template's arithmetic error is a render error: a division by zero, or a range longer than the sandbox's cap, raises Jinja2TemplateRenderError where the raw Python exception escaped, which validation reported as an internal error rather than as the method's.
  • A sandboxed PipeFunc's imports resolve to the same file in every process: the sandbox searches a method's root directory first and then its subdirectories in sorted order, where the order followed the hash of their paths, which changes from one process to the next. A module name used in two directories of a method, such as a structures.py shipped in a subdirectory beside the structures module the sandbox generates at the root, could resolve to either file. A temporary directory reached through a symlink, as on macOS, no longer lets a file's own directory jump ahead of that order or stay on sys.path after the run.
  • Docling extracts HTML, Markdown and CSV: a document Docling reads without pages (HTML, Markdown, CSV, AsciiDoc) comes back as one page holding the whole document, where it came back with no pages and no text, and one given as a storage key or a data: URL reaches Docling, where its bytes were refused as an unknown file type.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Every template renders in a sandbox (Breaking): prompts, compose and construct templates, image and search prompts and condition expressions may read data and call methods of plain values (strings, numbers, dates, containers) only, so a template that reaches for a Python internal, calls a method of a Pipelex or pydantic object, or reads a name starting with an underscore other than an input's _stuff_name, _content_class, _concept_code and _stuff_code raises Jinja2TemplateSecurityError instead of rendering, and validation refuses the visible cases with the new template_private_name error. _content and the stuff property are no longer readable on an input, and bracket access and get on an input resolve only its content fields and metadata fields; a plain dict's keys stay readable with brackets, record['_id'] included, and a namespace() holds data only, refusing a callable. The jinja2 floor rises to 3.1.6, the release carrying Jinja's own sandbox fix for the attr filter.
  • Dotted paths refuse underscore segments: a PipeCompose construct from path such as note.__class__.__init__.__globals__.sys.modules.os.environ walked into Python internals with plain getattr and could copy the process environment into a method's output. A from path or list_to_dict_keyed_by name with a segment starting with an underscore is now refused at validation, and every dotted path the runtime walks, batch lists and prompt image references included, refuses one.
  • A scoped run reads only under its read scope, and never the local disk: on a run with a read scope, a pipelex-storage:// key is read only when it lies under that scope, compared segment by segment, and a bare path or a file:// URI is never read, whichever value carries it — an input, a PipeCompose construct that assembles a URL from text, a model's structured output. Every content-generation leaf checks the URLs it will read before the dry-run branch, and the input seam checks a CSV input and every file it would upload or sign; a refused read raises UriReadRefusedError, answered as a 422, which names where the URL sat without quoting it. A run whose read scope is None reads as before.
  • A sandbox-hosted load imports no method Python, and refuses structure classes (Breaking): on a deployment whose PipeFunc execution mode is not direct, loading a library directory captures every .py file as source for the sandbox and imports none of them, where a file declaring a StructuredContent subclass was imported into the loading process and its module-level code ran. A load whose Python declares such a class, however the method arrived, now raises MethodStructuresRefusedError naming each file and class by its relative path, the error a fetched package already got: declare the types as MTHDS concepts with inline structures, which a PipeFunc imports in the sandbox from the generated structures module. The module pipelex build structures writes is accepted while it is left as generated, by this refusal and by the fetched-package one, and is not sent to the sandbox, which generates its own from the same concepts. Both refusals, and the local warnings that predict them, now give that same route. A direct load is unchanged.
  • Fetching a URL refuses private destinations (Breaking): every download of a URL a value carries — a prompt image or document for a provider that does not take URLs, a document to extract or render, a generated image a provider returned as a link — now refuses a host that is localhost, a cloud metadata alias or resolves to any private, loopback, link-local or metadata address, on the first request and on every redirect hop, raising SsrfBlockedError and failing the pipe, where it followed redirects anywhere and returned the body. The guarded fetch connects directly and ignores HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY; a self-hosted deployment that reads documents from an intranet host or reaches the internet through a proxy sets the new [runtime.network] is_fetch_ssrf_guard_enabled = false. make_base64_url_from_any_uri and make_base64_url_from_http_url move to pipelex.tools.uri.uri_base64.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text: Structured output moves to instructor 1.17, and the provider SDKs move with it. The mistralai extra takes mistralai 2.x, and the Bedrock and S3 extras take aiobotocore in place of aioboto3, which renames the bedrock_aioboto3 SDK handle to bedrock_aioboto. Structured output on the google backend now accepts enum fields and sends the system prompt, the temperature and the token limit.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• A bare string at an Anything input is an Anything value (Breaking): it becomes a native.Anything stuff holding text, where it used to become a native.Text stuff.
  • A JSON input reads a JSON object literally (Breaking): a bare string at a JSON input is refused instead of becoming native.Text, the compact inputs template of a JSON input is the bare object rather than the envelope {"concept": "native.JSON", "content": {"json_obj": …}}, and a JSONContent holding a value JSON cannot encode, such as a date or a set, raises a pydantic ValidationError instead of a TypeError.
  • An envelope-shaped item of a bare Anything[] or JSON[] list is refused (Breaking): an item holding concept and content keys is no longer read as data; wrap the whole list in one envelope to type it.
  • A value the fallback has no reading for is a StructureValidationError (Breaking): at a Dynamic or container-native input, a bare value the bottom-up reading cannot build, such as a list of plain objects, raises StructureValidationError naming the input and its concept instead of an unnamed StuffFactoryError, and its next step names the declaration that reads the value (JSON, JSON[], Anything or Anything[]) when one does.
  • An explicit single value at a fixed-count input is refused (Breaking): an envelope holding one value at a Concept[N] input raises MultiplicityCountMismatchError instead of being stored as a single value.
  • NaN and the infinities are refused at Number, JSON and Anything inputs (Breaking): a TOML inputs file can spell nan and inf, which JSON cannot hold, so a Number or Anything input given one raises WrongScalarKindError, and an object holding one anywhere inside it raises StructureValidationError, where each used to store a number that JSON serialization turns into null. A JSONContent or a NumberContent holding one raises a pydantic ValidationError, which is also what an explicit envelope building one reports.
  • Chaining an Anything value through --with-memory changes it (Breaking): an Anything stuff's content is dumped as its content class's fields, so a bare "hi" sent to an Anything input is dumped as {"text": "hi"}, and a method reading that memory at an Anything input receives that object rather than the string; a list is dumped as one object holding its items. It used to travel as native.Text, since a bare string at an Anything input became a native.Text stuff.
  • The Anything input schema excludes array and null: the JSON Schema published for an Anything input carries "not": {"type": ["array", "null"]}, and so does each item of an Anything[] input's schema.
  • aiobotocore replaces aioboto3, and the bedrock_aioboto3 SDK handle is renamed bedrock_aioboto (Breaking): the bedrock and s3 extras depend on aiobotocore 3.x instead of aioboto3, whose latest release pins boto3 below 1.40.62, so both extras now take boto3>=1.42.42. The new handle names the async Bedrock client rather than the library under it, so a later change of library will not rename it again. Migration: a backend file that still sets sdk = "bedrock_aioboto3" keeps loading but fails on every call to its models, with an error that points at pipelex migrate, which names each such file under inference-backend@3 without rewriting it, so replace the handle with bedrock_aioboto by hand.
  • instructor 1.17, and the mistralai extra on mistralai 2.x (Breaking): pipelex now requires instructor>=1.17.0,<2.0.0, and the mistralai extra takes mistralai>=2.10.0, whose client lives under mistralai.client, so a project that imports mistralai 1.x beside pipelex must move to 2.x with it. instructor 1.17 dropped its strict tool mode, so the instructor/openai_structured_outputs structure method now sends the same non-strict tool schema as instructor/openai_tools, and OpenAI no longer enforces the schema on its side: pipelex still validates the response and re-asks on a mismatch.
  • opentelemetry-api and opentelemetry-sdk 1.39 or later: pipelex now requires both at >=1.39.0 instead of >=1.38.0.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Anything inputs take any JSON value: a string, a number, a boolean, an object or a date at an Anything input becomes its natural content under the Anything concept, Anything[] takes a list of them, a prebuilt list mixing contents of different kinds included, and a typed envelope keeps its own concept; they used to be refused, a bare string aside. A sequence declaring an Anything output over a narrower last step now validates.
  • JSON inputs take objects and lists of objects: a JSON object at a JSON input, and a list of them at a JSON[] input, now build, where a list of plain objects used to be refused with an error naming neither the input nor its concept.
  • A single Anything value survives the transport boundary: a stuff whose concept is native.Anything keeps its content's class through dump_for_transport and hydration, which a distributed or sandboxed run relies on; hydration used to fail looking for an AnythingContent class.
  • A composite nested in an Anything value or in another composite survives transport: its components, a nested composite and a list of composites included, come back through hydration as typed contents, where they came back as dicts carrying class markers.
  • The result files of an Anything output render its value: a delivery whose main output is Anything renders main_stuff.json, .md and .html from the hydrated content, where it fell back to a raw dump of the transport form.
  • A prebuilt list is refused where one value belongs: a ListContent given as an item of a plural input, or as the content of an Anything envelope at a single input, is refused instead of being stored nested or in a singular slot.
  • bedrock_anthropic models run with AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK set: under bedrock_access_variant = "aws_access", the default, Anthropic models on Bedrock sign their requests with the configured AWS access keys and ignore a Bedrock bearer token in the environment, where every one of them used to fail at client construction with a raw ValueError. When the access keys are missing and the environment carries such a token, the AwsCredentialsError now says so and names bedrock_access_variant = "bedrock_token" as the way to authenticate with a bearer token.
  • Structured output on the google backend accepts enum fields: under instructor/genai_tools, instructor validated Gemini's function-call arguments strictly and refused a string for any enum field, so every schema with an enum failed on every attempt; those arguments are now validated in lax mode, so a google.toml an earlier pipelex init copied keeps working unchanged. The backend file we ship now sets structure_method = "instructor/genai_structured_outputs", Gemini's native JSON output.
  • Structured output on the google backend sends the system prompt, temperature and token limit: instructor ignored the Google config pipelex handed it, so every structured call ran with no system prompt, the default temperature and the model's default output token limit, whichever structure method the backend used; they now reach Gemini.
  • A transport error inside a structured-output call is classified again under instructor 1.15.3 and later: those releases wrap a provider's rate limit, timeout or refused connection in their own retry exception, which pipelex classified as an unknown error, or after a re-ask as the earlier parse failure; the provider's error is now read first, so it keeps its category, its retryability and its provider metadata.
  • A gateway that does not allow the model asks for another model: the inference gateway's model_not_allowed_error refusal (HTTP 412) now reads as a configuration error whose change_model action names the model handle and says who settles a model deck that lists a model the gateway refuses, where it said to review the prompt, parameters and inputs. The HTTP status stays 500.
  • A structured-output call is re-asked when the model returns no tool call or no JSON: under instructor 1.16 and later such a response raises a parse error that pipelex's re-ask loop did not retry, so it failed at once; the loop now retries exactly the parse errors instructor itself re-asks.
  • A model whose structure_method names a provider-specific instructor mode sets up again: instructor 1.17 refuses another provider's mode on an OpenAI-compatible client, which failed the setup of such a model, the gateway's mistral-large among them; each structure method now builds with the core mode instructor itself resolves it to.
  • Mistral OCR on an image returns the figures it finds: an extract from an image, rather than a document, failed with MistralExtractResponseError whenever Mistral OCR detected a figure inside it, because the request never asked for the figures' pixels; it now sends the same image options as a document extract, so max_nb_images and image_min_size apply to images too, and a request for captions, which Mistral OCR cannot write, is refused on an image as it already was on a document instead of returning none.
  • A no-op tracer no longer stamps a fake Pipelex span on log lines: from opentelemetry-api 1.40, the no-op tracer OTEL_SDK_DISABLED hands out returns its parent instead of an invalid span, so every line of a run carried pipelex.trace_id and a pipelex.span_id of 0000000000000001 naming no span; a pipe or an LLM call now starts no span under such a tracer, as with no tracer at all.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • pipelex.providers.openai.openai_func (Breaking): the module and its create_pydantic_model_from_function, create_openai_schema_from_function and list_openai_tools helpers are removed; nothing in pipelex called them.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text: Every log line can be joined to its run and to your own traces. A run driven through the kernel, each kernel step and a run dispatched to a distributed orchestrator's workers now stamp request_id, pipeline_run_id and pipe_run_id on their lines as an interpreted run does, and a host passes the inbound request id it filters its logs on. A line's standard trace fields now name your process's current OpenTelemetry span, with Pipelex's own span beside them under pipelex.*, and the gcp sink refuses to boot on credentials Google rejects instead of losing every record in silence.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• PipelexKernel.log_context() and JobMetadata.log_context(): JobMetadata.log_context() binds a job's request_id, pipeline_run_id and pipe_run_id onto the log context in one call, and PipelexKernel.log_context() binds a kernel run's request_id and pipeline_run_id, which a host wraps its run in so the lines it emits between kernel calls name the run.
  • PipelexKernel.make takes request_id and pipeline_run_id: a kernel-driven run can now carry the inbound request id a hosted deployment filters its logs on, and name itself with an id the host chooses. A host inside a replay-based executor passes a pipeline_run_id or a trace context, since the default uuid4 changes on every replay; a trace context and a pipeline_run_id that disagree, or an empty pipeline_run_id, raise ValueError.
  • PipelexMTHDSProtocol.execute takes request_id: a host running execute passes the inbound request id, which the run's RunMetadata carries, so the log lines of a run dispatched to a distributed orchestrator's workers carry request_id as a direct run's do. A value that is not one to 128 printable ASCII characters is refused with a ValueError before the run is set up, where it used to surface as a PipeExecutionError blaming the caller's input; the constraint is stated once, as validate_request_id in pipelex.system.job_metadata, which RunMetadata applies too.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The gcp log sink stops the boot when Google refuses its credentials (Breaking): the sink refreshes its credentials once when it is built, within five seconds, and credentials Google refuses (a revoked or expired refresh token, a deleted service-account key, a Google Cloud machine with no service account) or that cannot be loaded (no Application Default Credentials, a key file that is missing or holds no valid key) raise the new GcpLogSinkCredentialsError, a config-domain CredentialsError naming the credentials, Google's answer and what renews them, which pipelex doctor reports in its log-sink row. Such a process used to boot and lose every record in silence, since over gRPC the failed refresh is retried for a minute before anything reports it; a refresh that cannot reach the token endpoint or the metadata server, gets an answer that says to retry (a 5xx, 408 or 429), or does not answer in time, is said on stderr and the boot goes on.
  • A log line's standard trace fields name OpenTelemetry's current span, and the Pipelex span rides under pipelex.* (Breaking): in the json, otlp and gcp sinks, trace_id, span_id and trace_flags (the otlp record's own trace context, the gcp entry's trace) now always name your process's current span and are absent when there is none, inside a Pipelex run too, where they used to name the pipe's or the LLM call's span; that span is written beside them as pipelex.trace_id and pipelex.span_id, keys in the json line and the gcp payload and attributes on the otlp record, reserved on every line like the sinks' other keys. The gcp entry's trace is no longer derived from pipeline_run_id and is set only under a current span, with the new spanId and traceSampled beside it, and the pipeline_run_id label still selects a run's lines. If you export Pipelex's spans to your own backend, join a line inside a run to them on pipelex.trace_id and pipelex.span_id. For a sink plugin, span_context_for_logs() and otel_context_for_logs() are replaced by current_span_context_for_logs(), pipelex_span_context_for_logs() and pipelex_trace_fields_for_logs() in pipelex.system.telemetry.current_span.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The gcp log sink says when its flush runs out of time, and why: a teardown whose flush reaches its five-second deadline with records still held now prints on stderr that they are lost unless the transport sends them while it closes, followed by what a fresh refresh of the credentials answers, where only the client library's "Failed to send N pending logs." used to appear. A handler that has closed no longer flushes again when the process exits, which cost a second five-second wait.
  • A GcpLogSink installed a second time raises instead of sending nothing: installing the same sink object again after a reset built a handler on the transport the first teardown had closed, which queued every record and sent none; make_handler now raises RuntimeError, as the otlp sink does, and the registered gcp factory still builds a new sink at every boot.
  • A kernel step's log lines name its run and its step: run_llm_text, run_llm_object, generate_object_content, run_extract, run_search and run_img_gen now bind the job_metadata they are handed for the whole call, so a program driving the kernel directly gets log records carrying request_id, pipeline_run_id and pipe_run_id, as an interpreted run's do. An interpreted run's lines are unchanged.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • pipelex-agent --runner api run reports the runner's refusal, not its status line: when the API runner answers run pipe, run bundle or run method with a non-2xx status, the error envelope, in markdown and in JSON, now carries what its problem document says: the runner's error class as error_type (ValidateBundleError, ModelNotFoundError, StuffFactoryError), a message quoting its reason, which names the failing pipe and its path on a failed run, its next step as hint, its error_domain, error_category and retryable, its validation_errors rendered as validate renders them, pipe_code and pipe_stack when it carries them, its code as error_code, the Retry-After delay as retry_after_seconds, and http_status and request_id, where the envelope used to read only HTTPStatusError and Client error '422 Unprocessable Entity'. An answer that advises no next step gets one from its status: a 401 or 403 points at the API key, a 404 at MTHDS_BASE_URL, a 429 says to wait and retry and is retryable, a 503 warns that a retry can repeat a paid run, any other 4xx says to change the request, and any other status says to report the request_id. It requires mthds 0.17.0, whose client raises the typed ApiResponseError.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • The API runner's credentials hint names the variables it reads: a ClientAuthenticationError now says to set MTHDS_API_KEY and MTHDS_BASE_URL or to run mthds config set, where it pointed at pipelex-agent doctor and PIPELEX_API_KEY, which the API runner does not read.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• An unknown model is a located unknown_model validation item: a pipe whose model field names a handle, alias, preset or waterfall the model deck does not define now validates to an invalid verdict with one pipe_validation item of the new closed error_type unknown_model, carrying the pipe_code, domain_code, source, field_name, the field_path of the reference (pipe.<code>.model, or pipe.<code>.model_to_structure), and the new optional item fields model_reference (the reference as written), model_type and suggestions (the deck's close matches of the same kind, also kept in the message). Every pipe type that names a model gives the same item, where PipeExtract and PipeSearch used to give an unknown_validation_error whose message was a Python repr, and with exactly one suggestion the item carries an unsafe rename-model fix, which pipelex fix bundle never applies on its own because a fuzzy match can name a different model. The MTHDS Test Corpus gains the invalid_unknown_model entry covering the new error.unknown_model tag.
  • An unsafe suggested fix says so wherever it is printed: the per-error line of pipelex validate, of pipelex fix's remaining errors and of every pipelex-agent Markdown rendering, the rendered_markdown shared with /validate included, reads 💡 Suggested fix (unsafe, confirm before applying): for a fix whose safety is unsafe, while a safe fix keeps the plain 💡 Suggested fix: line, so a person or an agent can tell which fixes to check before making them by hand.
  • A run graph marks a list-valued stuff as a list: every io item of a GraphSpec produced by a dry or live run now carries multiplicity, true when the stuff is a list and null otherwise, so a renderer shows an input declared Document[], a Record[] output, a batch's aggregate, a step run with nb_output or a lifted plural output as a list, on both the in-process graph and the one assembled from trace events. A trace event carrying the field cannot be read by an earlier pipelex, so the process that assembles a graph must run a pipelex at least as new as the workers that wrote its events. The Mermaid renderer labels such a stuff Record[], and its labels now keep square brackets instead of turning them into parentheses.
  • Validation items carry the positions and declared concepts the parser knew: a TOML syntax error's item carries the 1-based line and column the parser stopped at, as new optional item fields, and an unresolved_concept item carries declared_concepts, the bare codes of the concepts the validated bundle declares in its domain, so an editor can anchor the diagnostic and an author sees what the reference could have named.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Every refusal raised while loading a bundle is a validation verdict (Breaking): validation turns any refusal of the caller's input that has no arm of its own into an invalid verdict with one item, keeping the refusal's message only when it is caller-facing and otherwise its title, while a configuration or runtime fault still propagates as no verdict. A refusal raised while a pipe is built leaves the library load as the new PipeLoadRefusalError, naming the pipe, its domain and its file with the original as its cause, and gives a pipe_validation item located there; any other gives a blueprint_validation item. pipelex validate bundle no longer prints a traceback for an unknown model, pipelex-agent validate bundle answers it with is_valid: false and exit 1 instead of the no-verdict envelope and exit 2, and the in-process validator behind /validate returns it as an invalid verdict instead of raising.
  • PipeOperatorModelChoiceError is the located unknown-model refusal (Breaking): it is now raised whenever a pipe naming an unknown model is built, with a message naming the pipe and the field; it is input-domained and caller-facing, carries domain_code, field_name, suggestions and source, and its model_choice is the reference as written. The agent CLI's hint for it points at check-model rather than doctor.
  • A PipeParallel branch whose multiplicity differs from its field's is refused with the fix to make: when the combine of the branch results refuses a list branch fed into a single field, or a single branch fed into a list field, the refusal now names the parallel, the branch, the result and the field, and says to declare the field with the branch's multiplicity or to make the branch produce the field's, instead of reporting a Python validation error about ListContent. The dry run of pipelex validate and pipelex-agent validate carry it in their dry_run item, and a run reports it as a StuffFactoryError in the input domain, so a hosted runner under STRICT disclosure answers a 422 whose message and change_input next step name the change, where it answered An internal error occurred..
  • The invalid-bundle verdict's next step points at its items: ValidateBundleError's user action, the 💡 Tip: of pipelex validate and the hint of pipelex-agent's JSON, now reads "Edit the bundle as each validation error says: apply its suggested fix where it has one, after confirming an unsafe one" instead of "Check the validation_errors array for specific issues".
  • A run refuses an invalid bundle with the validation verdict (Breaking): a run loads its bundle before any pipe runs, and a bundle that load refuses now raises ValidateBundleError with the same located validation_errors validating it gives, which a hosted run route answers as an HTTP 422 that keeps them under STRICT disclosure, instead of the raw class of whichever check refused it (a 500 for a misspelled concept or a wiring mismatch, a 422 without items for a TOML fault, a runtime PipeExecutionError for a check inside a pipe's validator, a PipeOperatorModelChoiceError for an unknown model); an unknown entry pipe still raises its PipeNotFoundError. pipelex run prints the grouped panel pipelex validate prints, pipelex-agent run and any other agent error envelope caused by such a verdict carry its validation_errors, and the runner's new library_dirs_are_callers option, which both CLIs set, gives a refusal in the caller's own library directories the same verdict while a host's directories still load untranslated.
  • A pipe factory's refusal is a located validation item: PipeLLMFactoryError, PipeComposeFactoryError, PipeExtractFactoryError, PipeConditionFactoryError and PipeParallelFactoryError are now input-domained and caller-facing, so a PipeExtract whose input is neither an image nor a document validates to a pipe_validation item on that pipe and its file, whose message names the input and says to redeclare it, where it used to escape every validator as no verdict; a PipeLLM whose prompt or inherited system prompt does not parse is refused with the line of that prompt it fails at and no longer quotes any of the prompt, which may be a host's; the builder's validate_ops.validate_pipe and validate_all also answer a refusal raised while they load libraries or dry-run a pipe with the ValidateBundleError verdict instead of the raw error. pipelex-agent validate pipe --all keeps the file on an item raised while its libraries load.
  • pipelex validate pipe and pipelex validate --all render a refusal as an invalid bundle: a pipe whose dry run fails, and a refusal of the libraries while they load, now print the grouped invalid-bundle output and exit 1 instead of a traceback; pipelex-agent validate pipe and --all answer a load-time refusal with the invalid-verdict envelope.
  • A failing dry run is one located item per failing pipe (Breaking): validation reports a dry-run failure as one dry_run item per failing pipe, with the error type DryRunError and the pipe_code, domain_code and source of the innermost pipe that failed and is not allowed to fail (when submitted content is validated beside a host's library directories, the source only for that content's own pipes, never a file of the host's own library directories), where it used to report one item holding a Python repr of the sweep's records, once more for every controller the failure passed through. The item keeps the failure's own message only when that message is caller-facing and otherwise names the failure's title, so a configuration or storage failure met during a dry run no longer reaches a hosted caller through the verdict; pipelex validate lists the items under Dry Run Errors:, pipelex-agent validate pipe and validate pipe --all answer a failing dry run with the invalid-verdict envelope and its items instead of a DryRunError envelope with none, and the agent inputs commands drop their dry_run_error key. In Python, ValidateBundleError takes dry_run_failures in place of dry_run_error_message, and DryRunError carries failures.
  • A run failure reports its root fault, located at the failing pipe (Breaking): the report of a PipelineExecutionError, and of the PipeRouterError under it, now carries the error_type, title, type_uri, caller-facing flag and own message of the root fault, the innermost Pipelex error on the cause chain, with the message prefixed by the failing pipe and its path (Pipe 'summarize' failed (two_steps → summarize): …), and the exception's pipe_code and pipe_stack name that pipe instead of the entry pipe. A bridge's sentence no longer reaches the report, a report recovered from a remote worker is taken as it is, so a run reports the same failure in process, through the in-process orchestrator or on a worker, and the fallback action names the failing pipe instead of saying Check pipe_stack to identify which pipe failed.
